closest.title: Bottlenecked Transformers: Periodic KV Cache Consolidation for Generalised Reasoning
closest.evidence: this can be seen as analogous to performing in-place rewrites of new KV segments, and rewrites of recalled past segments... introduces the Bottlenecked Transformer, which augments a backbone LLM with a Cache Processor, an auxiliary Transformer that performs periodic, non-causal, in-place KV rewrites at new
closest.why: this is exactly a periodic, non-causal in-place rewrite of a bounded window of KV entries by an auxiliary module trained with the base model, matching the proposal's component (KV cache), mechanism (non-causal rewrite of a trailing window, equivalent per the task's own equivalence rule to denoising rewrite), and purpose (correcting/refining earlier KV using later context).

closest.title: Deferred Commitment Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: DCD maintains a certainty-aware sliding window over masked tokens, resolving low-uncertainty tokens early while deferring high-uncertainty tokens until sufficient contextual evidence becomes available
closest.why: shares the goal of using later context to refine earlier uncertain representations within a window, though at the token/decoding level rather than explicitly the KV cache.

closest.title: Attention Is All You Need for KV Cache in Diffusion LLMs
closest.evidence: Elastic-Cache performs adaptive, layer-aware cache updates for diffusion LLMs, reducing redundant computation and accelerating decoding
closest.why: also periodically updates/refreshes cached KV states using bidirectional denoising context, though framed for efficiency rather than correction of write-time errors.

survives: Only a genuinely different twist (e.g., a formal masked-diffusion training objective for the denoiser distinct from Bottlenecked Transformer's in-place rewrite, or proof the mechanisms differ mathematically rather than just terminologically) could survive, but per the stated equivalence rule (non-causal in-place rewrite = denoising rewrite) this proposal is already covered.

closest.title: Data Fusion and Contrastive Alignment for Unconstrained IR Molecular Structure Elucidation
closest.evidence: we implement a novel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoder module that utilizes non-additive aggregation via linear-order statistics and the Choquet integral
closest.why: This places a Choquet integral directly inside an MoE module, but as an aggregation operator over already-selected/all expert outputs rather than as the top-k subset-selection criterion for redundancy-aware routing.

closest.title: GatePro: Parameter-Free Expert Selection Optimization for Mixture-of-Experts Models
closest.evidence: GatePro identifies the most similar expert pairs and introduces localized competition mechanisms, preventing redundant expert co-activation while maintaining natural expert specialization.
closest.why: Same capability (pairwise-redundancy-aware expert selection at the router) but via a parameter-free competition heuristic rather than a learned 2-additive Choquet capacity/fuzzy measure with a discrete Choquet integral optimization.

closest.title: SHAPE: Coalition-Aware Expert Pruning for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
closest.evidence: SHAPE formulates routing traces on a small calibration set as an empirical cooperative game and assigns interaction-aware expert values via a Shapley-style attribution over observed top-$k$ coalitions
closest.why: Also treats expert selection as a coalitional/interaction-aware combinatorial optimization (game-theoretic capacity), close in spirit to Choquet capacities, but applied to post-hoc pruning rather than per-token joint-utility-maximizing top-k routing trained end-to-end.

survives: A genuinely novel contribution would be the specific formalism of a learned 2-additive Choquet capacity used at inference time per-token to select the joint-utility-maximizing k-subset (not aggregation, not post-hoc pruning, not a heuristic diversity penalty), trained jointly with the router from scratch and shown to beat both redundancy-heuristics (GatePro) and independent top-k scoring at matched FLOPs.

closest.title: A Hippocampus for Linear Attention: An Exact Memory for What the Recurrent State Forgets
closest.evidence: HOLA keeps the usual delta-rule state as a compressive memory and adds a bounded exact KV cache, forming a semiparametric test-time memory: the state models linearly compressible structure, while the cache stores associations that should not be forced through that state.
closest.why: Same dual-memory structure (delta-rule state + separate exact KV cache read jointly) but the delta-rule slot is the primary compressive memory and the KV cache is the exact overflow store, inverting the proposal's framing of KV-as-primary/delta-slots-as-auxiliary overwrite mechanism.

closest.title: Tensor Cache: Eviction-conditioned Associative Memory for Transformers
closest.evidence: a fixed-size outer-product fast-weight memory as a second-level cache (L2) fed by KV pairs evicted from the window... A learned scalar gate fuses the L1 and L2 outputs, and per-head decay and write-rate parameters are trained end-to-end.
closest.why: Also concatenates a positional KV window with a small delta/outer-product associative memory read jointly via attention, matching the placement and mechanism closely, though fed by evictions rather than parallel to the full cache.

closest.title: Fan Duality Model Achieves O(1) Decode Memory with Superior Associative Recall
closest.evidence: a particle component (local-global cache) that retrieves specific tokens via learned associative addressing with W+K=272 slots independent of sequence length N
closest.why: Also pairs a fixed small associative-addressed slot memory alongside a positional/local cache read jointly by attention, similar architecture-level combination.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—training the delta-memory strictly as a parallel, non-evicted auxiliary slot bank at matched param/FLOP budget purely to let later tokens overwrite stale content at matched-key positions while the full append-only KV remains untouched (rather than being fed by evictions, replacing state, or serving as the primary compressive path)—is a narrower combination not explicitly tested in HOLA, Tensor Cache, or FDM, but it is very close to all three and would likely read as a direct follow-up/ablation of this cluster.

closest.title: KVSmooth: Mitigating Hallucination in Multi-modal Large Language Models through Key-Value Smoothing
closest.evidence: KVSmooth applies an exponential moving average (EMA) to both keys and values in the KV-Cache, while dynamically quantifying the sink degree of each token... to adaptively adjust the smoothing strength
closest.why: This applies EMA directly to cached key/value vectors in-place to produce a denoised, temporally-smoothed cache entry, matching the proposal's mechanism and object exactly.

closest.title: ReST-KV: Robust KV Cache Eviction with Layer-wise Output Reconstruction and Spatial-Temporal Smoothing
closest.evidence: we design exponential moving average smoothing to handle temporal variations and an adaptive window-based mechanism to capture spatial patterns
closest.why: Also uses EMA smoothing on KV cache values to reduce noise/variance, though framed within an eviction pipeline rather than as a standalone prefill-time denoising step.

closest.title: What Matters for Aggressive Decoding-Time KV Eviction? Temporal Aggregation and Ranking Preservation
closest.evidence: we find that exponential-moving-average (EMA) aggregation makes approximately order-preserving scorer modifications largely indistinguishable... we introduce InertiaKV, an EMA-based decoding-time eviction method
closest.why: Uses EMA aggregation on KV-related scores/values across time, a closely related but score-focused rather than value-vector-focused application.

survives: The only defensible twist is doing the EMA over multiple perturbed re-encodes of the same position during prefill (variance reduction via repeated forward passes) rather than EMA over sequential time-steps of a single trajectory, but this is a minor procedural variant of an already-published in-place EMA smoothing of cached K/V vectors.

closest.title: GradMem: Learning to Write Context into Memory with Test-Time Gradient Descent
closest.evidence: GradMem performs a few steps of gradient descent on a small set of prefix memory tokens while keeping model weights frozen... a loss-driven write operation with iterative error correction, unlike forward-only methods.
closest.why: Same mechanism (test-time gradient descent to iteratively refine cached representations against a learned objective) but applied to compressive prefix memory tokens for context removal/reconstruction, not to per-layer KV cache entries refined against an energy function for in-place consistency correction.

closest.title: dKV-Cache: The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: we propose a delayed and conditioned caching strategy for key and value states... different tokens have distinct representation dynamics throughout the diffusion process
closest.why: Addresses the same component (KV cache) and motivation (representations become stale/inconsistent as context grows) but via delayed caching schedules tied to diffusion denoising, not gradient descent on an energy function.

closest.title: Prefill-Time Intervention for Mitigating Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
closest.evidence: PTI intervenes only once during the prefill stage, enhancing the initial Key-Value (KV) cache before error accumulation occurs... correcting hallucination-prone representations at their source
closest.why: Same object (KV cache entries) undergoing corrective rewriting for consistency, but a single steering-vector intervention rather than iterative gradient descent on a learned energy function conditioned on growing context.

closest.title: LoCoCo: Dropping In Convolutions for Long Context Compression
closest.evidence: LoCoCo leverages a data-driven adaptive fusion technique, blending previous KV pairs with incoming tokens to minimize the loss of contextual information...This token integration is achieved through injecting one-dimensional convolutional kernels that dynamically calculate mixing weights for each KV cache slot.
closest.why: Same object (cache slot), same operation (in-place learned convex-like fusion of old KV with new incoming info) but via convolution weights rather than an explicit Kalman gain/uncertainty state.

closest.title: Dynamic Memory Compression: Retrofitting LLMs for Accelerated Inference
closest.evidence: a method for online key-value cache compression at inference time...the model learns to apply different compression ratios in different heads and layers
closest.why: Learned, trained-jointly adaptive merging of KV entries at inference, a neighboring mechanism to uncertainty-weighted fusion but framed as compression ratio rather than explicit Kalman fusion.

closest.title: ZigZagkv: Dynamic KV Cache Compression for Long-context Modeling based on Layer Uncertainty
closest.evidence: this paper proposes a simple yet effective KV cache compression method that leverages layer uncertainty to allocate budget size for each layer
closest.why: Uses an uncertainty-like signal tied to KV cache entries, but for eviction/budget allocation rather than in-place uncertainty-weighted fusion of old and new estimates.

survives: The explicit Kalman-filter formalism—maintaining a learned scalar/low-rank uncertainty per slot and updating both the KV estimate and its uncertainty via a Kalman-gain-weighted fusion with a periodic 'measurement' derived from later context—is a more principled and reversible (non-discarding, uncertainty-tracked) mechanism than LoCoCo's fixed convolutional mixing or DMC's compression-ratio learning, so a version demonstrating this specific recursive uncertainty-tracked fusion (not mere blending or ratio selection) would still be a genuine, if narrow, contribution.

closest.title: Graph-Guided Adaptive Channel Elimination for KV Cache Compression

survives: The proposal's twist of learned MLP message-passing that rewrites the actual K/V content (not just importance/eviction scores) along attention-derived edges is functionally very close to Bottlenecked Transformers' non-causal in-place KV rewrite via an auxiliary network; a genuinely new contribution would need to show the sparse-graph edge structure (vs. dense/windowed Transformer processor) yields a distinct capability such as long-range coreference propagation at strictly O(edges) cost with provable savings over the dense Cache Processor.

closest.title: Learning to Forget: Sleep-Inspired Memory Consolidation for Resolving Proactive Interference in Large Language Models
closest.evidence: SleepGate, a biologically inspired framework that augments transformer-based LLMs with a learned sleep cycle over the key-value (KV) cache. SleepGate introduces three mechanisms: ... a lightweight forgetting gate trained to selectively evict or compress stale cache entries; and (3) a consolidation module that merges surviving entries into compact summaries. These components activate periodically during inference in sleep micro-cycles
closest.why: This is exactly a sleep-inspired consolidation module that periodically compresses/merges KV cache entries into compact permanent summaries during offline-like sleep cycles, matching component, mechanism, and purpose.

closest.title: Bottlenecked Transformers: Periodic KV Cache Consolidation for Generalised Reasoning
closest.evidence: memory consolidation/reconsolidation ... can be seen as analogous to performing in-place rewrites of new KV segments, and rewrites of recalled past segments ... a Cache Processor, an auxiliary Transformer that performs periodic, non-causal, in-place KV rewrites
closest.why: Same mechanism (periodic non-causal consolidation module rewriting/compressing KV cache) at the same component, framed explicitly as sleep-consolidation-inspired.

closest.title: FadeMem: Distance-Aware Memory Consolidation for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
closest.evidence: a distance-aware KV memory consolidation mechanism that organizes historical KV blocks into a temporal hierarchy under a fixed cache budget ... older adjacent entries are progressively merged
closest.why: Also periodically distills/merges historical KV cache into compact fixed-budget summaries to retain long-range gist, same purpose in a different domain.

survives: Only a genuinely distinct twist (e.g., proving a different theoretical guarantee, a training-free variant, or targeting a capability neither interference-resolution nor generalized reasoning addresses) would separate this from SleepGate and Bottlenecked Transformers, which already implement periodic sleep-inspired consolidation modules that compress/merge KV cache entries into permanent summaries.

closest.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries: Beyond the Per-Vector Shannon Limit
closest.evidence: The second layer, predictive delta coding, stores only the residual of each new KV vector from the model's own prediction of it, achieving a per-token entropy bound of H(KV_{i+1} | KV_{<=i}) <= H(token_{i+1} | token_{<=i})
closest.why: This stores a prediction-error residual against the model's own predicted KV at write time, the same core mechanism (predictive residual coding of KV), though motivated purely for compression rather than for enabling top-down reinterpretation at read time.

closest.title: Efficient Serving for Dynamic Agent Workflows with Prediction-based KV-Cache Management
closest.evidence: PBKV predicts the agent invocations in several future steps by fusing the guidance from historical workflows and context of the target workflow. Based on the predictions, PBKV estimates the reuse potential of cache entries
closest.why: Uses prediction to manage KV cache entries, but predicts reuse/eviction utility rather than reinterpreting stored content via a top-down predictor recomputed at read time.

closest.title: The Residual Stream Is All You Need: On the Redundancy of the KV Cache in Transformer Inference
closest.evidence: keys and values at every layer are deterministic projections of the residual stream, and recomputing them from a single residual vector per token incurs exactly zero reconstruction error
closest.why: Shows KV can be recomputed fresh from stored state at read time rather than stored raw, conceptually adjacent to recomputing effective K/V at read time, but not framed as prediction-error residual coding or context-dependent reinterpretation.

survives: The proposal's distinctive twist—training a per-layer top-down predictor conditioned on the current (later) decoding state so that the SAME stored residual yields a DIFFERENT effective K/V as later context grows, i.e. genuine reinterpretation without mutation—is not demonstrated in the nearest paper (2604.15356), which uses predictive residual coding purely for compression with a fixed (not read-time-recomputed-per-later-context) prediction; if the mechanism is shown to implement content-dependent revision under append-only storage rather than just entropy reduction, it would remain new.

closest.title: Recurrent Preference Memory for Efficient Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation

survives: Only a genuinely different twist—such as a formal variational IB bound with an epsilon-constrained frozen predictor loss guarantee, or joint training with the base model rather than periodic in-place rewrites—would be new, but this is a training-recipe/framing difference, not a new capability.

closest.title: Tensor Cache: Eviction-conditioned Associative Memory for Transformers
closest.evidence: a fixed-size outer-product fast-weight memory as a second-level cache (L2) fed by KV pairs evicted from the window... A learned scalar gate fuses the L1 and L2 outputs, and per-head decay and write-rate parameters are trained end-to-end
closest.why: Places the exact same outer-product Hebbian fast-weight overlay (A <- lambda*A + eta*(k⊗v), read via a gated additive correction) at the same component (KV cache), differing mainly in that it is fed by evicted tokens for compression/recall rather than for live association revision.

closest.title: Lifelong In-Context Learning with Transformers Requires Parametric Forms of Attention
closest.evidence: They replace the ever-growing key-value cache with an online-trainable neural network, maintaining a constant memory footprint... fast weight programmers

closest.title: Can Video World Models Track Unobserved World States?
closest.evidence: TTT with a nonlinear fast weight succeeds by updating the feature map through which it reads its own state
closest.why: Uses an in-place fast-weight state update at the cache/state component for revising hidden associations across chunks, close in spirit to the claimed 'oh, X actually refers to Y' revision but framed for state-tracking extrapolation rather than short-lived decaying correction terms.

survives: The specific framing of a bounded-norm, fast-decaying (lambda<1) additive correction term explicitly designed to let recent associations be transiently revised and then auto-forgotten without ever touching stored K/V—rather than as a compression/capacity mechanism (Tensor Cache) or a persistent state-tracking substrate (TTT/parametric attention)—is a narrower purpose not directly targeted by the closest papers, but it is a thin twist given how mechanically identical the update/read rule is.

closest.title: PQCache: Product Quantization-based KVCache for Long Context LLM Inference
closest.evidence: we apply PQ to tokens' keys for each LLM layer and head... we use PQ codes and centroids to approximately identify important preceding tokens, then fetch the corresponding key-value pairs for self-attention computation
closest.why: Already applies PQ to the KV cache with importance-based (attention-proxy) selection of which entries get fetched/full precision versus PQ-coded, matching component, mechanism, and purpose.

closest.title: RDKV: Rate-Distortion Bit Allocation for Joint Eviction and Quantization of the KV Cache
closest.evidence: RDKV derives the weight of each token or channel from the distortion that compression induces on the attention computation... assigns each token or channel a bit-width ranging from full precision down to zero bits guided by reverse water-filling
closest.why: Directly allocates per-token storage precision (including full precision) based on attention-derived importance, the same capability of non-uniform, attention-proportional bit allocation in the KV cache.

closest.title: MILLION: Mastering Long-Context LLM Inference Via Outlier-Immunized KV Product Quantization
closest.evidence: we propose MILLION, a novel quantization framework achieving low-bitwidth KV cache through product quantization... a non-uniform quantization algorithm based on product quantization
closest.why: Establishes PQ as the core non-uniform KV-cache compression mechanism, the same component/mechanism pairing, differing mainly in the importance signal used for non-uniformity.

survives: Only a genuinely novel twist—e.g. online k-means codebook updates jointly trained with an EMA-attention-mass threshold policy that dynamically re-tiers entries between full precision and PQ during training itself (not just post-hoc/inference-time)—might be new, but this is a training-recipe nuance rather than a new capability beyond PQCache/RDKV's attention-weighted precision allocation.

closest.title: CSR: Achieving 1 Bit Key-Value Cache via Sparse Representation

closest.title: Sparse Attention across Multiple-context KV Cache

survives: The interpretability side-channel (inspecting which atoms compose an entry) and joint from-scratch training at matched FLOPs are not emphasized in Lexico/CSR (which are largely post-hoc/training-light on pretrained models), so a genuinely new angle would be exploiting atom co-activation patterns as an interpretability tool rather than just compression, but the core mechanism-at-component-for-compression claim is already taken.

closest.title: FreqKV: Key-Value Compression in Frequency Domain for Context Window Extension
closest.evidence: Motivated by the observation in the frequency domain that the context information is concentrated in the low-frequency components, we propose FreqKV, a parameter-free and architecture-agnostic approach. It iteratively compresses the increasing KV cache in the frequency domain
closest.why: This applies exactly the proposed mechanism (frequency transform per feature over time, keep low-frequency components, discard rest) at the KV cache for the same purpose of principled compression, training-free.

closest.title: Beyond Homogeneous Attention: Memory-Efficient LLMs via Fourier-Approximated KV Cache
closest.evidence: By projecting the long-context-insensitive dimensions onto orthogonal Fourier bases, FourierAttention approximates their temporal evolution with fixed-length spectral coefficients.
closest.why: Same spectral-transform-over-time-axis compression of KV cache retaining low-frequency coefficients, matching the proposal's exact mechanism and placement.

closest.title: SPECTRA: Pushing the KV Cache Beyond the 2-Bit Cliff via Spectral Transform Coding
closest.evidence: a small fraction of channels carries almost all the information, and spending the budget on those few is far more accurate than spreading it evenly
closest.why: Also applies spectral/transform coding directly to cache entries to concentrate energy and compress, same component and similar purpose though combined with quantization.

survives: Nothing substantive remains new: per-block DCT over rolling time windows with top-f coefficient retention and inverse-DCT reconstruction at read time is essentially what FreqKV and FourierAttention already implement and evaluate.

closest.title: Beyond Token Eviction: Mixed-Dimension Budget Allocation for Efficient KV Cache Compression
closest.evidence: allocates dimensions to tokens at a more granular level, and MixedDimKV-H, which further integrates head-level importance information
closest.why: allocates per-token resolution/budget from importance signals but uses a profiled/head-level scheme rather than a continuous per-entry EMA-driven homeostatic bit-width controller.

closest.title: BaKlaVa -- Budgeted Allocation of KV cache for Long-context Inference
closest.evidence: Using a one-time profiling approach, BaKlaVa assigns optimal memory budgets to each KV-cache
closest.why: allocates differential memory/precision budget based on importance, but via one-time profiling rather than an always-on running EMA homeostatic rule with a fixed-set quantization ladder maintaining constant population-mean attention-per-bit.

closest.title: KVSmooth: Mitigating Hallucination in Multi-modal Large Language Models through Key-Value Smoothing
closest.evidence: applies an exponential moving average (EMA) to both keys and values in the KV-Cache, while dynamically quantifying the sink degree of each token through the entropy of its attention distribution to adaptively adjust the smoothing strength
closest.why: uses EMA over attention-derived statistics to adaptively modulate KV-cache entries, closest in mechanism (EMA-driven per-entry adaptation) but applied to smoothing hidden states for hallucination mitigation, not to bit-width/quantization-level allocation for memory compression.

survives: The specific homeostatic control law that continuously re-quantizes each entry's bit-width (from a fixed set) to hold population-mean attention-mass-per-bit constant, without any profiling pass, budget target, or learned selector, is not shown in these papers; if that exact self-regulating EMA-to-quantization-level mapping is the twist, it could still be novel.

closest.evidence: we integrate adaptive caching that dynamically allocates cache space between recently and frequently occurring KV blocks

closest.title: Fractional Decay KV-Cache: Ownership-Aware Memory Management for Improved Inference Relevancy in Dialog Systems
closest.evidence: maintains a dual-channel scoring mechanism for each cached KV pair: a cumulative attention channel ... and a recency-weighted relevance channel ... enables FD-KVC to both preserve historically important tokens and rapidly adapt when dialog topics shift

closest.title: Lethe: Layer- and Time-Adaptive KV Cache Pruning for Reasoning-Intensive LLM Serving

closest.why: also adapts recency-based eviction dynamically based on changing attention patterns at the KV cache.

survives: The specific ARC ghost-list bookkeeping (tracking recency-evicted vs frequency-evicted shadow entries to adapt the split point) is a distinct implementation detail, but the capability and placement it targets are already claimed by existing recency/frequency adaptive KV caching work.

closest.evidence: We do this through the lens of Information Bottleneck (IB) theory, which posits that model generalisation emerges from an optimal balance between input information compression and retention of predictive information in latent representations... a Cache Processor, an auxiliary Transformer that performs periodic, non-causal, in-place KV rewrites

closest.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction via a Unified Information-Theoretic Objective

closest.why: Places an information-theoretic (IB-style) objective directly on KV cache retention to control the compression/prediction tradeoff, though via eviction rather than a learned encoder.

closest.title: Recurrent Preference Memory for Efficient Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
closest.evidence: Analysis reveals that the Preference Memory functions as a denoising Information Bottleneck, effectively filtering interaction noise to capture robust long-term interests.
closest.why: Uses a trained bottleneck to compress cache-like memory into minimal sufficient statistics for downstream prediction, same mechanism/purpose in a different domain.

survives: Only a genuinely per-entry, target-driven variable-rate allocation measured explicitly in nats via a VIB reparameterized-Gaussian encoder (rather than eviction/rewriting at fixed or heuristic budgets) could still be new, but 2505.16950 already frames KV rewriting explicitly as IB-driven compression-vs-prediction tradeoff at the same component for the same purpose.

closest.title: The risk of KV cache compression

closest.title: EvolKV: Evolutionary KV Cache Compression for LLM Inference

survives: A genuinely new twist would be the explicit online two-part MDL code-length computation (model bits for quantization level choice + residual bits under a fitted prior) reported and minimized per-entry as a measurable quantity, rather than a learned/heuristic/task-performance-driven importance score—none of the found papers compute or optimize this explicit code-length decomposition.

closest.title: ForesightKV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction for Reasoning Models by Learning Long-Term Contribution
closest.evidence: identifies the optimal eviction KV pairs at each step using future attention scores. These traces and the scores at each step are then distilled via supervised training

closest.title: Error Certificates for KV-Cache Eviction via Randomized Design
closest.evidence: We replace the deterministic tail with Poisson sampling at known inclusion probabilities, which makes the eviction error identifiable and turns a survey-sampling variance estimator over the retained set into a per-step error certificate
closest.why: Explicitly uses importance/inclusion-probability-based sampling theory at the KV-cache eviction component, the closest mechanism match to 'importance-sampling' framing, though for error certification rather than budget/precision allocation.

survives: A genuine self-normalized importance-sampling correction (explicit proposal q vs. target p reweighting, debiased rather than just predicted) mapped to a continuous bit-width/precision tier rather than binary evict/keep could still be new, but the core capability of estimating future attention mass to reallocate cache resources is already claimed by LookaheadKV and ForesightKV.

closest.evidence: a small per-layer Perceiver trained once against a frozen base model that produces compact keys and values in a single forward pass ... Because compaction is a forward pass, Still can be applied iteratively, entering a long-horizon regime unavailable to per-context methods

closest.title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
closest.evidence: RestoreKV is trained through parameter-efficient self-distillation from the frozen full-cache model, optimizing only 0.4% of the parameters ... generating a compact, context-conditioned restore cache
closest.why: Same mechanism (self-distillation into a compact synthetic KV complement for evicted/compressed info, base frozen) at the same component (kv-cache), aimed at recovering lost eviction information rather than explicit slow/fast dual-teacher consolidation.

closest.title: KVSculpt: KV Cache Compression as Distillation
closest.evidence: we optimize a smaller set of unconstrained KV pairs in continuous embedding space to preserve each layer's attention behavior
closest.why: Same idea of distilling/optimizing a smaller synthetic KV set to preserve attention behavior of evicted entries, though framed as per-context optimization rather than an online EMA-teacher slow-cache update.

survives: The specific two-tier fast/slow cache architecture with a continuously EMA-stabilized teacher and incremental every-k-token online gradient consolidation (rather than one-shot amortized synthesis or per-context optimization) is a narrower architectural variant that these papers do not explicitly instantiate, so a proposal centered on that exact online slow-teacher/fast-student consolidation loop could still be marginally new, though the core mechanism is already well covered.

closest.title: MomentKV: Closing the Directional Gap in KV Cache Eviction for Long-Context Inference
closest.evidence: MomentKV, which maintains compact, small-size moment statistics over the evicted token set, including a count, key mean, value mean, and value-key covariance ... During inference, they yield a closed-form first-order approximation of the evicted attention output
closest.why: This maintains a fixed-size running summary of evicted KV entries updated online and used during attention, the same core mechanism/purpose as the proposal, though via moment statistics rather than a plain EMA slot.

closest.title: Moment-KV: Momentum-Based Decode-Time KV Cache Compression for Long Generation
closest.evidence: models token importance as a continuously evolving state, where attention is aggregated with decay, capturing both long-term influence and recent relevance
closest.why: Uses momentum/decay-based running aggregation over evicted/decaying tokens to retain long-horizon influence at bounded cost, closely paralleling the EMA summary-slot idea, though applied to importance scoring rather than literal key/value folding.

closest.title: KVSmooth: Mitigating Hallucination in Multi-modal Large Language Models through Key-Value Smoothing
closest.evidence: KVSmooth applies an exponential moving average (EMA) to both keys and values in the KV-Cache
closest.why: Directly applies EMA smoothing to keys and values in the cache, the same mechanism at the same component, but for hallucination mitigation rather than preserving evicted-token influence.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—an explicit extra 'summary slot' per head that receives exactly the evicted entry via alpha*summary+(1-alpha)*evicted_kv and then participates in attention like a normal KV pair (rather than smoothing all live entries or using moment statistics for score correction)—is a narrower, more literal instantiation than what MomentKV or KVSmooth do, so a tightly scoped version could survive, but it is very close to MomentKV's mechanism and purpose.

closest.title: MemDecay: Region-Aware KV Cache Eviction for Efficient LLM Agent Inference
closest.evidence: MemDecay assigns tokens region-specific base priorities and decay rates, refreshes retention scores when tokens receive attention, and evicts the lowest-scoring pages under a fixed cache budget while allowing critical regions to be pinned.
closest.why: Uses differentiated retention/decay rules and periodic recalibration to protect long-lived but relevant tokens from a uniform recency rule, the same core capability the proposal targets, though partitioned by semantic region rather than by age-tier with promotion sweeps.

closest.title: QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding
closest.evidence: QEvict maintains high-confidence windows in full precision, stores intermediate windows in a quantized recoverable tier, and deletes only the lowest-confidence windows... when a quantized window becomes important again, it is dequantized and promoted to the full-precision.
closest.why: Implements a multi-tier structure with promotion between tiers based on renewed importance, structurally similar to a generational promotion/sweep scheme, though tiers are precision levels not age-since-last-hit with periodic sweep cadence differences.

closest.title: On the Limits of Learned Importance Scoring for KV Cache Compression
closest.evidence: position-based heuristics (keep first 4 + last N tokens) match or exceed learned approaches
closest.why: Relates to age/position-based retention baselines but does not implement tiered generational promotion/sweep cadence.

survives: The specific generational-GC mechanics (distinct sweep cadences per age tier, promotion between tiers based on attention-mass survival thresholds tuned to hit a cache-size budget, explicitly modeled on age-since-last-hit rather than semantic region or precision) is not directly instantiated by any single paper, so a system built precisely around age-partitioned differential sweep frequency with promotion thresholds could still be novel relative to MemDecay's region-based decay and QEvict's precision-tier promotion.

closest.title: Bottlenecked Transformers: Periodic KV Cache Consolidation for Generalised Reasoning
closest.evidence: we give a theoretical justification as to why memory (re)consolidation via KV cache rewrites is beneficial for improved reasoning... through the lens of Information Bottleneck (IB) theory... augments a backbone LLM with a Cache Processor, an auxiliary Transformer that performs periodic, non-causal, in-place KV rewrites
closest.why: This trains an auxiliary side network per the base model's KV cache under an explicit IB objective to compress/rewrite old KV entries in place, exactly matching the proposal's mechanism, object, and purpose.

closest.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction via a Unified Information-Theoretic Objective
closest.evidence: we derive a closed-form mutual information objective that characterizes the effective information capacity of a retained KV cache subset... a capacity-aware eviction method that directly targets information preservation
closest.why: Applies an information-bottleneck-style objective to KV eviction, though via closed-form scoring rather than a trained side network for compression.

closest.title: Training Transformers for KV Cache Compressibility
closest.evidence: we formalize the notion of KV compressibility and show that it is a property of the learned representations... propose KV-Compression Aware Training (KV-CAT)
closest.why: Related IB-flavored training-based approach to KV compressibility but modifies the base model rather than training a frozen-base side network for eviction replacement.

survives: Little remains new: the core twist (frozen base model, trained per-layer side network replacing about-to-be-evicted KV blocks with a fixed-size summary optimized via an explicit rate+task IB loss) is essentially what Bottlenecked Transformers already implements as IB-justified, non-causal, in-place KV cache rewrites via an auxiliary Cache Processor.

closest.title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
closest.evidence: This approach dynamically adjusts the KV cache size across different layers, allocating more cache in lower layers and less in higher ones... a novel and effective KV cache compression method
closest.why: Uses a 'pyramid' framing and layer-wise coarsening of cache allocation, but the pyramid is across layers not a recursive multi-scale merge of aging blocks along the sequence/time axis.

closest.title: Model Tells You Where to Merge: Adaptive KV Cache Merging for LLMs on Long-Context Tasks
closest.evidence: we propose a novel KV cache merging approach, called KVMerger, to achieve adaptive KV cache compression... Gaussian kernel weighted merging algorithm to selectively merge all states within each merging set
closest.why: Performs trained/weighted merging of KV pairs into coarser summaries, the same basic operation (merge to reduce resolution), but as a single-pass eviction-time merge rather than a recursive, log-depth, scale-boundary-triggered RG pyramid with a merge operator trained to match downstream attention outputs specifically at cache-write time off the causal path.

closest.title: LightVLM: Acceleraing Large Multimodal Models with Pyramid Token Merging and KV Cache Compression
closest.evidence: we propose pyramid token merging to reduce tokens of different LLM layers in a hierarchical manner by finally only keeping a few dominant tokens
closest.why: Also uses 'pyramid' hierarchical merging for cache/token reduction, but hierarchy is across layers/encoding stage, not a recursive multi-scale temporal coarsening of aging KV blocks with an RG-style trained merge operator.

survives: The specific RG framing—recursive, scale-boundary-triggered merging into a log-depth pyramid where the merge operator is explicitly trained to preserve exactly the attention outputs later queries would use (an information-theoretic renormalization criterion), applied purely at cache-write time as blocks age past scale boundaries—is a more principled and recursive construction than the single-level or layer-wise merging in KVMerger/PyramidKV/LightVLM, so a version that demonstrates genuine multi-scale (log-depth) recursive coarsening with RG-consistent training could still be new.

closest.title: KVCOMM: Online Cross-context KV-cache Communication for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
closest.evidence: KVCOMM estimates and adjusts KV-caches for shared content by referencing a pool of cached examples-termed anchors-that store observed cache deviations under varying prefixes. The anchor pool is maintained and updated online, allowing dynamic adaptation to distinct user requests and context structures.
closest.why: This is an online, cross-request pool of stored KV-related patterns retrieved by similarity to approximate KV for a new non-identical prefix, matching the proposal's core capability of non-exact-match cross-request KV reuse.

closest.title: Blurry Window Attention
closest.evidence: BLA stores a frequency window from which a blurry KV history is reconstructed via interpolation using Dirichlet kernels.
closest.why: Reconstructs an approximate KV representation from stored patterns rather than exact cache, analogous in spirit to approximate retrieval, though within a single sequence rather than cross-request bank.

closest.title: RcLLM: Accelerating Generative Recommendation via Beyond-Prefix KV Caching
closest.evidence: RcLLM decomposes prompts into reusable blocks... to reduce redundant quadratic attention computation, RcLLM combines an affinity-based global scheduler that improves data locality with a selective attention mechanism that corrects approximation errors.
closest.why: Also targets non-contiguous/non-exact-prefix KV reuse across a shared cache with an approximation-plus-correction scheme, similar to the proposal's retrieve-then-verify structure.

survives: The specific mechanism of energy-descent (modern-Hopfield) retrieval over a trained pooling/query projection against a bank of pooled prefix representations, with an explicit iterative attractor-dynamics formulation and partial-recompute verification, is more specific than KVCOMM's anchor-deviation estimation, so a paper demonstrating genuine Hopfield energy-descent convergence properties (not just nearest-anchor lookup) for KV approximation could still be new.

closest.title: ChunkAttention: Efficient Self-Attention with Prefix-Aware KV Cache and Two-Phase Partition
closest.evidence: a prefix-aware self-attention module that can detect matching prompt prefixes across multiple requests and share their key/value tensors in memory at runtime to improve the memory utilization of KV cache
closest.why: This is exactly a global cross-request KV cache keyed by prefix match, splicing shared KV into new requests to avoid recompute, the same component/mechanism/purpose as proposed.

closest.title: Shared Disk KV Cache Management for Efficient Multi-Instance Inference in RAG-Powered LLMs
closest.evidence: This system, together with an optimal system configuration... proactively generates and stores disk KV caches for query-related documents and shares them across multiple LLM instances to enhance inference performance.
closest.why: Persists and shares KV cache entries across requests/instances by content match to skip prefill, matching the proposal's amortization goal.

closest.title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
closest.evidence: Proximity reuses previously retrieved documents when similar queries appear... employs a locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) scheme that enables fast cache lookups while preserving retrieval accuracy.
closest.why: Uses approximate/embedding-similarity retrieval (not exact hash) to decide cache reuse, matching the proposal's kNN/verification-tolerance mechanism, albeit on retrieval results rather than KV directly, closely paralleling the design.

survives: Only a genuinely new twist—e.g. proving tight guarantees on approximate (non-exact) KV splicing with logit-verified tolerance across arbitrary non-prefix overlaps rather than exact/prefix-tree matching—would be new, but the core capability (shared, persistent, cross-request KV cache retrieval to skip prefill) is already established by ChunkAttention, RadixAttention-style systems, and disk/object KV sharing works.

closest.title: SemShareKV: Efficient KVCache Sharing for Semantically Similar Prompts via Token-Level LSH Matching
closest.evidence: SemShareKV applies fuzzy token matching using locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) on token embeddings ... By selectively reusing relevant key-value pairs from a reference prompt's cache, SemShareKV reduces redundant computation while maintaining output quality.
closest.why: This is exactly the proposed mechanism: LSH over prompt embeddings to detect approximate prefix similarity across requests and splice in cached KV blocks instead of recomputing prefill.

closest.title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
closest.evidence: Proximity reuses previously retrieved documents when similar queries appear ... Proximity employs a locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) scheme that enables fast cache lookups while preserving retrieval accuracy.

closest.title: RKSC: Reasoning-Aware KV Cache Sharing and Confident Early Exit for Multi-Step LLM Inference
closest.evidence: ASKS (Attention-Similarity KV Sharing) computes the prefix KV cache once and broadcasts it to all semantically similar branches via hidden-state cosine similarity, strictly generalising the token-exact prefix caching used by vLLM and SGLang.
closest.why: Also generalizes exact prefix caching to semantically-similar prefixes for KV reuse, same capability though via cosine similarity rather than LSH buckets.

survives: Nothing substantive survives; SemShareKV already implements LSH-bucketed fuzzy prefix matching on token embeddings to reuse KV cache blocks across semantically similar but lexically different prompts, which is the same mechanism at the same component for the same purpose.

closest.title: Sink vs. diagonal patterns as mechanisms for attention switch and oversmoothing prevention
closest.evidence: we further prove an equivalence between sinks and hard attention switch, in which the output of the attention is identically 0

closest.title: Threshold Differential Attention for Sink-Free, Ultra-Sparse, and Non-Dispersive Language Modeling
closest.evidence: TDA applies row-wise extreme-value thresholding with a length-dependent gate, retaining only exceedances... produces >99% exact zeros and eliminates attention sinks
closest.why: Achieves the same near-zero/abstention capability at attention-scores via thresholding/gating rather than a null key, overlapping mechanism-purpose but different gating principle (extreme-value threshold vs. MDL code-length).

survives: The specific MDL/code-length gating mechanism—an auxiliary head estimating bits-saved per key via ablation, used to penalize logits before softmax over {keys, null}—is not described in any of these papers, which use fixed sink tokens, geometric/threshold-based sparsity, or oversmoothing analysis rather than an information-theoretic per-key description-length cost; if the team can show the MDL auxiliary-loss induced abstention differs functionally (e.g. context-dependent code-length rather than static/thresholded sparsity) that twist could survive.

closest.title: Mixture of Attention Heads: Selecting Attention Heads Per Token
closest.evidence: Given an input, a router dynamically selects a subset of $k$ attention heads per token. This conditional computation schema allows MoA to achieve stronger performance than the standard multi-head attention layer.
closest.why: Same component (attention heads) and same capability class (per-token adaptive weighting/selection of heads instead of fixed combination), but the router is a learned function of the query, not an online Bayesian posterior over causal per-head predictive accuracy.

closest.title: Repulsive Attention: Rethinking Multi-head Attention as Bayesian Inference
closest.evidence: we provide a novel understanding of multi-head attention from a Bayesian perspective... we propose a non-parametric approach that explicitly improves the repulsiveness in multi-head attention
closest.why: Explicitly frames multi-head attention combination via Bayesian inference, overlapping the 'Bayesian model averaging over heads' framing, though its purpose is diversity/repulsion not per-token reliability-based reweighting.

closest.title: Improving Transformers with Dynamically Composable Multi-Head Attention
closest.evidence: DCMHA... transforms the attention score and weight matrices in an input-dependent way... dynamically composing attention heads.
closest.why: Same component and general idea of dynamically reweighting/composing head outputs per token, but composition is a learned input-dependent transform, not a posterior built from running per-head log-likelihood/causal accuracy tracking.

survives: The specific mechanism of maintaining an explicit running per-head log-likelihood (via auxiliary per-head next-token heads) and converting it into a causal Bayesian posterior strictly from past prediction accuracy—rather than a router or composition function conditioned on the current query—appears novel relative to MoA/DCMHA/Repulsive Attention, none of which track online predictive reliability as the weighting signal.

closest.title: ASAP: Amortized Doubly-Stochastic Attention via Sliced Dual Projection
closest.evidence: Doubly-stochastic attention has emerged as a transport-based alternative to row-softmax attention... the standard approach is Sinkhorn scaling, which trains more efficiently but still repeats matrix scaling in every inference forward pass... to reduce attention sinks and rank collapse
closest.why: This directly places Sinkhorn-based doubly-stochastic transport at the attention-score step as a softmax replacement to prevent collapse/sink phenomena, the same component and same purpose as the proposal.

closest.title: Spacetime Optimal-Transport Attention for Visuo-Haptic Imitation Learning
closest.evidence: SO-TA, a tri-modal fusion backbone that replaces softmax-normalized patch attention by an entropy-regularized Optimal Transport (OT) alignment... Explicit marginal constraints act as a structured inductive bias... encouraging conditioning-aware spatial selection
closest.why: Same mechanism (OT/Sinkhorn marginal-constrained transport plan replacing softmax) at the same component (attention-scores) for the same purpose of enforcing balanced/structured mass distribution, just in a different domain.

closest.title: OTSeg: Multi-prompt Sinkhorn Attention for Zero-Shot Semantic Segmentation
closest.evidence: inspired by the success of Sinkformers in unimodal settings, we introduce the extension of MPS, called Multi-Prompts Sinkhorn Attention (MPSA), which effectively replaces cross-attention mechanisms within Transformer framework
closest.why: Confirms the established lineage of Sinkhorn-normalized attention as a drop-in softmax replacement, generalizing the same core mechanism-at-component substitution the proposal claims as novel.

survives: Only the causal, sliding-window streaming variant with a running column-mass budget under strict autoregressive masking is not explicitly tested in these papers, but this is a scale/setting variant of an already-established mechanism (Sinkhorn/OT replacing softmax to enforce balanced marginals and prevent attention collapse), not a new capability.

closest.title: FourierQK: Spectral Preprocessing of Query-Key Projections Improves Transformer Attention
closest.evidence: FFT-based spectral preprocessing of learned query-key (Q/K) projections substantially improves transformer attention... Causal filters (Gaussian, Mexican Hat, Morlet) do not improve over standard attention at character-level tokenisation... this defines an architectural boundary between bilateral spectral attention (this paper) and genuinely causal spectral attention at word-scale tokenisation (companion paper MorletQK)
closest.why: Same component (attention scores) and same mechanism (spectral transform of Q/K before dot product) for the same purpose of improving long-range similarity computation, including explicit causal-vs-bilateral framing that the proposal also emphasizes.

closest.title: Beyond Self Attention: A Subquadratic Fourier Wavelet Transformer with Multi Modal Fusion
closest.evidence: MultiDomain Fourier Wavelet Attention(MDFWA) that integrates frequency and time localized transforms to capture both global and local dependencies efficiently... achieves sub quadratic time and memory cost while improving expressive power.
closest.why: Directly proposes replacing/augmenting attention with local+global frequency-domain token mixing to reduce quadratic cost while capturing long-range dependencies, matching the stated new capability.

closest.title: Discrete Cosine Transform Based Decorrelated Attention for Vision Transformers
closest.evidence: DCT-based attention compression technique that exploits the decorrelation properties of the frequency domain... truncate high-frequency components... reducing the dimensionality of the query, key, and value projections
closest.why: Uses a DCT basis applied to Q/K before the bilinear score, the same specific transform (causal chunked DCT) the proposal proposes, though for compression rather than causal long-range modeling.

survives: A genuinely causal, chunk-local multi-resolution DCT/Hadamard transform with cumulative low-frequency summaries carried across chunks (mimicking a causal multi-scale memory) is not shown in FourierQK's bilateral FFT or MDFWA's non-causal Fourier-wavelet mixing, so a working causal chunked-DCT variant with the multi-resolution carry-over could still be new if it demonstrably preserves strict causality while matching FLOPs.

closest.title: Collapse-Free Prototype Readout Layer for Transformer Encoders
closest.evidence: uses a small set of global prototype vectors and assigns tokens to them through soft probabilistic matching... an exact decomposition of the training loss into a reconstruction term and a diversity term... the same framework supports... a differentiable codebook extending VQ-VAE
closest.why: This places a codebook with reconstruction+diversity (MDL-like) loss directly on token representations for compression, the same mechanism/purpose as the proposal but applied as a readout/pooling layer rather than inline in the QK/softmax attention-score computation.

closest.title: PQCache: Product Quantization-based KVCache for Long Context LLM Inference
closest.evidence: we apply PQ to tokens' keys for each LLM layer and head... use PQ codes and centroids to approximately identify important preceding tokens
closest.why: Applies vector quantization to keys per layer/head to compress and approximately select attention targets, close to snapping keys to a codebook, but for KV-cache memory/retrieval efficiency rather than an MDL-regularized inspectable/prunable routing structure learned end-to-end with the LM loss.

closest.title: Mixture-of-Top-k Attention: Efficient Attention via Scalable Fast Weights
closest.evidence: employs a small set of landmark queries to gather top-$k$ attended key-value pairs as query-aware and deformable routed experts... compressing the $N$-width MLP into a narrower shared expert
closest.why: Reduces all-pairs attention to routing through a small set of learned landmarks/experts, similar hub-routing idea, but framed as fast-weight efficiency rather than an MDL-derived inspectable code with explicit usage-entropy loss for pruning.

survives: The specific combination of an in-line VQ bottleneck on keys with an explicit MDL loss (reconstruction error plus log2(C) times codebook usage-entropy) trained jointly with the LM loss specifically to measure and prune attention structure per layer/head is not exactly instantiated by any single paper, though close analogues (prototype codebooks with diversity+reconstruction loss, PQ on keys, top-k landmark routing) already cover the mechanism and placement; the surviving novelty would be the explicit description-length-based pruning diagnostic rather than the routing/quantization mechanism itself.

closest.title: Relevant and Irrelevant: A Renormalization Group Analysis of Transformer Attention
closest.evidence: we treat the Transformer's attention mechanism as a perturbation of the trained MLP residual-stack fixed point and ask whether it constitutes a relevant, marginal, or irrelevant operator
closest.why: Applies Wilsonian RG language to attention, but as a post-hoc analysis/diagnostic tool rather than a mechanism computing coarse-grained attention scores at multiple scales during the forward pass.

closest.title: PSA: Pyramid Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Understanding and Generation
closest.evidence: PSA introduces multi-level pooled KV representations, enabling finer mask granularity. Specifically, each query block dynamically allocates lower pooling levels to critical KV blocks and higher levels to less important ones
closest.why: Implements essentially the same mechanism (block-pooled multi-level KV pyramid attended jointly with learned/dynamic level selection) at the same component (attention-scores/KV), but for sparse efficiency rather than for an RG-consistency-loss-enforced guaranteed-stable multiscale hierarchy.

closest.title: AHMSA-Net: Adaptive Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention Network for Micro-Expression Recognition
closest.evidence: AHMSA-Net captures the subtle changes of micro-expressions from different granularities (fine and coarse) by dynamically adjusting the size of the optical flow feature map at each layer
closest.why: Same general idea of multi-scale pooled attention pyramid but domain-specific (vision) and without an RG fixed-point consistency loss.

survives: The specific enforced fixed-point/consistency loss (requiring level L+1 attention weights equal the block-sum of level-L weights, i.e. a literal RG coarse-graining constraint rather than just multi-level pooled KV or post-hoc RG analysis) is not present in PSA or the RG-analysis paper, so a proposal built specifically around that trained consistency constraint as the mechanism generating the hierarchy would still be novel.

closest.title: FAD-Net: Frequency-Domain Attention-Guided Diffusion Network for Coronary Artery Segmentation using Invasive Coronary Angiography

closest.title: Mitigating spectral bias for the multiscale operator learning
closest.evidence: HANO features a scale-adaptive interaction range and self-attentions over a hierarchy of levels, enabling nested feature computation with controllable linear cost and encoding/decoding of multiscale solution space

survives: A genuinely causal, streaming-safe wavelet transform applied specifically to the KV-cache of an autoregressive LM (enabling per-band inspection/ablation of cache entries during generation) is not demonstrated in these vision/PDE/segmentation-focused non-causal wavelet-attention works, so the causal KV-cache-native framing and interpretability angle could still be new if not merely an application-domain relabeling.

closest.title: Modeling Expert Interactions in Sparse Mixture of Experts via Graph Structures

survives: The specific 2-additive Choquet-integral formalism with a learned low-rank pairwise interaction capacity, combined subset-scoring via greedy/beam search and a pairwise co-selection balancing loss, is not shown in any of these papers, so a rigorous instantiation and ablation of this exact mechanism at the router would still be new relative to the graph-interaction and Choquet-as-aggregator precedents.

closest.title: SlimCaching: Edge Caching of Mixture-of-Experts for Distributed Inference

closest.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing

closest.why: Places a probabilistic/posterior-style distribution over expert subsets at the router, replacing hard top-k, similar to the proposal's posterior-mass weighting.

closest.title: Modeling Expert Interactions in Sparse Mixture of Experts via Graph Structures
closest.evidence: introduces a social graph to model interactions among experts... enhances the token routing process

closest.title: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing

closest.why: Replaces discrete top-k with soft, differentiable weighting of experts, the core capability the proposal claims as new.

survives: A twist could survive if the explicit Bayesian/Dirichlet posterior formalism combined with an online EMA-updated low-rank pairwise correlation matrix used specifically to correct for non-independence in the aggregation weights (rather than just soft routing or graph-based interaction) yields measurably different calibration/uncertainty behavior than ProbMoE's exact-marginal surrogate or the graph-based SymphonySMoE, but this is a narrow technical distinction rather than a new capability.

closest.title: Is MoE Routing a Huffman Code? Discovering the Frequency-Diversity Law in Chain-of-Thought

survives: A concrete greedy KL-based conditional-redundancy penalty computed from expert output projections (rather than gating entropy or Huffman-code framing) could be a distinguishing implementation detail, but the core claim—MDL-based selection at the router to penalize redundant expert sets—is already proposed in GeMoE and explicitly called for in the Huffman-coding paper.

closest.why: same purpose of variable expert-set sizing per token at the router, but no distribution-free coverage guarantee or calibration procedure.

survives: None of these papers derive a nonconformity-score threshold from held-out calibration data to give a formal, distribution-free 1-alpha coverage guarantee on containing the oracle-optimal expert (nor do they flag tokens where no small set can achieve the target coverage), so a rigorous conformal calibration step with certified coverage semantics would still be a genuine addition over these heuristic dynamic-k methods.

closest.title: Making Every Verified Token Count: Adaptive Verification for MoE Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: EVICT ... truncating the draft tree before target verification and retaining only the cost-effective prefix ... combines them with offline-profiled verification cost
closest.why: Uses speculate-and-verify style cost/benefit gating around MoE expert activation to cut verification cost, but at the sequence/tree level for draft-model speculative decoding, not top-1 vs top-2 router disagreement checking within a single forward pass.

closest.title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: a verifier-side expert selector that combines target-router scores with offline-estimated commitment probabilities and automatically adjusts the number of eligible experts for each verification block
closest.why: Also conditions expert computation on a confidence/commitment signal to reduce cost in MoE speculative decoding, but operates in the draft-target speculative decoding setting (accepting draft tokens) rather than proxying top-2 mixture disagreement for a single top-1 forward pass.

closest.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
closest.evidence: Experts are activated in decreasing router weight until their cumulative mass reaches a threshold, with a small extension when the admitted experts disagree.
closest.why: This is the closest mechanism match: it uses router confidence/disagreement to decide whether to activate additional experts beyond top-1, directly analogous to the proposal's disagreement-triggered top-2 computation, though applied to MoE-LoRA adapters rather than exactly matching top-2 mixture via a distilled proxy and speculate-verify framing.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—using a cheap distilled/low-rank proxy to predict top-2 disagreement before deciding to compute the real second expert, framed explicitly as speculate-and-verify with exact top-2 recovery guarantee on the disagreement subset—is not clearly present in CARE (which uses the router's own softmax mass/disagreement directly rather than a separate trained proxy network) or the speculative-decoding papers (which operate on draft-token trees, not single-token top-1-vs-top-2 disagreement), so a version centered on the proxy-network verification-with-exact-fallback guarantee could still be new.

closest.title: DAG-MoE: From Simple Mixture to Structural Aggregation in Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: replacing the standard weighted-summation aggregation with structural aggregation expands the expert-combination space without altering the experts or router, and enables possible multi-step reasoning within a single MoE layer
closest.why: targets non-additive, structured combination of already-selected experts via a learned module, close in spirit but operates on aggregation not on iterative energy-based selection of the expert subset itself.

closest.title: SDG-MoE: Signed Debate Graph Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: adds a lightweight, iterative deliberation step before final aggregation ... a signed message-passing step that updates expert representations before aggregation
closest.why: introduces iterative refinement among selected experts to capture reinforcing/corrective (non-additive) interactions, but refines expert representations/weights post-selection rather than solving a joint energy over token-expert-subset assignment via gradient descent.

closest.title: DSelect-k: Differentiable Selection in the Mixture of Experts
closest.evidence: a continuously differentiable and sparse gate for MoE, based on a novel binary encoding formulation ... offers explicit control over the number of experts to select
closest.why: addresses smooth, learnable expert-subset selection but via a differentiable encoding, not an energy-based iterative refinement process capturing joint non-additive preferences.

survives: The specific mechanism of a joint energy function E(h_token, w) over continuous relaxed expert-inclusion vectors, optimized by K explicit gradient/mean-field descent steps at inference (an iterative denoising-like rewrite of the routing weights themselves, trained with a contrastive real-vs-corrupted-subset loss) is not instantiated by any of these papers, which use either static structural aggregation, message-passing among already-selected experts, or differentiable-but-single-pass gates; a genuine implementation of iterative energy descent for expert-subset selection itself would still be new.

closest.title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
closest.evidence: we introduce Expert-Space Exploration Reinforcement Learning (ESRL), an architecture-aware framework that explicitly explores the expert-routing space of MoE models... perturbation strength is further adapted according to router entropy
closest.why: places stochastic, uncertainty-modulated exploration directly at the router's expert-selection step during training, the same component and same exploration/exploitation purpose.

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture-of-Experts: Towards Making LLMs Know What They Don't Know
closest.evidence: Instead of forcing a single, deterministic expert selection, our approach models a probability distribution over the routing decision itself... in the weight-space, the logit-space, and the final selection-space
closest.why: directly replaces deterministic top-k router selection with sampling from a posterior/probability distribution over expert choice, the same mechanism at the same component.

closest.title: Variational Routing: A Scalable Bayesian Framework for Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
closest.evidence: VMoER confines Bayesian inference to the expert-selection stage which is typically done by a deterministic routing network... inferring a temperature parameter for stochastic expert selection
closest.why: also replaces deterministic top-k routing with a Bayesian/posterior-based stochastic selection mechanism at the router.

survives: A count-based Beta/Gaussian per-expert-token-cluster posterior updated from per-token training loss as reward, with explicit sample-at-train/mean-at-inference switching framed strictly as a bandit exploration-exploitation solution replacing load-balancing losses, is a narrow variant but not clearly distinct from the Bayesian-routing and expert-space-exploration frameworks already proposed for the identical purpose at the identical component.

closest.title: Distribution-Consistent Inference for Dynamic Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: Inference-time dynamic top-$k$ routing can reduce computation without retraining, but existing methods often overlook the distributional shift caused by deviating from the training-time routing configuration.
closest.why: Also modifies per-token expert count/decision at inference using a lightweight correction, but corrects output distribution rather than verifying/rerouting the top-1 choice via a speculative top-2 comparison.

closest.title: ExpertFlow: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Inference via Predictive Expert Caching and Token Scheduling
closest.evidence: a predictive expert cache that loads only the required experts while correcting mispredictions at runtime
closest.why: Uses a predict-then-correct-mispredictions pattern at the router, similar in spirit to speculative-then-verify, but targeted at cache/memory efficiency rather than correcting the routed FFN output itself.

closest.title: Elbow-Based MoE Routing: A Training-Free Inference Time Plugin for Expert Selection
closest.evidence: a training-free inference-time modification that dynamically adjusts the number of experts on a per-token basis
closest.why: Also dynamically decides when to spend extra expert compute per token based on router signal confidence, but uses a distributional elbow heuristic rather than a trained verifier comparing top-1 vs top-2 outputs.

survives: The specific mechanism of speculatively computing both top-1 and top-2 FFN outputs and using a trained lightweight verifier scorer (conditioned on an EMA of historical per-expert hit-rate) to choose which to commit before writing to the residual stream is not explicitly implemented in any of these papers, which instead do cache-miss correction, distributional recalibration, or heuristic expert-count adjustment.

closest.evidence: VMoER confines Bayesian inference to the expert-selection stage ... reduces calibration error by 94%, and increases out-of-distribution AUROC by 12%
closest.why: Places a calibrated probabilistic mechanism directly at the MoE router to turn gate outputs into trustworthy uncertainty signals, the same component and purpose as proposed.

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture-of-Experts: Towards Making LLMs Know What They Don't Know
closest.evidence: models a probability distribution over the routing decision itself ... significantly improves routing stability, in-distribution calibration, and out-of-distribution (OoD) detection
closest.why: Directly reworks the router into a calibrated probabilistic head so its output can serve as a trustworthy per-token uncertainty/confidence signal, matching the proposal's new capability.

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture of Experts For Large Language Models
closest.evidence: applies a structured Laplace approximation ... enabling calibrated uncertainty estimation without modifying the original training procedure
closest.why: Also targets calibrated per-expert/router uncertainty in MoE LLMs, though it applies Bayesian inference to expert layers rather than router logits specifically, making it slightly less central than the top two.

survives: Little room remains unless the mixture-density-of-Gaussians parameterization trained against realized downstream loss (rather than variational/Laplace/Bayesian posteriors over routing logits) yields materially different calibration behavior or enables new abstention/compute-triggering mechanisms not demonstrated in VMoER or Bayesian-MoE.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we propose a data-free, online test-time framework that continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data... During the prefill stage, and later in regular intervals, we optimize the routing decisions of the model using self-supervision based on the already generated sequence... We implement this through lightweight additive vectors that only update router logits in selected layers
closest.why: This is exactly test-time training of the router only, at regular intervals, using self-supervision from the generated sequence, freezing the rest of the model — the same component, mechanism, and purpose (adapting expert selection to distribution shift at inference without labels).

closest.title: R2-T2: Re-Routing in Test-Time for Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: we propose a novel and efficient method "Re-Routing in Test-Time (R2-T2)" that locally optimizes the vector of routing weights in test-time... without training any base-model parameters
closest.why: Also optimizes only router outputs at test time per-sample while freezing the base model, matching the placement and purpose even though the optimization strategy differs (neighbor search vs SGD proxy loss).

closest.title: Local Mixtures of Experts: Essentially Free Test-Time Training via Model Merging
closest.evidence: We show that TTMM is an approximation of test-time training (TTT), which fine-tunes an expert model for each prediction task, i.e., prompt.
closest.why: Explicitly frames MoE-based test-time training as approximating TTT for adapting to the input at inference, though it merges/adapts experts rather than only router parameters.

survives: The proposal's twist of updating only a small subset of router parameters via a hindsight-teacher-forced next-token loss (rather than additive router-logit vectors or output-side re-weighting) is a narrow implementation difference, not a new capability, so it would need a demonstrably different self-supervised objective or theoretical guarantee to survive as new.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we propose a data-free, online test-time framework that continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data ... we optimize the routing decisions of the model using self-supervision based on the already generated sequence
closest.why: Same component (router) and same capability (mid-sequence, gradient-free adaptation of routing based on the model's own recent generation) as the proposal, though via additive router-logit vectors optimized by self-supervised loss rather than a Hebbian outer-product update.

closest.title: STAR: Rethinking MoE Routing as Structure-Aware Subspace Learning
closest.evidence: augmenting standard learnable routing with an evolving principal subspace that tracks dominant input structure via Generalized Hebbian Algorithm (GHA)
closest.why: Uses a Hebbian-style update mechanism directly on the router to adapt routing to input structure, including test-time subspace updates, but purpose is stabilizing specialization/robustness rather than reacting to per-token downstream prediction error within a sequence.

closest.title: Adaptive Hebbian Memory Routing in Vision Transformers for Few-Shot Learning
closest.evidence: Hebbian fast-weight memory can provide temporary associative information during an episode... a lightweight MLP router to control the contribution of Hebbian memory, the strength of memory updates, and the retention of previous memory
closest.why: Combines Hebbian fast-weights with routing, but the fast-weights are applied to a memory module, not to the router's own gate weights, and the router controls memory blending rather than being itself modulated by Hebbian error feedback.

survives: The specific mechanism of an outer-product Hebbian fast-weight matrix added directly onto the router's gate weight, driven explicitly by the chosen expert's downstream prediction-error signal (not self-supervised loss on generated text or GHA-based subspace tracking), applied per-token with decay/reset within a sequence, is not demonstrated by any of these; a rigorous comparison against STAR's GHA-router and Rewiring's self-supervised router-vector update would need to show this error-driven Hebbian credit-assignment step is a genuinely distinct update rule.

closest.title: Deep Delta Learning
closest.evidence: Each layer reads the current state along a learned direction, compares the resulting readout with a learned target, and writes back a gated rank-1 correction along the same direction. Closing the gate recovers the identity map, while fully opening it exactly overwrites the selected residual readout.
closest.why: This is exactly a per-block delta-rule erase/overwrite operator applied directly to the residual stream state, matching the proposal's placement, mechanism, and stated capability (targeted overwrite rather than pure additive superposition).

closest.title: Massive Activations Are Architecturally Robust: A Controlled Scratch/Commitment Residual Stream Test
closest.evidence: a mutable scratch stream (Deliberation) that intermediate computation may freely overwrite

closest.title: Enhancing Linear Attention with Residual Learning
closest.evidence: we introduce a delta-rule version, Residual Delta Net (RDN), incorporating adaptive gating and residual clipping for enhanced correction control and stability
closest.why: Applies delta-rule gating to a residual/correction mechanism but within linear-attention state rather than the literal backbone residual stream.

survives: Nothing distinct remains: DDL already implements a gated rank-1 read-compare-overwrite delta-rule update directly on the residual stream at each layer, matching the proposal's mechanism, placement, and purpose almost exactly.
