closest.evidence: AdaPonderLM uses iteration-specific MLP gates with a monotonic halting mask to decide when each token stops recurring... reduces inference compute at about 10% while maintaining comparable language modeling perplexity
closest.why: Same capability (per-token variable re-application of a block/loop with a learned halting signal, budget-penalized) at the same component (recurrent layer depth), differing only in using MLP gates rather than a PID controller.

closest.title: Adaptive Computation Modules: Granular Conditional Computation For Efficient Inference
closest.evidence: An additional gating mechanism determines the optimal number of learners to execute for each token
closest.why: Also implements per-token variable iteration count via a learned gate deciding how many times to refine, the same mechanism/purpose as the proposal's re-entry decision.

closest.title: DACT-BERT: Differentiable Adaptive Computation Time for an Efficient BERT Inference
closest.evidence: DACT-BERT adds an adaptive computational mechanism to BERT's regular processing pipeline, which controls the number of Transformer blocks that need to be executed at inference time.
closest.why: Same halting/adaptive-depth idea (ACT-style ponder mechanism) applied per-token to control block repetition, directly overlapping with the proposed layer-schedule feedback loop.

survives: The specific twist of using an explicit trained PID (proportional-integral-derivative) control law—with separate P/I/D gains reacting to residual-norm error dynamics rather than a single learned scalar halting probability—is a different controller parameterization, but since ACT/AdaPonderLM/ACM already achieve the identical capability (data-dependent iterate count via error/halting signal) at the identical component, this is a controller-design variant rather than a new capability.

closest.title: Differentiable Generalised Predictive Coding
closest.evidence: Gradient-based predictive coding optimises inferred states and weights locally in for each layer by optimising precision-weighted prediction errors that propagate from stimuli towards latent states.
closest.why: This applies iterative gradient-based error-minimization inference per layer, the same core mechanism (error e, gradient update to a local state estimate) proposed in the proposal, though not specifically instantiated as a transformer layer-schedule replacement with T-step gating.

closest.title: Predictive Coding Approximates Backprop along Arbitrary Computation Graphs
closest.evidence: predictive coding converges asymptotically (and in practice rapidly) to exact backprop gradients on arbitrary computation graphs using only local learning rules... We construct predictive coding CNNs, RNNs, and the more complex LSTMs
closest.why: Shows PC's iterative local-error inference loop applied within standard deep architectures as an alternative to feedforward computation, the same placement (per-layer iterative refinement replacing single forward pass) though for training-algorithm equivalence rather than as an inference-time transformer capability with convergence gating.

closest.title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding
closest.evidence: PC-ALM introduces recurrent dynamics in each layer's activations... aligns each weight update toward BP by accumulating per-layer constraint errors into a layer-local Lagrange multiplier
closest.why: Also inserts per-layer iterative recurrent error-driven refinement of local activations, matching the mechanism of inner-loop mu updates via local error, differing mainly in the objective (matching BP gradients) and lacking the transformer-specific gated re-application/convergence-detection framing.

survives: The proposal's specific instantiation as a drop-in replacement for the transformer residual stream at nano-scale with matched-FLOPs comparison and adaptive-T convergence-gated re-application (rather than as a biologically-motivated alternative to backprop or a generic feedforward-to-PC translation) is a narrower systems/architecture claim not directly tested in the cited PC papers, so a demonstration that this gating yields a genuinely new capability (early-exit-like convergence detection at inference within a causal transformer) could still be novel.

closest.title: Selective Sinkhorn Routing for Improved Sparse Mixture of Experts
closest.evidence: We revisit the token-to-expert assignment as an optimal transport problem. We add constraints to ensure balanced expert utilization... derives gating scores directly from the transport map
closest.why: Applies Sinkhorn-based balanced-marginal OT routing to guarantee expert load balance, the same mechanism/purpose but at the granularity of discrete MoE experts rather than dense FFN key-value memory slots.

closest.title: DOT-MoE: Differentiable Optimal Transport for MoEfication
closest.evidence: we model neuron assignment as a balanced transport problem, utilizing differentiable Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations to enforce strict expert capacity constraints
closest.why: Uses Sinkhorn OT with hard capacity/marginal constraints directly on FFN neurons (partitioning the FFN itself), closely matching the proposal's placement inside the FFN rather than at a separate MoE gate.

closest.title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
closest.evidence: region-to-expert assignment formulated as entropic optimal transport (Sinkhorn) with explicit per slide capacity marginals, enforcing balanced expert utilisation without auxiliary load-balancing losses
closest.why: Same Sinkhorn balanced-marginal mechanism for hard load-balancing guarantees, applied to MoE expert routing rather than a standard dense FFN's key-value memory.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—treating the FFN's key-value memory itself (not discrete MoE experts) as the doubly-stochastic-routed object, with capacity constraints per key/neuron in an otherwise dense, non-MoE FFN—is closest to DOT-MoE's neuron-level Sinkhorn assignment, so genuine novelty would require showing the guarantee/inspection benefit holds for a standard dense-FFN key-value view distinct from any expert partitioning, which none of the papers directly frame that way.

closest.title: HoReN: Normalized Hopfield Retrieval for Large-Scale Sequential Model Editing
closest.evidence: HoReN treats each codebook entry as both a knowledge key and a Hopfield stored pattern, retrieves edits by angular similarity on the unit hypersphere, and refines queries through damped Hopfield dynamics
closest.why: Same mechanism (iterative Hopfield energy-descent retrieval over a key-value memory attached to an MLP layer) but applied to model editing/knowledge patching rather than replacing the FFN's core forward computation end-to-end from scratch.

closest.title: Hierarchical Associative Memory, Parallelized MLP-Mixer, and Symmetry Breaking
closest.evidence: integrating Krotov's hierarchical associative memory with MetaFormers, enabling a comprehensive representation of the entire Transformer block ... as a single Hopfield network
closest.why: Casts the whole transformer block including FFN-like mixing as Hopfield/associative-memory energy dynamics, closely overlapping with reinterpreting FFN as Hopfield retrieval.

closest.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
closest.evidence: feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns
closest.why: Establishes the FFN-as-key-value-memory framing the proposal builds on, but uses single-step score-and-sum, not iterative Hopfield convergence.

survives: The proposal's specific twist is training the pattern set/beta end-to-end from scratch as a direct multi-step-iteration replacement for the FFN's single matmul at matched FLOPs (rather than as a post-hoc editing/interpretability wrapper as in HoReN), which is not demonstrated in these papers.

closest.title: Decoupling Knowledge and Reasoning in Transformers: A Modular Architecture with Generalized Cross-Attention
closest.evidence: the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) in a standard Transformer is a specialized case (a closure) of this generalized cross-attention, revealing its role in implicit knowledge retrieval... explicitly decouples knowledge and reasoning through a generalized cross-attention mechanism to a globally shared knowledge base
closest.why: This replaces the FFN with a cross-attention retrieval over an external knowledge base, the same placement and purpose of decoupling capacity from parameters via retrieval, though framed as cross-attention rather than kNN search.

closest.title: Mixture of Lookup Experts
closest.evidence: these experts can be re-parameterized as lookup tables (LUTs) that retrieves expert outputs based on input ids, and offloaded to storage devices
closest.why: Also converts FFN computation into an external lookup/retrieval structure to decouple capacity from active parameter compute, though keyed on input ids rather than learned kNN over activation vectors.

closest.title: Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation
closest.evidence: Parametric retrieval-augmented generation (Parametric RAG), a new RAG paradigm that integrates external knowledge directly into the parameters of feed-forward networks (FFN) of an LLM through document parameterization
closest.why: Targets the FFN as the site for injecting/expanding external knowledge/memory without full retraining, similar capacity-growth motivation but via parameterization rather than kNN search over a bank.

survives: The specific mechanism of exact top-k nearest-neighbor search over a frozen/refreshed (key,value) activation bank feeding attention-like mixing into the FFN down-projection, trained/matched at FLOPs parity as in Memorizing Transformers/kNN-LM but applied inside the FFN sublayer rather than at the output layer or via cross-attention, is not directly shown in these papers.

closest.title: Forget, Anticipate and Adapt: Test Time Training for Long Videos
closest.evidence: TTT is a mechanism in which a model adapts to an incoming test-sample by performing some self-supervised (SSL) task and updating its weights even during inference... operates on only three frames within the sliding window

survives: The specific twist of grafting a frozen-base rank-r LoRA solely onto the FFN down-projection with a strictly causal masked reconstruction of past FFN hidden activations (not full weight TTT or offloaded memory blocks) in an autoregressive LM stream is not exactly what Locas or the video/3D TTT papers do, so a tightly scoped causal-LM FFN adapter variant could still be new, though it is a narrow delta.

survives: Nothing distinguishes this proposal from 2506.12000/2009.13003/ExCP, which already quantize+entropy-code optimizer moment/gradient tensors per empirical distribution purely as an I/O-path checkpoint codec; a genuinely new twist would need a different guarantee (e.g. provable bit-exact bounded-loss reconstruction certificates or exploiting cross-step redundancy in a way none of these do).

closest.title: Gefen: Optimized Stochastic Optimizer
closest.evidence: automatically shares second-moment estimates across parameter blocks and quantizes the first moment using a learned codebook, thereby reducing AdamW's memory footprint by ~8x while maintaining the same performance
closest.why: Same target (per-parameter second moment replaced by learned block/module-shared low-dimensional statistics) and same purpose (structured, lower-dimensional optimizer state for Adam-like adaptivity), differing mainly in the block-sharing/quantization mechanism versus an explicit IB-trained encoder-decoder.

closest.title: CAME: Confidence-guided Adaptive Memory Efficient Optimization
closest.evidence: we first study a confidence-guided strategy to reduce the instability of existing memory efficient optimizers... to simultaneously achieve two goals: fast convergence as in traditional adaptive methods, and low memory usage as in memory-efficient methods
closest.why: Same component (second-moment optimizer state) and same purpose (compress it while preserving predictive power for adaptivity), though via a confidence heuristic rather than an explicit mutual-information objective.

closest.title: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization
closest.evidence: We describe an effective and flexible adaptive optimization method with greatly reduced memory overhead. Our method retains the benefits of per-parameter adaptivity while allowing significantly larger models and batch sizes.
closest.why: Adafactor-style factored second-moment approximation is the direct ancestor of replacing per-parameter v with a compressed per-module representation for the same adaptivity purpose.

survives: The explicit information-bottleneck training objective (minimizing I(z; raw grads) while maximizing an auxiliary decoder's predictive power for next-step gradient magnitude) as a provable, tunable compression criterion is not what Gefen, CAME, or Adafactor do—they use heuristic sharing/confidence/factorization rather than an IB loss with a trained encoder/decoder, so a rigorous IB-based ablation of exactly how much state is necessary would be a genuine (if narrow) methodological twist.

closest.title: Online Learning of a Memory for Learning Rates

survives: A genuinely new angle could survive if the delta-rule's causal, in-place erase-then-write update (with formal fast-weight-programmer guarantees) is shown to give qualitatively different stability/capacity properties than the heuristic or search-based controllers in ExpTest/AdaLRS/POLA-style memories, but as stated the capability and placement are already covered.

closest.title: Velocitune: A Velocity-based Dynamic Domain Reweighting Method for Continual Pre-training

closest.title: SPICE: Synergy and Partial Information Based Curriculum Evolution

closest.title: EASE-TTT: Evidence-Aligned Selective Test-Time Training for Long-Context Question Answering

EASE-TTT... converts selected evidence chunks into a soft attention supervision target over their token positions... EASE-TTT uses the resulting attention target to guide query-side adaptation
closest.why: this adapts attention allocation parameters online via a self-supervised/evidence-aligned objective during inference, the same component (attention-topology/allocation) and mechanism family (test-time parameter updates on a stream) but for evidence localization rather than dynamic window widening.

closest.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
closest.evidence: our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights... a Transformer with sliding-window attention
closest.why: uses next-token-prediction-driven online SGD updates on a streaming window with sliding-window attention, closely matching the proposal's update rule and objective, but the updated parameters are general fast-weights/model weights rather than a dedicated low-rank attention-mask gating vector reshaping connectivity.

closest.title: Training-free Context-adaptive Attention for Efficient Long Context Modeling
closest.evidence: an online token selection phase that adaptively retains core context tokens using a lightweight redundancy metric... without requiring parameter updates or architectural changes
closest.why: targets the same capability (input-adaptive reshaping of attention connectivity mid-sequence) but via a training-free heuristic rather than gradient-based test-time training of gate parameters.

survives: A twist could survive if the gate is explicitly a per-head low-rank bias trained once and then adapted purely to trigger connectivity/window changes (not evidence localization or general context compression) with an explicit widening-on-loss-spike mechanism validated as such, since EASE-TTT targets evidence alignment and E2E-TTT updates general fast weights rather than an explicit topology-widening gate.

closest.title: Real-time speech enhancement with dynamic attention span

closest.title: SWAA: Sliding Window Attention Adaptation for Efficient and Quality Preserving Long Context Processing
closest.evidence: preserving ‘sink’ tokens and (4) lightweight fine tuning, which mitigate the training inference mismatch
closest.why: Adapts window width and sink-token count together for attention topology, similar to the proposal's target of window+sink, though as a static/offline recipe rather than closed-loop control.

survives: A genuine PID closed-loop control law (explicit error-tracking with proportional-integral-derivative gains against a measured entropy/loss error, tuned per-head via grid search rather than learned end-to-end) is a different control mechanism than the learned/gated adaptive controllers in GSA or the dynamic-span network in the speech paper, so a strict claim about closed-loop feedback control (vs. learned/heuristic adaptation) could still be a narrow but real twist.

closest.title: Parameter-free Adaptive Sparse Attention via Compression-Based Content Selection
closest.evidence: Because the compression profile is input-dependent, the resulting sparse mask adapts dynamically to content without learned parameters, auxiliary losses, or custom kernels.
closest.why: Uses a compression-based (description-length-adjacent) criterion computed online to select among sparse attention patterns per input, matching the proposal's mechanism and component but via gzip ratios rather than an explicit MDL model-bits + residual-bits computation with candidate topology families.

closest.title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
closest.evidence: DHSA performs hierarchical routing by estimating importance at the chunk level and propagating it to token-level interactions, preserving causally important dependencies while enabling efficient sparsification.
closest.why: Also predicts attention sparsity/topology online per input while keeping backbone frozen, same component and adaptive-topology capability, though the selection criterion is a learned importance predictor rather than an MDL codelength comparison across a fixed topology family.

closest.title: Attention Sparsity is Input-Stable: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation via Offline Sparsity Profiling and Online QK Co-Clustering
closest.evidence: SVOO adopts a two-stage paradigm: (i) offline layer-wise sensitivity profiling to derive intrinsic per-layer pruning levels, and (ii) online block-wise sparse attention via a bidirectional co-clustering algorithm.
closest.why: Same idea of profiling then choosing sparsity/topology per input online, but the selection is via clustering/profiling not an explicit MDL codelength criterion over a discrete topology menu.

survives: The explicit MDL formulation—computing an actual two-part code (log topology-code + cross-entropy bits under each candidate mask on a held-out subsegment) and choosing the minimizer, over a small enumerable menu of named topologies (dense/windowed/sink/strided) shared-trained at matched budget—is a more principled, exactly-computed criterion than compression-ratio heuristics or learned importance scores, so a rigorous MDL-vs-heuristic comparison could still be a genuine contribution.

survives: Nothing genuinely new survives: the RG framing is just relabeling the same coarse-filter-then-fine-attend block-sparse mechanism already implemented (with joint training and matched compute) in HISA and DashAttention.

closest.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
closest.evidence: a "slow" neural net learns by gradient descent to program the "fast weights" of another net through sequences of elementary programming instructions which are additive outer products of self-invented activation patterns (today called keys and values)
closest.why: establishes the exact additive-outer-product fast-weight mechanism the proposal reuses, but as the entirety of attention (replacing softmax attention), not as a gating bias added to a separate static QK^T topology mask.

closest.title: Enabling Robust In-Context Memory and Rapid Task Adaptation in Transformers with Hebbian and Gradient-Based Plasticity
closest.evidence: we augment decoder-only Transformers with fast-weight modules updated either by (i) a neuromodulated Hebbian rule
closest.why: adds a Hebbian fast-weight module alongside attention for in-context adaptation, close in spirit but framed as a separate memory module for task adaptation rather than as an additive bias perturbing the attention-topology/mask itself.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: Recurrent fast-weight memories ... compress an expanding context into a fixed-size recurrent state, making the state transition an online learning rule

closest.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule

closest.title: Erase-then-Delta Attention: Decoupling Erase and Write Addresses in Delta-Rule Linear Attention

survives: A genuinely new angle would require showing the side lane specifically decouples read causality (queries at position t reading only past-written overwrites without ever seeing future tokens) in a way that differs functionally from HOLA's dual-memory or Gated DeltaNet's hybrid gating, e.g. a formal proof/ablation isolating the 'meaning revision without future leakage' property as distinct from simply improving recall; as stated the placement (delta-rule lane alongside causal attention) is already explored.

closest.title: Dialogue Without Limits: Constant-Sized KV Caches for Extended Responses in LLMs
closest.evidence: captures inter-token correlation with greater accuracy... iteratively refines the KV cache via lightweight updates guided by attention patterns of recent tokens

closest.title: GRKV: Global Regression for Training-Free KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLMs
closest.evidence: GRKV uses ridge-regression-based merge steps to distribute information from evicted tokens across retained tokens, while regularizing the updates to prevent over-smoothing
closest.why: also rewrites cached KV entries using later/aggregate information to denoise stale representations, though framed for compression not coherence.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need to show that Hopfield energy-descent rewriting (multi-step, content-addressed, attractor-based) yields qualitatively different long-range coherence gains than the existing delta-rule erase-write or attention-guided iterative refinement schemes at matched budget, since the mechanism class (in-place causal-safe KV rewrite triggered by later context) is already occupied by EDA and MorphKV/GRKV for closely related purposes.

closest.title: Retrospective Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Generation
closest.evidence: RetroAttention, a novel KV cache update technique that retrospectively revises past attention outputs using newly arrived KV entries from subsequent decoding steps... This breaks the fixed-attention-output paradigm and allows continual correction of prior approximations.
closest.why: Same mechanism/placement: periodically correcting existing cache entries in-place using later context, streaming, to fix accumulated approximation error rather than re-encoding from scratch.

closest.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries
closest.evidence: predictive delta coding, stores only the residual of each new KV vector from the model's own prediction of it
closest.why: Same core idea of storing/propagating a compact prediction-error residual against cache entries rather than full re-encoded values.

closest.title: HeadQ: Model-Visible Distortion and Score-Space Correction for KV-Cache Quantization
closest.evidence: stores a low-rank residual side code in a calibration-learned query basis and applies it as an additive logit correction... fixed-attention readout gives an A^2-weighted token-distortion surrogate
closest.why: Same operation of adding a learned residual correction to cached value/key representations to correct persistent error cheaply, applied forward at read time.

survives: Little room remains unless the predictive-coding framing yields a demonstrably different training/inference behavior (e.g. explicit top-down generative prediction rather than a learned residual/delta), but as an in-place additive correction to cached values driven by prediction error it is functionally covered by RetroAttention's retrospective revision and delta-coding/residual-correction approaches already in the pool.

closest.why: Archer addresses the same underlying tension (mutable/rewritable hidden states vs. immutable causal cache) but as a caching-efficiency fix for existing DLM rollback, not as a mechanism that grafts a bounded atomic rewrite window onto an otherwise causal autoregressive decoder.

closest.title: MotionStream: Real-Time Video Generation with Interactive Motion Controls

closest.title: Knot Forcing: Taming Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models for Real-time Infinite Interactive Portrait Animation

survives: The proposal's twist—an explicit all-or-nothing learned commit gate that atomically accepts/discards a bidirectional rewrite pass over a bounded trailing buffer in a text-token autoregressive transformer, trained from scratch at matched FLOPs—is not demonstrated by Archer (training-free KV cache reuse for already-bidirectional DLMs) or the video-streaming window/knot papers (smoothing/sink mechanisms without atomic commit gating or rollback semantics); a genuinely novel contribution would need to show this gated atomic transaction mechanism itself, not just windowed revision or cache reuse.

closest.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
closest.evidence: a "slow" neural net learns by gradient descent to program the "fast weights" of another net through sequences of elementary programming instructions which are additive outer products of self-invented activation patterns (today called keys and values)
closest.why: This establishes the exact outer-product fast-weight update A_t = decay*A_{t-1} + outer(k_t,v_t) as the core FWP mechanism the proposal reuses, but as a general sequence-modeling replacement for attention, not specifically framed as enabling 'causal-consistent revision' of a token's effective representation via later tokens.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: We study this rule under read-after-write autoregressive semantics. For the prefix-prediction objective considered here, the local fast-memory example revealed at step t is the prefix-aligned pair (x_t,y_t)=(φ(k_{t-1}),v_t)... The common same-step association (φ(k_t),v_t) remains causal, but optimizes a different internal objective.
closest.why: This paper explicitly analyzes fast-weight recurrent state under read-after-write causal semantics, i.e. the same idea that later-step updates to the fast memory affect what earlier-written positions can retrieve, which is very close to the proposal's 'update without touching stored KV' framing.

closest.title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
closest.evidence: These "fast weights" can be used to store temporary memories of the recent past and they provide a neurally plausible way of implementing the type of attention to the past that has recently proved very helpful in sequence-to-sequence models.
closest.why: This is the original Hebbian fast-weight association mechanism for attending to recent tokens, matching the proposal's Hebbian outer-product update but without the explicit causal-revision framing or dual-cache-plus-fast-weight read architecture.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need to show that the dual-path read (causal KV cache + separate short-horizon fast-weight matrix, trained jointly with matched parameter budget by trading off attention heads) produces a measurable causality-compliant 'revision' effect—i.e., that later tokens change how earlier positions are effectively read downstream—as a targeted ablation/capability claim, rather than just presenting fast-weights as an efficient attention substitute or memory augmentation as prior work does.

closest.title: Evolutionary Stochastic Gradient Descent for Optimization of Deep Neural Networks
closest.evidence: ESGD combines SGD and gradient-free evolutionary algorithms as complementary algorithms in one framework in which the optimization alternates between the SGD step and evolution step to improve the average fitness of the population.
closest.why: This proposes population-based mutation/selection interleaved with SGD steps at the same component (the gradient/update step) with an explicit fitness evaluation, which is the same general mechanism (evolutionary population applied to gradient step).

closest.title: Direct From Darwin: Deriving Advanced Optimizers From Evolutionary First Principles
closest.evidence: we prove that a broad family of battle-tested optimization algorithms are already perfectly compatible with evolutionary dynamics... By simply adding DLS noise (i.e., evolutionarily faithful genetic drift), these algorithms become scientifically valid in silico simulations of Darwinian evolution.
closest.why: Also frames gradient-step optimization through evolutionary/population dynamics with structured noise, though its purpose is theoretical unification rather than fitness-based step selection.

closest.title: Stochastic Gradient Line Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Noise-Robust Optimization of Parameterized Quantum Circuits
closest.evidence: SGLBO reduces the measurement-shot cost by estimating an appropriate direction of updating circuit parameters based on stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and further utilizing Bayesian optimization (BO) to estimate the optimal step size for each iteration in SGD.
closest.why: Similar idea of evaluating candidate update directions/step sizes against a cheap validation signal before committing, though via Bayesian optimization rather than mutation/selection.

survives: The specific twist of generating explicit mutant gradient variants scaled to per-layer norm and selecting/blending via a cheap held-out microbatch fitness check (rather than alternating population evolution steps or step-size search) is a narrower, more surgical mechanism than ESGD's population-based training loop, so a tightly scoped ablation showing this exact per-step mutate-and-select filter catches bad steps that ESGD's periodic evolution phase would miss could still be novel.

survives: Only the specific gating rule (skipping/scaling a layer's update when its local error is already small) is a minor addition not explicitly tested in these papers, but it is a straightforward inference-time thresholding on the already-standard PC local error signal, not a new mechanism or placement.

closest.title: L1 Augmented Attention as an Improved Vector Similarity Metric
closest.evidence: subtracts a learned, head specific L1 distance between queries and keys from the dot product score
closest.why: Same placement (attention scores, pre-softmax) and same mechanism shape (dot product minus a learned distance penalty between projected q and k), differing mainly in that the distance is computed from low-dimensional projections rather than a rank/transport index.

closest.title: LOTFormer: Doubly-Stochastic Linear Attention via Low-Rank Optimal Transport
closest.evidence: LOTFormer, a linear time doubly stochastic attention mechanism derived from an optimal transport view of attention as a coupling between query and key measures
closest.why: Also reframes attention via optimal transport but changes the normalization/coupling structure rather than adding a learned scalar rank-distance penalty to dot products.

closest.title: Modeling Localness for Self-Attention Networks
closest.evidence: cast localness modeling as a learnable Gaussian bias, which indicates the central and scope of the local region to be paid more attention
closest.why: Same purpose (penalize/bias attention by a learned notion of distance) at the same component, but the bias is a Gaussian window over fixed positions, not a learned rank/index-predicted transport coordinate.

survives: The specific twist of training a learned-index-style monotone rank predictor per token (rather than a raw distance in embedding/position space) to derive the transport coordinate, and combining it with an OT-cost interpretation rather than a generic learned distance penalty, is not exactly instantiated in the closest papers.

closest.title: Filtered not Mixed: Stochastic Filtering-Based Online Gating for Mixture of Large Language Models
closest.evidence: our approach employs time-adaptive stochastic filtering techniques to combine experts... leverages the conditional information in each expert's running performance to forecast the best combination of LLMs
closest.why: Uses a stochastic (Bayesian/HMM) filter tracking per-expert running performance to reweight expert combination scores at each step, the same core mechanism and purpose as fusing router score with a persistent reliability state, though applied to combining whole pretrained LLM outputs rather than inside a transformer MoE router's top-k gate.

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture-of-Experts: Towards Making LLMs Know What They Don't Know
closest.evidence: we propose a structured Bayesian MoE routing framework. Instead of forcing a single, deterministic expert selection, our approach models a probability distribution over the routing decision itself... in the weight-space, the logit-space, and the final selection-space
closest.why: Injects persistent uncertainty into router logits for calibration purposes, adjacent in mechanism/component but aimed at calibration/OoD detection rather than tracking drifting per-expert accuracy to reweight the gate.

closest.title: MoE-Based Learned Inertial Odometry for Bicycle Localization
closest.evidence: a neural velocity predictor... is tightly coupled with an extended Kalman filter for three-dimensional pose estimation... realized as a sparsely-gated Mixture of Experts (MoE) network with top-K routing
closest.why: Combines Kalman filtering with MoE routing but the Kalman filter operates on the pose/velocity output, not on per-expert router reliability, so mechanism-object pairing differs.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need a closed-form per-expert Kalman state (mean+variance) fused via inverse-variance weighting directly into the top-k router logits inside a transformer MoE layer, tracking online accuracy drift under distribution shift — the MoE-F paper does the analogous filtering but at the level of combining whole LLM predictions via HMM/Bayesian filtering rather than modifying token-level router logits pre-topk, so a demonstration that this specific in-router Kalman fusion changes expert selection and improves robustness to drift within a single trained MoE layer would still be a distinct, unclaimed result.

closest.title: Affinity Is Not Enough: Recovering the Free Energy Principle in Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: anticipatory routing, a next-state predictor conditioned on the beta-accumulated hidden state ... precision-weighted gating (Pi), a per-expert inverse variance of recent prediction error
closest.why: this paper already places a predictive/anticipatory mechanism at the MoE router that scores routing based on predicted vs actual hidden state error, the same component and closely related purpose of exploiting prediction residuals for routing.

closest.title: FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online Moe Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction
closest.evidence: FreeBalance leverages cross-layer similarities in hidden representations within the residual network to build a lightweight workload predictor... enabling proactive expert migration planning before routing decisions are available
closest.why: uses a predictor of hidden-state-derived residual signal before routing, but for load-balancing/migration rather than for changing what the router scores.

closest.title: Share First, Route What Remains: A Unified Framework for Token-Adaptive MoE Computation
closest.evidence: share first, then route what remains ... the complementary demand determines the residual expert count through cumulative routing mass
closest.why: routes based on a residual computed after removing an already-explained (shared) component, conceptually the same 'route the unexplained part' idea though computed via shared-expert subtraction rather than causal next-layer prediction.

survives: The specific causal predictive-coding formulation—predicting the current hidden state from the previous layer's chosen expert output via a trained predict head and routing on that residual, jointly trained end-to-end with matched FLOPs—is not exactly instantiated in 2605.00604 (which predicts next-token/next-state hidden states for transition detection rather than attributing residual to 'already explained by chosen expert') so a tightly scoped version emphasizing expert-attributed prediction (not just temporal/sequence prediction) could still be distinct, but the core mechanism and purpose are close enough that this must be argued explicitly against 2605.00604.

closest.title: Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing Strategy for Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: before the top-K routing decision, Loss-Free Balancing will first apply an expert-wise bias to the routing scores of each expert... does not produce any interference gradients
closest.why: solves the same decoupling problem (separating balance objective from quality-only routing loss) at the same moe-router component but via a bias term rather than a dual-gate override mechanism

closest.title: Incast-Free MoE Rate-Based Scheduling
closest.evidence: Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures have become key to large language models; however, their typical round-robin (RR) scheduling introduces significant bottlenecks
closest.why: treats round-robin/hash-style routing as a baseline fallback mechanism analogous to the proposal's 'reflex gate' but for network scheduling rather than quality-vs-balance tradeoff

closest.title: Binary-Integer-Programming Based Algorithm for Expert Load Balancing in Mixture-of-Experts Models
closest.evidence: maintains an additional vector q on each MoE layer that can help change the top-K order of s by solving a binary integer programming with very small time costs
closest.why: also introduces a secondary small parameter/mechanism layered on top of the quality-trained router purely to enforce balance, similar decoupling spirit

survives: The specific conditional-override architecture—two fully independent gates (parameter-free hash reflex vs. quality-only learned gate) arbitrated by a single trained per-layer confidence-margin threshold—is a distinct control-flow design not explicitly tested in Loss-Free Balancing's additive-bias approach, so a demonstration that margin-gated hard override outperforms bias-based decoupling would be new.

closest.title: Real-time Streaming Video Denoising with Bidirectional Buffers
closest.evidence: we propose a Bidirectional Streaming Video Denoising (BSVD) framework, to achieve high-fidelity real-time denoising for streaming videos with both past and future temporal receptive fields... a novel Bidirectional Buffer Block as the core module of our BSVD

closest.title: RDDMPI: Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Multivariate Time Series Imputation
closest.evidence: we reformulate probabilistic imputation as a baseline-residual decomposition, where a pretrained model captures the dominant signal and a diffusion process models the residual uncertainty
closest.why: Uses diffusion denoising explicitly on a 'residual' representation to revise/correct prior estimates, but in a time-series imputation context rather than a transformer's residual stream as read by downstream blocks.

survives: The proposal would survive only if the exact instantiation matters: applying masked-diffusion denoising specifically to a transformer's residual-stream cache (not video buffers or generic time-series residuals) with a periodic-every-k-tokens side-buffer overwrite scheme that downstream blocks preferentially read, is not shown by any paper here operating on LLM residual streams with this bidirectional-diffusion mechanism, whereas the closest paper (LPSR) achieves a similar retraction capability via a different (steering-vector/rollback) mechanism rather than masked denoising.

closest.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
closest.evidence: Test-time training (TTT) views sequence modeling as an online learning problem in which fast weights are updated by an internal learning rule... exposes the fast-weight network, loss function, learning rate, weight decay, and normalization as explicit design dimensions.
closest.why: Directly generalizes TTT machinery (loss, adapter, learning rate schedule) but as a token-mixing/sequence-model replacement rather than a per-token residual-write-width gate inserted into a transformer block's residual path.

closest.title: LARA: Lightweight Adapters in the Residual Stream for Composable Adaptation and Alignment
closest.evidence: LARA reads the hidden state at a small set of layers and adds a correction of low rank back to the residual stream, leaving all base weights untouched... routed automatically per token.
closest.why: Same component (residual stream, low-rank additive write, per-token routing) but the adaptation is trained offline per-behavior and selected/interpolated at inference, not updated online via a per-token self-supervised gradient step.

closest.title: TALAN: Task-Aligned Latent Adaptation Networks for Targeted Post-Training of Large Language Models
closest.evidence: a sequence-conditioned latent side path inserted into a transformer's residual stream and co-trained with a low-rank adapter... writes them back through a controlled residual update.
closest.why: Same placement (low-rank residual-stream writeback path) but trained via standard SFT, not an online per-token TTT loss updating the adapter causally at test time.

survives: The specific mechanism of taking one causal, per-token gradient step on a low-rank residual-write adapter using a masked/noised reconstruction loss to adaptively expand/contract write-width at inference (rather than a fixed, offline-trained or merely selected/interpolated correction) is not demonstrated by any of these; a paper combining TTT's per-token online update rule with LARA/TALAN's residual-stream low-rank write target would still be new.

closest.title: Rethinking Addressing in Language Models via Contexualized Equivariant Positional Encoding
closest.evidence: TAPE introduces dynamic, context-aware positional encodings, overcoming the constraints of traditional fixed patterns... incorporating sequence content across layers
closest.why: TAPE also makes positional codes content-conditioned and updated dynamically rather than a fixed function of index, though via layer-wise contextualization rather than an explicit delta-rule erase-then-write memory.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: we propose a Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding (DAPE) method, which dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors
closest.why: Same capability goal (content-adaptive position codes) but achieved through a data-adaptive adjustment mechanism, not an associative delta-rule overwrite memory.

closest.title: MapFormer: Self-Supervised Learning of Cognitive Maps with Input-Dependent Positional Embeddings
closest.evidence: disentangling structural relationships in the inputs from their specific content, a property that can be achieved by updating position encodings with input-dependent matrices
closest.why: Also rewrites/updates position representations conditioned on content to detect structural boundaries, though via Lie-algebra matrix updates rather than delta-rule associative memory.

survives: The specific mechanism of a delta-rule (erase-then-write) associative memory keyed by content hash, explicitly borrowed from DeltaNet's linear-attention state-update math and applied as an overwritable per-sequence positional memory (vs. TAPE/DAPE/MapFormer's layer-contextualization, learned biases, or Lie-algebra transforms), is a distinct enough mechanism-object pairing to remain novel if the delta-rule's specific erase-then-write algebra and capacity properties are shown to matter for the boundary-collapsing behavior claimed.

closest.evidence: we introduce Selective RoPE, an input-dependent rotary embedding mechanism, that generalizes RoPE, and enables rotation in arbitrary angles for both linear and softmax transformers
closest.why: Same target (RoPE/position code made input-dependent so it adapts within a sequence to recently seen content) though via gating/rotation-angle selection rather than a Hebbian outer-product fast-weight buffer.

closest.title: Adaptive Memory Decay for Log-Linear Attention
closest.evidence: We propose learning λ directly from the input via a lightweight two-layer MLP, producing per-token, per-level decay that adapts to content rather than position.
closest.why: Introduces content-dependent decay into a fast-weight-like hierarchical memory, close in spirit to the trained lambda/eta decay scalars but applied to attention memory levels, not the positional code itself.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: Recurrent fast-weight memories ... compress an expanding context into a fixed-size recurrent state, making the state transition an online learning rule
closest.why: Generic fast-weight outer-product update mechanism (the core Hebbian mechanism) but applied to content/key-value association, not to biasing the positional encoding channel.

survives: The specific twist of routing the Hebbian fast-weight outer-product update to bias the positional/RoPE channel itself (rather than content KV association or decay-gating of attention), enabling within-sequence adaptive position codes for repeated templates, is not directly shown in these papers and could still be novel if demonstrated to matter empirically.

closest.title: Bayesian Attention Mechanism: A Probabilistic Framework for Positional Encoding and Context Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: We propose the Bayesian Attention Mechanism (BAM), a theoretical framework that formulates positional encoding as a prior within a probabilistic model... motivates a new Generalized Gaussian positional prior that substantially improves long-context generalization.
closest.why: Same component (positional encoding) and same purpose (Bayesian probabilistic treatment for length extrapolation), but BAM uses a single learned prior distribution rather than an explicit online mixture over multiple discrete RoPE base hypotheses with calibrated per-hypothesis likelihood weights.

closest.title: PSC: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Phase Shift Calibration
closest.evidence: we introduce PSC (Phase Shift Calibration), a small module for calibrating the frequencies predefined by existing methods... many existing methods can be further enhanced, like PI, YaRN, and LongRoPE.
closest.why: Also calibrates/rescales RoPE base frequencies for context extension, but via a learned correction module rather than a Bayesian mixture of multiple bases weighted by held-out likelihood.

closest.title: CLEX: Continuous Length Extrapolation for Large Language Models
closest.evidence: We generalise the PE scaling approaches to model the continuous dynamics by ordinary differential equations over the length scaling factor, thereby overcoming the constraints of current PE scaling methods designed for specific lengths.
closest.why: Also addresses smooth adaptation of RoPE scaling factor as length grows past training length, but via continuous ODE dynamics rather than discrete multi-hypothesis Bayesian mixture with online-updated calibration weights.

survives: The specific mechanism of maintaining K parallel RoPE-base hypotheses and mixing their attention outputs/logits via an online exponentially-decayed calibration-buffer likelihood (explicit Bayesian model averaging over discrete rotary bases, not a single learned prior or continuous scaling function) is not directly implemented in any of these papers, so a demonstration of smooth, predictable mixture-weight shift and non-catastrophic collapse could still be a genuine contribution.

closest.title: Bayesian Attention Mechanism: A Probabilistic Framework for Positional Encoding and Context Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: We propose the Bayesian Attention Mechanism (BAM), a theoretical framework that formulates positional encoding as a prior within a probabilistic model... a new Generalized Gaussian positional prior that substantially improves long-context generalization.
closest.why: Places a probabilistic (Gaussian-family) distribution over position directly in the attention/positional-encoding component to improve length extrapolation, closely matching the mixture-density-over-position idea, though without an explicit mixture-of-Gaussians or an exposed confidence-gated fallback mechanism.

closest.title: Position as Probability: Self-Supervised Transformers that Think Past Their Training for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: PRISM learns continuous relative positions through a differentiable histogram-filter update, preserving position uncertainty via a probabilistic superposition rather than conventional deterministic embeddings.
closest.why: Explicitly replaces deterministic positional embeddings with a distribution/uncertainty-preserving representation for length extrapolation, the same capability target as the proposal.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: we propose a Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding (DAPE) method, which dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors.
closest.why: Also modifies the positional-encoding computation adaptively to improve length generalization, though via context-adaptivity rather than an explicit mixture-density/uncertainty read-out gate.

survives: The specific twist of using an explicit K-component Gaussian mixture-density head trained with NLL loss to expose a per-token variance-derived confidence scalar that gates interpolation between position-aware and position-agnostic (mean-pooled) attention is not demonstrated in these closest papers, which either use a single Gaussian-family prior (BAM) or a histogram/superposition representation (PRISM) without a learned downstream gating mechanism consuming calibrated uncertainty.

closest.title: MergeDNA: Context-aware Genome Modeling with Dynamic Tokenization through Token Merging
closest.evidence: the tokenization module automatically chunks adjacent bases into words by stacking multiple layers of the differentiable token merging blocks with local-window constraints... jointly optimizes a dynamic genomic tokenizer and latent Transformers
closest.why: This builds a hierarchical, jointly-trained dynamic tokenizer that merges adjacent base tokens using learned criteria, closely matching the proposal's block-pooling and joint training but without an explicit RG/mutual-information-survival framing or multi-level pyramid feeding different layers.

closest.title: zip2zip: Inference-Time Adaptive Tokenization via Online Compression
closest.evidence: dynamically expands its active vocabulary at inference time by continuously replacing fragmented token sequences with more compact hypertokens
closest.why: Shares the goal of a non-fixed, adaptive granularity tokenizer replacing a static merge table, though via LZW compression rather than RG-style mutual-information thresholding.

closest.title: LLM Vocabulary Compression for Low-Compute Environments
closest.evidence: grouping tokens based on Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) merges, we prevent materialization of the memory-intensive logits tensor
closest.why: Also groups tokens hierarchically for efficiency but targets the output layer, not a multi-scale input pyramid tied to information survival.

survives: The explicit RG framing—iteratively testing which mutual information with the target survives block-averaging via a probe classifier, and feeding different survival levels to different transformer depths—is a more principled and information-theoretically justified selection criterion than MergeDNA's differentiable merging or zip2zip's compression heuristic, so a version that rigorously operationalizes the RG coarse-graining/rescaling equivalence (not just adaptive merging) could still be new.

closest.evidence: introduce joint multi-token prediction (JTP), a lightweight modification of standard next-token prediction designed to enrich hidden state representations by jointly predicting multiple future tokens

closest.title: AdaMTP: An Adaptive Training Paradigm for Multi-Token Prediction

closest.title: Multi-Token Residual Prediction
closest.evidence: MRP exploits a key property of the denoising process: the logit distributions at adjacent denoising steps are remarkably similar... predicts the residual between steps from the backbone's hidden states

survives: The mixture-density parameterization (multiple weighted components per horizon capturing genuine multi-modal, calibrated uncertainty, verified against actual NLL) rather than a single point/categorical prediction per horizon is not demonstrated in any of the closest papers, so a proposal specifically validating calibrated multi-modal uncertainty via MDN heads at each horizon would still be new.

closest.title: Control Barrier Function for Aligning Large Language Models
closest.evidence: The presented framework applies the CBF safety filter to the predicted token generated from the baseline LLM, to intervene in the generated text... this safety filter is an add-on type, allowing it to be used for alignment purposes without fine-tuning the baseline LLM
closest.why: This applies a CBF safety filter directly at the LLM sampler to intervene on the token distribution for safe generation, the same component and mechanism as the proposal.

closest.title: Safety-Guided Flow (SGF): A Unified Framework for Negative Guidance in Safe Generation
closest.evidence: we leverage control-barrier functions analysis to justify the existence of a critical time window in which negative guidance must be strong; outside of this window, the guidance should decay to zero
closest.why: Uses CBF-based analysis to guide denoising/generation steps to avoid unsafe regions, closely analogous mechanism though applied to diffusion/flow generation rather than autoregressive token sampling.

closest.title: Detect-and-Guide: Self-regulation of Diffusion Models for Safe Text-to-Image Generation via Guideline Token Optimization
closest.evidence: DAG first detects harmful concepts from noisy latents... then applies safety guidance with adaptive strength and editing regions to negate unsafe generation
closest.why: Similar in-generation-loop safety steering without post-hoc rollback, but for diffusion image generation rather than LLM token sampling.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—learning a scalar barrier function on LLM hidden states and solving a per-step QP projection over the top-m token simplex with a formal CBF non-decreasing constraint (rather than a generic 'safety filter' or negative-guidance heuristic)—could still be novel if it demonstrates provable forward-invariance guarantees at the token level that 2511.03121 does not formalize.

closest.why: Uses SMC/importance-weighted resampling at the sampler over blocks of tokens to correct a modified (reward-tempered) proposal back toward a target distribution, the same mechanism-at-component structure proposed here, though for reward-guidance rather than per-position speed/exactness tradeoff.

closest.title: FlashSampling: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Sampling

survives: The genuinely new part would be the periodic self-normalized-importance-sampling buffer resampling specifically calibrated to correct drift from an aggressively varying per-position top-k/temperature proposal with a stored per-token receipt log for on-demand exact recovery, rather than reward-guided steering or a single global exactness kernel — but this is a narrow procedural twist on an established SMC-for-decoding pattern.

closest.evidence: a small auxiliary model is used to process the prompt and produce an approximation of the KV cache used by a base model. This approximated KV cache is then used with the base model for autoregressive generation without the need to query the auxiliary model again
closest.why: this is the same mechanism (a small predictor approximating the full-depth KV cache from a shallow pass to cut TTFT) but it never corrects/overwrites the approximation with the real deep pass before subsequent tokens, whereas the proposal's core twist is the background reconciliation.

closest.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Dynamic Early-Exit Process for Transformers
closest.evidence: enable dynamic early exit in both the prefill and generation phases... ADEPT further enhances KV generation procedure by decoupling sequential dependencies in skipped layers, making token-level early exit more practical
closest.why: early-exit skipping layers during prefill to speed token emission overlaps with the proposal's shallow-pass-for-token-1 idea, though it doesn't frame this as a background 'retroactive' correction of predicted KV.

closest.title: Fast Forward: Accelerating LLM Prefill with Predictive FFN Sparsity
closest.evidence: a lightweight expert predictor to select high-importance neurons per block... substantially reducing Time-to-Front-Token (TTFT)
closest.why: uses a lightweight predictor at prefill time to approximate deep computation for TTFT reduction, similar placement/purpose but targeting FFN sparsity rather than KV entries directly.

survives: The specific claim that the predicted KV is provisional and gets silently overwritten in-place by the real background deep pass before token 2 (a true speculative/retroactive reconciliation rather than a permanent approximation as in KV Prediction) is the one twist not clearly covered, though it is a narrow delta.

closest.title: Beyond Self Attention: A Subquadratic Fourier Wavelet Transformer with Multi Modal Fusion
closest.evidence: We revisit the use of spectral techniques to replaces the attention mechanism in Transformers through Fourier Transform based token mixing... introduce a novel MultiDomain Fourier Wavelet Attention(MDFWA)... detailed mathematical formulations of Fourier mixing and causal masking... sub quadratic time and memory cost
closest.why: Replaces attention with causal-masked Fourier/wavelet token mixing for global+local dependencies, the same mechanism-at-component idea as spectral prefill attention.

closest.title: From Attention to Atoms: Spectral Dictionary Learning for Fast, Interpretable Language Models
closest.evidence: jointly learns a global time varying Fourier dictionary and per token mixing coefficients, replacing the ubiquitous self attention mechanism in transformer architectures... operates with linear complexity
closest.why: Also swaps self-attention for a spectral/dictionary token-mixing transform at linear-ish cost, closely matching the proposed truncated spectral mixer.

closest.title: Cross-Family Speculative Prefill: Training-Free Long-Context Compression with Small Draft Models
closest.evidence: Prompt length is a major bottleneck... attention-based token importance estimation can enable training-free prompt compression
closest.why: Targets the same prefill-cost problem but via token pruning rather than a spectral transform, showing the capability space is being addressed by other mechanisms.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—causal/prefix-only FFT restricted to long-range mixing while explicitly retaining separate sink/local attention lanes for near-token precision, trained jointly at matched parameter count in a 'nano' LLM setting—is not demonstrated in these general spectral-replaces-attention papers, but the core mechanism (causal-masked Fourier token mixing replacing attention for long-range dependencies) is already claimed by MDFWA and the spectral dictionary paper.

closest.title: Speculative Decoding via Early-exiting for Faster LLM Inference with Thompson Sampling Control Mechanism
closest.evidence: we introduce a novel sampling mechanism that leverages Thompson Sampling to regulate the generation processes, automatically determining the quantity of draft tokens in each round
closest.why: Uses Thompson sampling to control an early-exit-style depth/draft-length decision in LLM inference, but the arm is 'how many draft tokens to generate' for speculative decoding, not per-token exit-layer selection via a posterior over per-layer stopping value.

closest.title: Beyond Greedy Exits: Improved Early Exit Decisions for Risk Control and Reliability
closest.evidence: UAT that adapts the threshold for exit decisions using a Multi-Armed Bandit framework, enabling online, unsupervised adjustment of exit decisions
closest.why: Applies a bandit framework to adapt early-exit thresholds online per sample, the same capability (online adaptive exit-depth) at the same component (layer-schedule), though via threshold-adaptation rather than explicit per-arm Thompson posteriors over each candidate exit layer.

closest.title: Sample-based Dynamic Hierarchical Transformer with Layer and Head Flexibility via Contextual Bandit
closest.evidence: we deploy combinatorial Thompson Sampling in order to select specific head combinations given their number
closest.why: Uses Thompson sampling for per-sample dynamic depth/head configuration in transformers, closely matching the mechanism-component pairing though targeting layer+head count jointly rather than pure per-token exit-layer arms.

survives: A twist could survive if the proposal's per-arm Beta/Normal posteriors over each individual candidate exit-layer (rather than a single adaptive threshold or joint layer-head bandit) and its budget-adjusted sampled-value stopping rule yield materially different exploration dynamics or provable regret/accuracy-per-FLOP guarantees not shown in UAT or EESD, but on mechanism-component-purpose grounds it is very close to existing bandit-controlled early-exit work.

closest.title: Towards A Unified View of Sparse Feed-Forward Network in Pretraining Large Language Model
closest.evidence: Large and sparse feed-forward layers (S-FFN) such as Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) have proven effective in scaling up Transformers model size for pretraining large language models. By only activating part of the FFN parameters conditioning on input, S-FFN improves generalization performance while keeping training and inference costs (in FLOPs) fixed.
closest.why: This directly frames sparse activation of FFN memory blocks to scale parameter/key count at fixed FLOPs, the same core capability claimed by the proposal, though via MoE/block-selection rather than a sparse-coding dictionary encoder.

closest.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
closest.evidence: we show that feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary.
closest.why: Establishes the FFN-as-key-value-memory framing that the proposal's dictionary/atoms formalism builds on, but does not introduce sparse-coding-based scaling of key count.

closest.title: OmniMoE: An Efficient MoE by Orchestrating Atomic Experts at Scale
closest.evidence: OmniMoE introduces vector-level Atomic Experts, enabling scalable routing and execution within a single MoE layer... pushes expert granularity to its logical extreme.
closest.why: Scales an FFN-like memory to very fine-grained units with sparse activation and constant compute, functionally close to a huge dictionary of atoms selected sparsely, though framed as MoE routing rather than matching-pursuit/ISTA sparse coding.

survives: The specific mechanism of an explicit reconstruction-driven sparse code (top-k matching pursuit or ISTA-unrolled encoder optimizing a reconstruction objective over a dictionary, rather than a learned router/gating network selecting discrete experts) is a genuine mechanistic difference from MoE/PKM-style routing and is not directly instantiated in the cited S-FFN or MoE works, so a rigorous head-to-head comparing sparse-coding-based key selection against routing-based selection at matched FLOPs and matched dictionary/atom scale would still be new.

closest.title: LookupFFN: Making Transformers Compute-lite for CPU inference
closest.evidence: we propose an alternative formulation (we call it LookupFFN) to GEMM based FFNs inspired by the recent studies of using Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to approximate FFNs. Our formulation recasts most essential operations as a memory look-up
closest.why: This applies LSH directly to the FFN memory to restrict computation/lookup to hashed buckets instead of scoring all keys, the same component and same purpose (sub-linear FFN key scoring) as the proposal.

survives: Only a genuinely different twist (e.g. learned multi-probe hashing jointly optimized end-to-end with a straight-through estimator shown to preserve quality at scale, or theoretical guarantees on bucket collision for arbitrary key growth) would be new, since LookupFFN already establishes LSH-bucketed FFN key lookup as the mechanism for scaling FFN keys sub-linearly.

closest.title: Dynamic Learning Rate for Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Bandit Approach
closest.evidence: We introduce LRRL, a meta-learning approach that dynamically selects the learning rate based on policy performance rather than training steps. LRRL adaptively favors rates that improve returns, remaining robust even when the candidate set includes values that individually cause divergence.
closest.why: This places a bandit over a discrete candidate set of learning rates, selecting based on observed reward (performance improvement) to adaptively reallocate away from a fixed schedule, exactly the proposed mechanism and purpose.

closest.title: Learning Rate-Free Reinforcement Learning: A Case for Model Selection with Non-Stationary Objectives
closest.evidence: We present a model selection framework for Learning Rate-Free Reinforcement Learning that employs model selection methods to select the optimal learning rate on the fly... solely uses the reward feedback to select the learning rate.
closest.why: Same component (LR schedule) and same capability (online reward-driven LR selection replacing fixed schedule), evaluating bandit algorithms among model-selection strategies.

closest.title: Dynamic Learning Rate Scheduling based on Loss Changes Leads to Faster Convergence
closest.evidence: GreedyLR, a novel scheduler that adaptively adjusts the learning rate during training based on the current loss.
closest.why: Same purpose of adaptively reallocating LR based on observed loss improvement rather than a fixed curve, though not explicitly Thompson sampling.

survives: Only a genuinely new twist—such as a formal Beta/Normal-Gamma Thompson-sampling posterior update proven to outperform the epsilon-greedy/model-selection LRRL approach, or a specific theoretical regret guarantee tailored to LR-bandit non-stationarity—would be new, but the core capability (bandit-selected LR reward-driven adaptive reallocation replacing fixed schedule) is already covered by LRRL.

survives: Only a genuinely different twist—e.g. proving mixture-density heads scale favorably at LLM vocabulary size/hidden-width tradeoffs, or a new theoretical link between component collapse and calibration guarantees—would be new; applying MDN heads to next-token prediction itself is a straightforward reapplication of Bishop's MDN mechanism already used for the same aleatoric-multimodality purpose in autoregressive/sequential settings.

closest.title: AgentKVShift: Efficient KV Cache Reuse for Agentic Memory Systems
closest.evidence: a training-free, probe-guided KV residual correction method that operates per retrieved memory unit ... AgentKVShift also corrects the tokens it does not recompute, turning the refresh budget into useful signal across the entire chunk
closest.why: Same object (in-place correction of stale cache entries via a learned offset) and same purpose (detect/correct drift), differing mainly in being training-free and using a residual offset rather than an ECC syndrome/parity check.

closest.title: Polestar: Drift-Aware Cache Calibration and Token Commitment for Efficient Inference of Diffusion LLMs
closest.evidence: Polestar-Cache, which identifies stale KV-cache positions via drift and performs sparse KV-cache refreshes to enable efficient reuse
closest.why: Also detects which specific cache entries are stale (via a drift signal) and selectively refreshes only those, mirroring the syndrome-triggered selective repair capability.

closest.title: CONDUIT: A Unified Residual-Stream Restoration Framework for KV Cache Reuse in Vision-Language Models
closest.evidence: Selective recomputation can recover quality under a small visual-token budget, but only when the right stale tokens are refreshed ... ranks cached visual tokens using cached-key query attention
closest.why: Also selectively identifies and restores stale cache entries rather than uniformly rewriting the whole cache.

survives: The specific mechanism of a fixed linear parity/checksum code with an explicit syndrome magnitude as a corruption signal (versus drift/attention/residual heuristics) and its logged auditability could be a genuine twist, but the capability of selective, syndrome/drift-triggered cache repair is already established by these training-free and training-based drift-detection methods.

closest.title: DiSK: Differentially Private Optimizer with Simplified Kalman Filter for Noise Reduction
closest.evidence: DiSK employs Kalman filtering, a technique drawn from control and signal processing, to effectively denoise privatized gradients and generate progressively refined gradient estimations... We simplify the Kalman filtering process, minimizing its memory and computational demands.
closest.why: This directly applies a simplified per-parameter Kalman filter to fuse a running gradient estimate with the noisy minibatch gradient to reduce effective gradient noise during training, the same component and same capability as proposed.

closest.title: EVPO: Explained Variance Policy Optimization for Adaptive Critic Utilization in LLM Post-Training
closest.evidence: By casting baseline selection as a Kalman filtering problem, we unify PPO and GRPO as two extremes of the Kalman gain and prove that explained variance (EV)... identifies the exact boundary: positive EV indicates the critic reduces variance, while zero or negative EV signals that it inflates variance.
closest.why: Uses Kalman-gain framing to fuse a model-based prediction (critic) with a noisy measurement (batch-mean advantage) to reduce variance in the gradient/update signal, closely analogous but applied to RL advantage estimation rather than raw gradients.

closest.title: Online Natural Gradient as a Kalman Filter
closest.evidence: applying an extended Kalman filter to estimate a fixed unknown parameter of a probabilistic model from a series of observations, is rigorously equivalent to estimating this parameter via an online stochastic natural gradient descent
closest.why: Establishes the theoretical equivalence of Kalman filtering to gradient-based parameter estimation, underpinning the mechanism the proposal reuses, though framed as natural gradient rather than explicit noise-fusion at the raw gradient step.

survives: DiSK already implements a simplified per-parameter Kalman filter fusing a running gradient prediction with fresh noisy gradient measurements (via clipped/noised gradients) to reduce effective noise with a trackable covariance state, which is essentially the same mechanism, component, and purpose as the proposal; the only distinguishing detail is DiSK's differential-privacy motivation versus this proposal's plain optimizer noise-reduction motivation, which is not a substantive twist.

closest.title: Improving Generative Adversarial Networks with Self-Distillation
closest.evidence: we introduce Self-Distilled GAN (SD-GAN) that employs the EMA generator as a teacher to guide the active generator (student) via perceptual loss
closest.why: This is exactly the proposal's mechanism: an EMA copy of the weights updated continuously, used every step as a teacher for the live model via a distillation loss, with the EMA never checkpointed separately but computed on the fly during training.

closest.title: FedEMA-Distill: Exponential Moving Average Guided Knowledge Distillation for Robust Federated Learning
closest.evidence: a server-side procedure that combines an exponential moving average (EMA) of the global model with ensemble knowledge distillation from client-uploaded prediction logits
closest.why: Also uses a continuously updated EMA copy as a distillation teacher against the live model, the same placement/mechanism though in federated learning.

closest.title: Temporal Self-Ensembling Teacher for Semi-Supervised Object Detection
closest.evidence: our teacher model ensembles its temporal model weights with the student model weights by an exponential moving average (EMA) which allows the teacher gradually learn from the student
closest.why: Same EMA-teacher-as-continuous-distillation-signal mechanism applied at every step rather than at checkpoint boundaries.

survives: Nothing distinguishes the proposal from SD-GAN's mechanism except domain (language/general models vs GANs); a genuinely new twist would need a different placement or a capability EMA-self-distillation doesn't already give, such as explicitly compressing multiple discarded intermediate checkpoints' trajectory information beyond what a single EMA can encode.

closest.title: Inshrinkerator: Compressing Deep Learning Training Checkpoints via Dynamic Quantization
closest.evidence: a non-uniform quantization scheme... a quantization-aware delta compression mechanism that rearranges weights to minimize checkpoint differences, thereby maximizing compression
closest.why: same purpose (cheap storage of frequent intermediate weight snapshots via quantization for later recovery) but uses per-weight non-uniform/delta quantization rather than product-quantisation codebooks over subspaces.

closest.title: BitSnap: Checkpoint Sparsification and Quantization in LLM Training
closest.evidence: the cluster-based quantization method achieves 2x compression ratio with little precision loss
closest.why: cluster-based (i.e., codebook/k-means-like) quantization of checkpoints is essentially the same mechanism (vector quantization) applied to the same object (training checkpoints) for the same compression goal.

closest.title: On Efficient Constructions of Checkpoints
closest.evidence: LC-Checkpoint uses quantization and priority promotion to store the most crucial information for SGD to recover
closest.why: also applies quantization to intermediate training checkpoints to enable cheap storage and recovery of trajectory states, though not framed as PQ with per-subspace codebooks.

survives: The specific twist of per-layer-block product quantisation with online k-means-trained codebooks refreshed only at checkpoint intervals, enabling much finer-grained (every N<<checkpoint-interval steps) trajectory reconstruction than these delta/cluster-based approaches, could still be new if it demonstrably operates at a much higher temporal resolution than prior cluster-based or delta-quantization checkpoint compressors.

closest.title: Diachronic Sample Integration: Robust Tail-Risk Estimation with Generative Models
closest.evidence: DSI, a test-time inference framework that ensembles generated samples across checkpoints from a stochastic training trajectory. DSI targets a checkpoint-mixture distribution that averages checkpoint-specific tail fluctuations rather than relying on a single brittle endpoint.
closest.why: Mixes outputs from multiple training-trajectory checkpoints at inference to get an ensemble-like uncertainty/robustness signal without extra models, matching the proposal's core mechanism and purpose.

closest.title: Uncertainty-Driven Reliability: Selective Prediction and Trustworthy Deployment in Modern Machine Learning
closest.evidence: a model's training trajectory contains rich uncertainty signals that can be exploited without altering its architecture or loss. By ensembling predictions from intermediate checkpoints, we propose a lightweight, post-hoc abstention method
closest.why: Same purpose (uncertainty signal from checkpoint trajectory ensembling at inference, post-hoc, cheap) as the proposal's blending of nearby checkpoints.

closest.title: Recycling Scraps: Improving Private Learning by Leveraging Intermediate Checkpoints
closest.evidence: the sample variance from last few checkpoints provides a good approximation of the variance of the final model of a DP run.
closest.why: Uses intermediate checkpoints aggregated to both improve accuracy and estimate predictive variance/uncertainty, overlapping with the proposal's placement and purpose.

survives: The specific retrieval-based kNN selection of nearby checkpoints via learned sketch-distance (rather than fixed windows or all-checkpoint aggregation) is a minor implementation variant, not a new capability beyond what DSI and the trajectory-ensembling uncertainty work already deliver.
