closest.title: Efficient Knowledge Distillation from Model Checkpoints
closest.evidence: a weak snapshot ensemble of several intermediate models from a same training trajectory can outperform a strong ensemble of independently trained and fully converged models, when they are used as teachers
closest.why: Uses an ensemble of trajectory checkpoints as a KD teacher, closely matching the proposal's ensemble-of-recent-checkpoints consolidation loss, but as a one-off distillation into a separate student rather than a periodic offline replay-consolidation cycle that rewrites the next checkpoint itself.

closest.title: MyGO: Memory Yielding Generative Offline-consolidation for Lifelong Learning Systems
closest.evidence: During the "sleep" phase, the system enters an offline state, using all learned G-mem models to generate pseudo-data ("dreams") and consolidate new and old knowledge into a core feature extractor via knowledge distillation
closest.why: Explicit wake-sleep replay-consolidation via KD matches the mechanism and framing, but it targets continual-task forgetting rather than compressing a single trajectory's optimization window into periodic checkpoints.

closest.title: Phasor Agents: Oscillatory Graphs with Three-Factor Plasticity and Sleep-Staged Learning
closest.evidence: we separate wake tagging from offline consolidation, inspired by synaptic tagging-and-capture and sleep-stage dynamics: deep-sleep-like gated capture commits tagged changes safely, while REM-like replay reconstructs and perturbs experience for planning
closest.why: Same wake/sleep replay-consolidation framing applied to an oscillatory architecture for stability/planning, not to standard checkpointing during ordinary SGD training.

survives: The proposal's specific twist — periodically pausing ordinary (non-continual, single-task) training to replay the last N minibatches and KD-consolidate against an ensemble of the last few live checkpoints so each checkpoint itself summarizes a trajectory window, rather than solving catastrophic forgetting across tasks or producing a separate compressed student — is not demonstrated in these papers, though it is very close to checkpoint-ensemble KD and wake-sleep continual learning mechanisms.

closest.title: PQCache: Product Quantization-based KVCache for Long Context LLM Inference
closest.evidence: We propose PQCache, which employs Product Quantization (PQ) to manage KVCache... During the prefilling phase, we apply PQ to tokens' keys for each LLM layer and head... then fetch the corresponding key-value pairs for self-attention computation.
closest.why: Applies PQ per-layer/per-head to KV cache entries to extend effective context at fixed memory, exactly the proposal's mechanism and purpose.

closest.title: MILLION: Mastering Long-Context LLM Inference Via Outlier-Immunized KV Product Quantization
closest.evidence: we propose MILLION, a novel quantization framework achieving low-bitwidth KV cache through product quantization... comprehensive evaluation results demonstrate that MILLION can achieve 4 bits quantization with trivial perplexity and accuracy loss... at 32K context length.
closest.why: Same PQ-on-KV-cache mechanism aimed at enabling longer context at fixed memory.

closest.title: PolyKV: A Shared Asymmetrically-Compressed KV Cache Pool for Multi-Agent LLM Inference
closest.evidence: Keys are quantized at int8... while Values are compressed using TurboQuant MSE... keeping recent/full precision vs compressed older entries
closest.why: Mixed precision by recency/position with codebook-based compression of KV entries, matching the sliding-window exact-vs-quantized split described in the proposal.

survives: Only a genuinely different twist—such as training the PQ codebooks jointly with recency-aware eviction policy learned end-to-end, or provable guarantees on which positions are safe to compress—would be new; the core mechanism (per-layer/head PQ on KV cache with exact cache for recent tokens) is already established.

closest.title: Sparse Attention across Multiple-context KV Cache

closest.title: SALS: Sparse Attention in Latent Space for KV cache Compression

survives: Only a genuinely different twist (e.g., per-layer online K-SVD dictionary adaptation jointly trained with the base model, or theoretical guarantees on reconstruction fidelity vs. context length scaling) not already covered by Lexico's universal sparse-coding dictionary for KV cache would remain novel.

closest.title: FreqKV: Key-Value Compression in Frequency Domain for Context Window Extension
closest.evidence: Motivated by the observation in the frequency domain that the context information is concentrated in the low-frequency components, we propose FreqKV... It iteratively compresses the increasing KV cache in the frequency domain, allowing models to process lengthy contexts efficiently.
closest.why: Applies a spectral transform directly to evicted/growing KV cache entries, keeping low-frequency coefficients and discarding high-frequency ones, exactly the same mechanism and purpose as the proposal.

closest.title: FAEDKV: Infinite-Window Fourier Transform for Unbiased KV Cache Compression
closest.evidence: FAEDKV operates by transforming the KV cache into the frequency domain using a proposed Infinite-Window Fourier Transform (IWDFT)... A preliminary frequency ablation study identifies critical spectral components for layer-wise, targeted compression.
closest.why: Same placement (KV cache) and mechanism (Fourier transform, keep select frequency components) for the same capacity-preserving-under-compression goal.

closest.title: Beyond Homogeneous Attention: Memory-Efficient LLMs via Fourier-Approximated KV Cache
closest.evidence: By projecting the long-context-insensitive dimensions onto orthogonal Fourier bases, FourierAttention approximates their temporal evolution with fixed-length spectral coefficients.
closest.why: Also applies orthogonal spectral transform to KV cache dimensions to compress while preserving long-range dependency information, matching component and mechanism.

survives: Nothing distinguishes the proposal's DCT/learned-basis block-wise scheme applied specifically at sliding-window eviction boundary from FreqKV's iterative frequency-domain compression of the growing KV cache, which already keeps low-frequency coefficients and discards high-frequency detail for the same long-range-preservation purpose.

closest.title: Near-Lossless Model Compression Enables Longer Context Inference in DNA Large Language Models
closest.evidence: inserts summary tokens at k-mer granularity and progressively compresses attention key and value activations across multiple Transformer layers, retaining only the summary KV states across windows while discarding ordinary-token KV
closest.why: This performs the same operation (periodic replay/compression of old KV segments into fixed summary slots with originals discarded) on the same object (the KV cache) to extend effective context, though trained end-to-end online rather than via a distillation loss and applied to DNA sequences.

closest.title: EpMAN: Episodic Memory AttentioN for Generalizing to Longer Contexts
closest.evidence: processing long contexts in an episodic memory module while holistically attending to semantically relevant context chunks... reweigh the decoder's self-attention to the stored KV cache
closest.why: Also targets retaining gist-level long-range information beyond the live window via an auxiliary module operating on stored KV, but does not evict/replace raw KV with a compact consolidated trace at a fixed cadence.

closest.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Semantic Compression
closest.evidence: employs a pre-trained model to reduce the semantic redundancy of long inputs before passing them to the LLMs for downstream tasks
closest.why: Same purpose (extend effective context via compression of stale content) but compresses the input text/embeddings before the LLM rather than operating on live KV cache entries in place with periodic eviction.

survives: A genuinely new twist would need to show the periodic (every-k-token) offline consolidation with joint distillation-trained cross-attention pooling replacing raw KV in place is mechanistically distinct from FOCUS's progressive cross-layer summary-token compression—e.g. demonstrating that the specific replay+evict+distill loop yields properties (asynchronous 'sleep phase' scheduling, no architectural summary-token insertion) that FOCUS's continuous compression does not achieve.

closest.title: Locret: Enhancing Eviction in Long-Context LLM Inference with Trained Retaining Heads on Consumer-Grade Devices
closest.evidence: By evaluating the causal importance of KV cache units by learnable retaining heads, Locret enables precise eviction of cache units, facilitating efficient long-context inference.
closest.why: Uses a trained lightweight scorer over KV cache entries to decide eviction, same mechanism/purpose as the proposal's relevance probe, but applied uniformly rather than with generational age-partitioned sweep frequencies.

closest.title: PagedEviction: Structured Block-wise KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
closest.evidence: PagedEviction introduces an efficient block-wise eviction algorithm tailored for paged memory layouts.
closest.why: Introduces structured, block-partitioned eviction of the cache analogous to generation partitioning, but without differential sweep frequencies tied to age.

closest.title: RedKnot: Efficient Long-Context LLM Serving with Head-Aware KV Reuse and SegPagedAttention
closest.evidence: different heads exhibit different functional roles, attention distances, and runtime importance... a full KV cache is not always necessary for every head, token range, or serving scenario
closest.why: Proposes structured, heterogeneous management of cache segments by role/age-like criteria, though partitioned by head rather than by sweep-frequency generations.

survives: The specific twist of generation-indexed differential sweep frequency (checking gen0 every step, gen1 every 8, gen2 every 64, with promotion/eviction as an amortized GC schedule) to bound average per-step compute is not explicitly present in any single paper; most works either use a single-pass or per-step scorer (Locret, SAGE-KV) or structural/head partitioning (PagedEviction, RedKnot) but none combine age-based generations with exponentially decreasing re-evaluation frequency as an amortized cost mechanism.

closest.title: Recency/Frequency Adaptive KV Caching for Large Language Model Serving
closest.evidence: we integrate adaptive caching that dynamically allocates cache space between recently and frequently occurring KV blocks
closest.why: This is exactly ARC-style dynamic recency/frequency balancing applied to the KV cache to replace LRU eviction, the identical mechanism-object-purpose triple proposed.

closest.title: Fractional Decay KV-Cache: Ownership-Aware Memory Management for Improved Inference Relevancy in Dialog Systems
closest.evidence: maintains a dual-channel scoring mechanism for each cached KV pair: a cumulative attention channel that tracks aggregate importance (akin to H2O), and a recency-weighted relevance channel
closest.why: Also combines recency and frequency (attention-mass) tracking per KV entry to adaptively decide eviction, closely mirroring the dual-list ARC design.

closest.title: Lethe: Layer- and Time-Adaptive KV Cache Pruning for Reasoning-Intensive LLM Serving
closest.evidence: a Recency-Aware Selective Retention (RASR) mechanism... extends traditional recency-based heuristics by also considering token relevance derived from evolving attention patterns
closest.why: Adaptively balances recency and attention-derived importance for eviction decisions, overlapping with the recency/frequency blending goal.

survives: Only a literal implementation of ARC's ghost-list adaptive parameter-tuning mechanism (as opposed to a simpler two-score blend) could be distinct, but that is a minor algorithmic variant, not a new capability.

closest.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Token-Wise Adaptive Compression for KV Cache (DynaKV)
closest.evidence: the first method to dynamically allocate compression rates to individual tokens according to their semantic meaning... low-rank KV cache compression... post-training framework
closest.why: Same mechanism (learned low-rank compression applied per-token to KV cache with variable rank) at the same component (KV cache) for the same purpose (fit more effective context in fixed budget by compressing predictable/low-importance tokens more).

closest.title: Don't Waste Bits! Adaptive KV-Cache Quantization for Lightweight On-Device LLMs
closest.evidence: assigns bit-width proportional to token importance... extracts lightweight token-level features, including token frequency, quality score, attention variance, and entropy-based uncertainty, and feeds them into a compact data-driven controller
closest.why: Uses entropy/predictive-uncertainty signals computed per token to decide differential storage cost per KV position, matching the proposal's core placement mechanism, just with quantization bit-width instead of low-rank projection.

closest.title: Information-Aware KV Cache Compression for Long Reasoning (InfoKV)
closest.evidence: introduce Forward Influence... entropy-aware KV cache compression framework that incorporates information-theoretic signals... combines token-level predictive uncertainty with layer-wise representation evolution
closest.why: Also uses per-token predictive-entropy/uncertainty signal (available from the model's own next-token distribution) to determine differential KV cache treatment, matching the proposal's entropy-accounting placement rationale.

survives: Only the specific arithmetic-coding framing and joint training of a percentile threshold plus rank-r compressor via reconstruction/distillation loss might be a narrow implementation delta, but the core idea (measure per-token entropy/predictive-uncertainty for free during the forward pass, then allocate differential KV storage fidelity accordingly to extend effective context under fixed budget) is already realized by DynaKV, InfoKV, and the entropy-based quantization papers.

closest.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction via a Unified Information-Theoretic Objective
closest.evidence: we derive a closed-form mutual information objective that characterizes the effective information capacity of a retained KV cache subset ... replaces heuristic selection with a theoretically grounded mechanism that preserves the maximum predictive signal
closest.why: Applies an information-bottleneck/mutual-information objective directly to the KV cache to give per-position (capacity-aware, non-uniform) compression verified by information preservation rather than heuristics, matching the proposal's component, mechanism, and purpose.

closest.title: Bottlenecked Transformers: Periodic KV Cache Consolidation for Generalised Reasoning
closest.evidence: We do this through the lens of Information Bottleneck (IB) theory ... a Cache Processor, an auxiliary Transformer that performs periodic, non-causal, in-place KV rewrites
closest.why: Uses an IB-justified trained auxiliary module performing periodic in-place rewrites/compression of KV cache entries, the same mechanism-at-component pairing as the proposed bottleneck encoder/decoder at window boundaries.

closest.title: Recurrent Preference Memory for Efficient Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
closest.evidence: Analysis reveals that the Preference Memory functions as a denoising Information Bottleneck, effectively filtering interaction noise to capture robust long-term interests
closest.why: Also frames a trained compression memory replacing cache/history as an IB, giving variable-cost retention of predictive information, same underlying mechanism though different domain.

survives: Only a genuinely new twist—such as a formally derived rate-distortion bound tied to a provably optimal variable-bit-per-position allocation with guarantees beyond what CapKV's capacity-maximization or Bottlenecked Transformer's IB-justified rewrites already offer—could still be novel, but the core idea of IB-gated variable-cost KV compression is already staked out.

closest.title: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization

survives: The specific two-part MDL formalism—jointly optimizing code length of quantized KV entries plus the residual description length of held-out future-token prediction error via a trained Gumbel-softmax gate, yielding a provable per-position bit certificate—is not what any of these papers do; they use attention/mutual-information/energy heuristics or profiling rather than an explicit MDL two-part code with a residual/future-token proof term.

closest.evidence: episodic interactions are transformed into semantic facts and user insights, which are then progressively integrated through hierarchical coarse-graining, thresholded updates, and rescaling into a dynamically evolving user profile

closest.title: LaCache: Ladder-Shaped KV Caching for Efficient Long-Context Modeling of Large Language Models
closest.evidence: an iterative compaction mechanism that progressively compresses older caches, freeing up space for new tokens within a fixed cache size

closest.title: Artificial Hippocampus Networks for Efficient Long-Context Modeling

closest.why: same mechanism (learned recurrent compression of stale KV into fixed-size summary, trained via distillation with frozen base LM) for the same capability of fixed cache size over arbitrarily long history.

survives: Only the explicit dyadic multi-level scale hierarchy (many nested coarsening resolutions each with its own trainable map, rather than a single window/compression stage) could be a genuine twist, but RGMem already frames this as literal multi-scale RG coarse-graining and LaCache/AHN already implement the iterative block-merging and distillation-trained compression mechanism at the KV cache.

closest.title: Stochastic Sparse Attention for Memory-Bound Inference
closest.evidence: sparsifies value-cache access by sampling S << n_k indices from the post-softmax distribution and aggregates only those value rows. This yields an unbiased estimator of the post-softmax value aggregation ... stratified and systematic sampling to design variance-reduced, GPU-friendly variants
closest.why: This is exactly the proposal's mechanism: importance sampling over cached positions with self-normalized/unbiased correction to approximate full attention with a sparse subset, at the same component (KV cache attention) for the same purpose (cheap unbiased approximation of dense attention).

closest.title: Rethinking Attention with Performers
closest.evidence: Performers use a novel Fast Attention Via positive Orthogonal Random features approach (FAVOR+) ... unbiased or nearly-unbiased estimation of the attention matrix, uniform convergence and low estimation variance
closest.why: Also provides an unbiased sampling/estimator-based approximation of full softmax attention with reduced complexity, overlapping the same variance-reduction goal though via random features rather than adaptive proxy scores.

closest.title: PIS: Linking Importance Sampling and Attention Mechanisms for Efficient Prompt Compression
closest.evidence: we introduce Prompt Importance Sampling (PIS), a novel compression framework that dynamically compresses prompts by sampling important tokens based on the analysis of attention scores of hidden states
closest.why: Uses importance sampling driven by attention-derived relevance scores to select a subset of context tokens, closely paralleling the proposal's proxy-scored sampling of context positions, albeit framed as compression rather than an unbiased estimator.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need a trained proxy scorer jointly optimized via a variance-reduction objective to match exact dense attention (rather than post-softmax or random-feature sampling) and a frozen-base-model graft ablation, but SANTA already implements the core mechanism (importance sampling of cache entries with unbiased correction) at the same component for the same purpose, so this is largely taken.

closest.title: WaveFilter: Enhancing the Long-Context Capability of Diffusion LLMs via Wavelet-Guided KV Cache Filtering
closest.evidence: This framework innovatively introduces the wavelet transform for decomposition of long sequences to achieve precise identification of key tokens, based on which a sparse KV Cache is constructed to compute the final contextual representation.
closest.why: Applies wavelet decomposition directly to the KV cache along the sequence axis to enable longer effective context at fixed memory, the same component and purpose as the proposal.

closest.title: TreeKV: Smooth Key-Value Cache Compression with Tree Structures
closest.evidence: Our wavelet analysis reveals that as tokens approach the end of sequence, their contributions to generation gradually increase... Unlike most compression methods, TreeKV is applicable to both the generation and prefilling stages... allowing LLMs trained with short context window to generalize to longer window with a 16x cache reduction.
closest.why: Uses wavelet-motivated multiresolution/hierarchical structure over the KV cache to give variable effective cost per position (near tokens finer, distant coarser) for the same long-context-at-fixed-memory capability.

closest.title: Kwai Summary Attention Technical Report
closest.evidence: Maintaining a linear relationship between the KV cache and sequence length, but performing semantic-level compression through a specific ratio k... trades acceptable memory costs for complete, referential, and interpretable retention of long distant dependency.
closest.why: Also places coarser summarization on older/distant KV entries with trained projections to preserve long-range retention at fixed budget, matching the placement and purpose.

survives: A genuinely new angle would require showing the fixed multiresolution wavelet basis (versus learned/attention-guided pooling) yields provably better reconstruction fidelity or a formally derived error bound per scale that these heuristic hierarchical/summary methods lack, but as stated the mechanism-component-purpose triple is already covered.

closest.title: Tensor Cache: Eviction-conditioned Associative Memory for Transformers
closest.evidence: a two-level cache that pairs sliding-window softmax attention as a first-level cache (L1) with a fixed-size outer-product fast-weight memory as a second-level cache (L2) fed by KV pairs evicted from the window ... per-head decay and write-rate parameters are trained end-to-end
closest.why: This is exactly the proposal's architecture: fixed-size decayed outer-product fast-weight matrix running alongside a shortened sliding-window exact-attention lane, jointly trained, to give variable effective retention beyond the hard window without discarding tokens.

closest.title: Fast-weight Product Key Memory
closest.evidence: FwPKM updates sparsely activated parameters at both training and inference time using chunk-level gradient descent on a local memory-rewrite objective ... enabling rapid memorization and retrieval of many new key-value associations while keeping per-token compute low and fixed
closest.why: Also places a fixed-size associative fast-weight store alongside standard attention to extend effective context beyond the window, though via sparse product-key updates rather than dense outer-product decay.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: Recurrent fast-weight memories and selective state-space models compress an expanding context into a fixed-size recurrent state, making the state transition an online learning rule ... together with numerically stable positive-decay renormalization
closest.why: Formalizes the same decayed outer-product fast-weight update rule for compressing context into a fixed-size state, the same mechanism/purpose as the proposal.

survives: Tensor Cache already implements the identical mechanism (decayed outer-product fast-weight matrix A, read via matrix-vector product, added to sliding-window attention, jointly trained end-to-end) for the identical purpose of freeing capacity beyond the window while retaining low-contribution-token decay; the proposal would need a genuinely different twist (e.g. a provably different decay/read rule with distinct guarantees) to survive, which is not stated.

closest.title: PolyKV: A Shared Asymmetrically-Compressed KV Cache Pool for Multi-Agent LLM Inference
closest.evidence: multiple concurrent inference agents share a single, asymmetrically compressed KV cache pool. Rather than allocating a separate KV cache per agent -- the standard paradigm -- PolyKV writes a compressed cache once and injects it into N independent agent contexts
closest.why: This directly implements a shared compressed KV cache pool across concurrent requests/agents at fixed memory to serve more agents, the same serving-batch-level deduplication capability the proposal claims as new.

closest.title: TokenDance: Scaling Multi-Agent LLM Serving via Collective KV Cache Sharing
closest.evidence: TokenDance scales the number of concurrent agents by exploiting the All-Gather pattern for collective KV Cache sharing... achieving 11-17x compression... supports up to 2.7x more concurrent agents than vLLM with prefix caching
closest.why: Same purpose (more concurrent requests at fixed memory via cross-request cache sharing) though via diff-based storage rather than PQ codebooks.

closest.title: AQPIM: Breaking the PIM Capacity Wall for LLMs with In-Memory Activation Quantization
closest.evidence: We explore clustering-based vector quantization approaches... AQPIM, a novel PIM-aware activation quantization framework based on Product Quantization (PQ)
closest.why: Applies PQ to KV/activation cache for memory reduction, though at the PIM hardware level rather than explicitly for cross-request batch sharing.

survives: A twist emphasizing online k-means codebook updates shared across the batch specifically to deduplicate near-identical subvectors across different requests' prefixes (not just one compressed copy injected into many contexts) with an exact recency buffer could differ, but PolyKV already establishes the shared-compressed-pool-for-concurrency capability, making this a follow-up rather than new.

closest.title: KVCOMM: Online Cross-context KV-cache Communication for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
closest.evidence: KVCOMM estimates and adjusts KV-caches for shared content by referencing a pool of cached examples-termed anchors-that store observed cache deviations under varying prefixes. The anchor pool is maintained and updated online, allowing dynamic adaptation to distinct user requests and context structures.
closest.why: Both maintain a dynamically updated cross-request memory bank that a new request's cache computation queries/associates against to reuse others' K/V, closely matching the batch-level associative bank idea, though via anchor-offset correction rather than Hopfield energy-descent retrieval.

closest.title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
closest.evidence: CacheBlend, a scheme that reuses the precomputed KV caches, regardless prefix or not, and selectively recomputes the KV values of a small subset of tokens to partially update each reused KV cache.
closest.why: Same purpose (cross-request KV reuse for overlapping non-prefix context reducing redundant compute) but mechanism is selective recomputation/fusion rather than Hopfield associative retrieval added as extra attention slots.

closest.title: SparseX: Efficient Segment-Level KV Cache Sharing for Interleaved LLM Serving
closest.evidence: SparseX uses contiguous token segments as reuse units and exploits Sparse-Q indices that naturally arise in KV Cache reuse workloads to estimate the key tokens that require correction... restoring cross-segment contextual interactions under complex interleaved reuse patterns
closest.why: Also retrieves/corrects shared KV segments across requests at attention time to enable cross-request reuse, similar capability via a query-driven correction rather than an explicit trained associative-memory energy-descent bank.

survives: A genuinely new twist would be the explicit modern-Hopfield energy-descent update rule (trained offline) operating over a rebuilt per-batch associative memory of K/V blocks as literal extra attention slots, rather than anchor-offset correction, selective recomputation, or Sparse-Q segment correction, plus demonstrating this energy-descent retrieval yields materially different reuse/robustness properties than the nearest correction-based systems.

closest.title: CoDec: Prefix-Shared Decoding Kernel for LLMs
closest.evidence: we propose a dedicated attention kernel to combine the memory access of shared prefixes in the decoding stage, namely CoDec... optimizes memory hierarchy and exploits both intra-block and inter-block parallelism
closest.why: this builds a specialized fused kernel triggered by detected shared prefixes across batched requests, which is the same mechanism (compute-graph specialization keyed on cross-request prefix sharing) at the same component (serving-batch attention/decoding), though it is a static kernel design rather than an online JIT triggered by rolling-window statistics.

closest.title: PAT: Accelerating LLM Decoding via Prefix-Aware Attention with Resource Efficient Multi-Tile Kernel
closest.evidence: PAT packs queries by shared prefix to reduce repeated memory accesses, runs a customized multi-tile kernel to achieve high resource efficiency
closest.why: also fuses/specializes decode kernels around detected shared prefixes across concurrently batched requests, directly overlapping with the proposal's core mechanism and component.

closest.title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference
closest.evidence: prefix-aware schedulers... rely on radix-tree traversals... Feather, a prefix-aware scheduler that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn the optimal tradeoff between batch size and prefix homogeneity
closest.why: detects prefix-sharing statistics online during serving to change batch composition/scheduling, close to the trigger mechanism described, though it targets batching decisions rather than kernel specialization/tracing.

survives: The specific twist of an explicit JIT-style trace-and-compile step triggered by a k-hit rolling-window threshold on prefix statistics (as opposed to a pre-built specialized kernel or scheduler reshuffling) is not clearly demonstrated in these papers, so a system that treats prefix detection as a genuine online compilation trigger (with trace caching/invalidation semantics) could still be distinct if that JIT-specific online-compilation angle is developed rather than just kernel design or scheduling.

closest.title: Block Transformer: Global-to-Local Language Modeling for Fast Inference
closest.evidence: we aggregate tokens into fixed size blocks to apply attention across the entire sequence at coarse-grained detail, to capture the global context while minimizing KV cache overhead... upper layers, we apply attention within each block to decode individual tokens
closest.why: same coarse-to-fine hierarchical KV mechanism but built per-request into a trained-from-scratch model rather than a cross-request shared background pyramid served offline.

closest.title: ZoomR: Memory Efficient Reasoning through Multi-Granularity Key Value Retrieval
closest.evidence: uses summary keys as a coarse-grained index during decoding, ZoomR uses the query to retrieve details for only the most important thoughts... This hierarchical strategy significantly reduces memory usage by avoiding full-cache attention at each step
closest.why: same coarse-summary-first, drill-down-when-needed serving pattern, but applied per-request to that request's own cache, not to a shared multi-request background representation.

closest.title: FadeMem: Distance-Aware Memory Consolidation for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
closest.evidence: organizes historical KV blocks into a temporal hierarchy under a fixed cache budget... new history is inserted as fine-grained entries, while older adjacent entries are progressively merged under a power-law temporal allocation schedule
closest.why: same block-averaging/coarsening-into-hierarchy operation on KV cache, again single-request/single-stream rather than cross-request shared corpus statistics.

survives: The genuinely new piece is sharing one coarsened pyramid across many independent requests' unrelated contexts (common-domain background statistics amortized server-wide) with per-request KL-gated unrolling to decide how deep to read, rather than each request building/consulting its own hierarchy over its own cache — none of the closest papers do cross-request shared coarse-graining, so a proposal narrowly targeting that cross-request amortization would still be new.

closest.title: SemShareKV: Efficient KVCache Sharing for Semantically Similar Prompts via Token-Level LSH Matching
closest.evidence: SemShareKV applies fuzzy token matching using locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) on token embeddings ... By selectively reusing relevant key-value pairs from a reference prompt's cache, SemShareKV reduces redundant computation while maintaining output quality.
closest.why: This applies LSH over prompt/token representations across different requests to detect near-duplicate prefixes and share KV cache instead of recomputing, exactly the proposed mechanism and purpose.

closest.title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
closest.evidence: Proximity employs a locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) scheme that enables fast cache lookups while preserving retrieval accuracy... reuses previously retrieved documents when similar queries appear
closest.why: Uses LSH-based cache lookup across requests to detect similarity and reuse cached computation, same cross-request redundancy exploitation idea applied to a related caching layer.

closest.title: PrefixWall: Mitigating Prefix Caching Side Channels in Shared LLM Systems
closest.evidence: APC works by reusing previously computed states for the beginning part of a request (prefix), when another request starts with the same text.
closest.why: Confirms the baseline cross-request prefix KV sharing capability already exists in production systems, which the proposal claims independent batchers cannot do.

survives: A twist could survive if the LSH hashing were applied to rolling mid-sequence windows (not just prefixes) with per-token verification fallback baked into the batch scheduler itself rather than a separate cache layer, but SemShareKV already covers token-level LSH matching for semantically similar (non-exact-prefix) cross-request KV reuse, closing most of this gap.

closest.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
closest.evidence: a "slow" neural net learns by gradient descent to program the "fast weights" of another net through sequences of elementary programming instructions which are additive outer products of self-invented activation patterns (today called keys and values)
closest.why: This establishes exactly the outer-product Hebbian fast-weight update mechanism (with a delta-rule refinement) trained end-to-end for in-context key-value binding and recall, the same mechanism and purpose proposed.

closest.title: Meta-Learning Fast Weight Language Models
closest.evidence: We present Fast Weight Layers (FWLs), a neural component that provides the benefits of dynamic evaluation much more efficiently by expressing gradient updates as linear attention... FWLs can also be applied at training time so the model learns to make good use of gradient updates.
closest.why: Places a trainable fast-weight (linear-attention/outer-product) update inside the network layers, trained end-to-end, for the same purpose of using recent-context associations to improve prediction without gradient updates at inference.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: Recurrent fast-weight memories and selective state-space models compress an expanding context into a fixed-size recurrent state, making the state transition an online learning rule.
closest.why: Directly studies decaying, per-token outer-product fast-weight update rules (Falcon variants) for binding recent token associations within a forward pass, the same mechanism/object as proposed.

survives: Little: applying the fast-weight outer-product update specifically to gate/mix into a standard FFN's weight matrix (rather than as a separate linear-attention layer) is a placement detail already covered by the FWP/linear-transformer equivalence and FWL's training-time fast-weight layers; a genuinely new twist would need a mechanism qualitatively different from outer-product Hebbian/delta updates, not just relocating it inside the FFN.

closest.title: A Theoretical Framework for Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing of Sparse Mixture-of-Experts in Large-Scale AI Models

survives: Adding explicit integral and derivative terms (full PID vs. pure proportional bias) with online-tuned gains is only a tuning/parameterization refinement of the same mechanism already established as loss-free bias-based balancing, so it would need a demonstrated qualitative advantage (e.g., provably better transient stability or oscillation control) to not be a follow-up.

closest.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries: Beyond the Per-Vector Shannon Limit
closest.evidence: predictive delta coding, stores only the residual of each new KV vector from the model's own prediction of it, achieving a per-token entropy bound
closest.why: closest analogue: predicts KV vectors and stores only residuals, similar to the proposal's predict-then-correct scheme, but built on trie-based sequence prediction rather than a positional/n-gram learned-index MLP with explicit pointer/no-store for exact hits.

closest.title: AttentionPredictor: Temporal Patterns Matter for KV Cache Compression
closest.evidence: learns a lightweight, unified convolution model to dynamically capture spatiotemporal patterns and predict the next-token attention scores
closest.why: uses a learned small model per layer to predict something about KV/attention for compression, but predicts attention scores for eviction, not the KV content itself for replacement.

closest.title: Where Matters More Than What: Decoding-aligned KV Cache Compression via Position-aware Pseudo Queries
closest.evidence: positional information plays a more critical role than semantic content
closest.why: uses position-based prediction for KV cache importance, adjacent but for eviction scoring not for regenerating stored key/value content.

survives: Yes: no candidate trains a per-layer positional/n-gram predictor whose output replaces the stored key/value itself (with a pointer and threshold-gated residual correction) analogous to a learned-index structure; the nearest paper (PLT-based predictive delta coding) predicts KV residuals from the model's own sequence prediction rather than a tiny auxiliary MLP keyed on position+local n-gram context with explicit store-nothing-else pointer semantics, so a concrete implementation of position-indexed KV lookup with learned-index-style sparse residual storage is not shown to exist.

closest.title: A Unifying View of Attention Sinks: Two Algorithms, Two Solutions
closest.evidence: adaptive nop, where a head suppresses its update by routing to a null token ... Proposed interventions like gating or registers work because they implicitly target one or the other
closest.why: already places a learned null/sink token in attention to let a head contribute near-zero net update when nothing is relevant, the same capability the proposal targets, but without any conformal calibration guarantee.

closest.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
closest.evidence: adding a placeholder token as a dedicated attention sink during pre-training can further improve streaming deployment
closest.why: introduces a trained dedicated null/placeholder KV token appended for every query, the same placement and mechanism skeleton (learned sink slot) though for cache-eviction stability rather than abstention with a coverage guarantee.

closest.title: Affine-Scaled Attention: Towards Flexible and Stable Transformer Attention
closest.evidence: Prior work has explored modifications such as attention sinks or gating mechanisms, but these approaches provide only limited or indirect control over attention reweighting
closest.why: explicitly aims to relax the softmax unit-sum constraint to allow variable effective mass, the same target capability (non-forced mass allocation), via a different (affine bias/scale) mechanism rather than a calibrated null key.

survives: The distribution-free, split-conformal calibration of a per-head threshold to guarantee a target false-abstention rate is not present in any sink/null-token paper, which use heuristic or learned thresholds/gates without a coverage guarantee — if that calibration-with-guarantee is the load-bearing claim (not just adding a null KV pair), it could survive as a genuinely new twist.

closest.why: uses a mixture-of-experts framing to analyze attention scores but as a theoretical lens for sigmoid vs softmax comparison, not to add a learned abstain component with multiple mixture modes at inference.

closest.title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing
closest.evidence: Queries and keys are mapped to posterior responsibility vectors over a shared latent routing space; their overlap defines an implicit responsibility-space affinity
closest.why: replaces pairwise attention with a mixture-of-Gaussians routing mechanism over keys, but the goal is linear-time efficiency, not multi-modal uncertainty or an explicit abstain mode.

closest.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
closest.evidence: applying a head-specific sigmoid gate after the Scaled Dot-Product Attention (SDPA)-consistently improves performance... this sparse gating mechanism mitigates 'attention sink'
closest.why: introduces a gating mechanism that can suppress attention output (functionally an abstain-like effect) but via a single scalar sigmoid gate, not a mixture-of-softmaxes with multiple learned modes including a dedicated null component.

survives: None of the papers implement a per-query mixture of several full softmax-over-keys distributions (K>=2) with one component pinned to pure null/abstain and a router predicting mixture weights trained jointly with the LM loss; the closest works either use mixture-of-experts as a theoretical attention-analysis tool, replace attention with Gaussian-mixture routing for efficiency, or add a single scalar gate for sink suppression, so the proposed multi-modal discrete mixture with an explicit abstain mode as one of several attention distributions appears genuinely novel.

closest.title: Interleaved Head Attention

survives: Nothing in the set implements a multi-voter quorum gate on attention scores that forces a null/abstain output per query when independent sub-head votes disagree, so the specific mechanism (thresholded voting sub-projections + quorum-based abstention vector) remains open.

closest.title: A Dynamic Head Importance Computation Mechanism for Neural Machine Translation
closest.evidence: design an additional attention layer together with multi-head attention, and utilize the outputs of the multi-head attention along with the input, to compute the importance for each head
closest.why: Uses an auxiliary trained module over multi-head attention outputs to compute per-head importance/weighting, similar placement and purpose to the proposed gating MLP scaling head contributions by agreement.

closest.title: Cascaded Head-colliding Attention
closest.evidence: we re-formulate the MHA as a latent variable model... CODA which explicitly models the interactions between attention heads through a hierarchical variational distribution
closest.why: Explicitly models cross-head interactions/agreement to reweight head contributions, close to a consensus mechanism among heads but framed probabilistically rather than as pairwise voting rounds.

closest.title: MoH: Multi-Head Attention as Mixture-of-Head Attention
closest.evidence: MoH replaces the standard summation in multi-head attention with a weighted summation, introducing flexibility to the attention mechanism
closest.why: Also reweights head outputs before summation using a trained gate, though selection is per-token routing rather than cross-head agreement voting.

survives: The specific pairwise cosine-overlap voting protocol with explicit majority-agreement fraction scaling (rather than a single learned importance/gate score or latent variational interaction) is a distinguishable mechanism if it demonstrably captures corroboration-based down-weighting that differs functionally from importance gating or variational head interaction.

closest.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
closest.evidence: skips an expert slot only when both views identify it as low-contribution, while always retaining the top-1 expert
closest.why: Uses a cheap post-hoc estimate at the router to decide fallback behavior, but per-token/per-expert skipping, not a multi-layer speculative-then-rollback transaction with dense fallback.

closest.title: STAR: A Spatial-Topology Aware Routing Framework for Generalizable 3D Scene Understanding
closest.evidence: Entropy-controlled Dynamic Allocation (EDA), which adjusts the number of activated experts according to routing uncertainty
closest.why: Adjusts routing based on an uncertainty signal, but this is a single-layer allocation adjustment, not a cross-layer transactional commit/rollback to a dense path.

closest.title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents
closest.evidence: a complete abort must restore the state the model attends, not just the transcript
closest.why: Uses rollback/transaction language but targets KV-cache state consistency in agent sessions, not MoE routing consistency across layers.

survives: Nothing in this set groups several consecutive MoE layers into a speculative transaction with a post-hoc cross-layer consistency check that triggers rollback to a dense/averaged path; existing work does per-token/per-expert skipping or single-layer uncertainty gating, not multi-layer speculative commit-or-fallback, so the proposal's cross-layer atomicity guarantee is still open.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we can optimize MoE expert selection on-the-fly based only on input context ... continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data
closest.why: Same capability (in-context routing adaptation without gradient steps or extra data) and same component (router), but via self-supervised optimization of additive router-logit vectors rather than a delta-rule fast-weight memory keyed on a lagged reward signal.

closest.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
closest.evidence: introducing a router memory mechanism to maintain an explicit routing state across model depth. The memory is constructed via linear attention, incrementally aggregating preceding routing scores and their induced residual updates into a compact history representation
closest.why: Places an associative/linear-attention fast memory at the router to condition routing on history, close in mechanism but applied across depth (layer skipping) not per-expert scoring keyed by realized loss delta within a sequence.

closest.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
closest.evidence: gating enables rapid memory erasure while the delta rule facilitates targeted updates
closest.why: Source of the delta-rule fast-weight mechanism itself, but applied to token-mixing/attention memory, not to the MoE router's expert-scoring key-value memory.

survives: The specific twist of using a one-step-lagged, loss-delta-derived error signal (an internal credit-assignment target rather than self-supervised generation quality or purely history-based context) as the delta-rule target for updating router key-value memory is not demonstrated in these papers, so a version centered on that credit-assignment mechanism could still be novel.

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture-of-Experts: Towards Making LLMs Know What They Don't Know
closest.evidence: Instead of forcing a single, deterministic expert selection, our approach models a probability distribution over the routing decision itself... in the weight-space, the logit-space, and the final selection-space
closest.why: Closest match in placing uncertainty modeling directly on router logits, but uses variational/Bayesian distributions rather than a Kalman filter fusing a prior gate score with a causal downstream-error measurement.

closest.title: ROMER: Expert Replacement and Router Calibration for Robust MoE LLMs on Analog Compute-in-Memory Systems
closest.evidence: recalibrates router logits via percentile-based normalization to stabilize routing under noise
closest.why: Also adjusts router logits based on a noise/error signal, but the mechanism is static percentile normalization for hardware noise, not a per-token Kalman gain blending prior and measurement uncertainty.

closest.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
closest.evidence: introducing a router memory mechanism to maintain an explicit routing state across model depth... conditions jointly on this accumulated state and the current hidden representation
closest.why: Shares the idea of maintaining router state updated over sequence/depth, but uses linear-attention memory aggregation rather than a variance-weighted Kalman fusion of prediction and measurement.

survives: The specific mechanism—maintaining an explicit per-expert (mean, variance) Kalman state that computes a gain from estimated prediction vs. measurement noise to blend the raw gate logit with a causal downstream-usefulness proxy from the previous token—is not implemented by any candidate; the nearest works either impose static/Bayesian distributions over routing or recalibrate logits without an online uncertainty-weighted fusion rule.

closest.title: AdaMoE: Token-Adaptive Routing with Null Experts for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

closest.title: Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing Strategy for Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: before the top-K routing decision, Loss-Free Balancing will first apply an expert-wise bias to the routing scores of each expert. By dynamically updating the bias of each expert according to its recent load
closest.why: Same goal of getting load balance without an aux loss by perturbing routing logits with a running statistic, though the perturbation is a deterministic proportional bias rather than a sampled posterior.

closest.title: Variational Routing: A Scalable Bayesian Framework for Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
closest.evidence: VMoER confines Bayesian inference to the expert-selection stage... amortised variational inference over routing logits and inferring a temperature parameter for stochastic expert selection
closest.why: Places a Bayesian/posterior mechanism at the exact same component (router expert-selection) to get uncertainty-aware, stochastic routing, the closest architectural analogue to Thompson sampling over experts.

closest.title: ProbMoE: Differentiable Probabilistic Routing for Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: models expert selection as a distribution over cardinality-constrained expert subsets and formulates routing as probabilistic inference in this discrete subset space
closest.why: Also treats routing as sampling from a probability distribution over experts rather than deterministic top-k, overlapping with the proposal's probabilistic-routing mechanism.

survives: A twist could survive if it specifically uses per-expert conjugate Bayesian bandit posteriors (Beta/Gaussian, online reward-based updates) with the explicit claim that load balance emerges purely from exploration-driven uncertainty with zero auxiliary loss and no explicit balancing bias term, contrasting with VMoER's variational/temperature-based stochasticity and Loss-Free's deterministic bias-correction mechanism — but this delta is narrow and mostly a tuning/parameterization difference rather than a new capability.

closest.title: What Layers When: Learning to Skip Compute in LLMs with Residual Gates
closest.evidence: Each Attention/MLP branch is equipped with a sigmoid-linear gate that condenses the branch's output before it re-enters the residual stream.
closest.why: Nearest mechanism gates residual writes but only scales/skips branch outputs via a fixed learned gate, not via test-time gradient descent (TTT) on a self-supervised reconstruction loss to suppress/invert earlier contributions based on later context.

closest.title: Hyper-Connections
closest.evidence: hyper-connections allow the network to adjust the strength of connections between features at different depths and dynamically rearrange layers
closest.why: Also modifies how residual writes combine across depth, but via a static learned mixing matrix, not an inference-time gradient-based fast-weight update.

closest.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding an Attention Head
closest.evidence: If components in earlier layers predict a certain token, and this token appears earlier in the context, the head suppresses it: we call this copy suppression.
closest.why: Shows an existing mechanism (attention head) that suppresses an earlier-layer contribution based on later context, but this is a fixed learned circuit, not a test-time-trained gate.

survives: Yes: no candidate uses inner-loop gradient descent on a self-supervised reconstruction loss to produce a fast-weight gate that attenuates/inverts specific earlier blocks' residual contributions conditioned on context up to position t; existing gating/hyper-connection work uses static learned parameters rather than test-time training.

survives: Yes: none of the candidates implement a per-block scalar commit gate trained end-to-end (straight-through) that can hard round to zero at inference to fully discard a conflicting/redundant update while bounding aggregate KL drift from an always-commit baseline; the Hyper-Connections family reweights/mixes continuous streams rather than learning a discrete abstain-from-writing veto conditioned on write-write conflict detection.

closest.title: What Layers When: Learning to Skip Compute in LLMs with Residual Gates
closest.evidence: Each Attention/MLP branch is equipped with a sigmoid-linear gate that condenses the branch's output before it re-enters the residual stream. During inference we rank tokens by the gate values and skip low-importance ones using a per-layer budget.
closest.why: This gates whole-branch writes into the residual stream per token/layer, but it is a learned importance gate, not an ARC-style recency/frequency two-list eviction policy over per-channel slots.

closest.title: Scaling Adaptive Depth with Norm-Agnostic Residual Networks
closest.evidence: leads to an interpretable Mixture-of-Depths (MoD) mechanism that adaptively skips both attention and MLP layers
closest.why: Another MoD-style depth-skipping mechanism operating on the residual stream, again gating whole blocks rather than maintaining per-channel recency/frequency counters for eviction.

closest.title: LAVa: Layer-wise KV Cache Eviction with Dynamic Budget Allocation
closest.evidence: we introduce a unified framework for cache compression by minimizing information loss in Transformer residual streams... enabling layer-wise compression with dynamic head budgets
closest.why: This applies dynamic eviction/budgeting logic tied to residual-stream information loss, but at the KV cache, not at residual-stream channels written per token.

survives: The specific combination of ARC's two-list (recency vs frequency) admit/evict balance implemented as a per-token, per-channel router over residual-stream slots (not KV cache entries, not whole-block skipping) giving genuinely variable effective residual width per token is not directly instantiated by any of these; a paper doing exactly this per-channel ARC transplant would still be new.

closest.title: Variable-Width Transformers
closest.evidence: narrowing the middle layers, utilizing a parameter-free residual resizing mechanism... nonuniform width allocation can result in more resource-optimal scaling
closest.why: Allocates residual width non-uniformly but across depth (per-layer), not per-token bandwidth bands within a wavelet-decomposed residual channel.

closest.title: What Layers When: Learning to Skip Compute in LLMs with Residual Gates
closest.evidence: a simple residual-stream gating mechanism that enables token-wise layer skipping... rank tokens by the gate values and skip low-importance ones
closest.why: Achieves per-token adaptive compute via gating on the residual stream, but skips whole layers rather than partitioning channel width into wavelet bands.

closest.title: Review Residuals: Update-Conditioned Residual Gating for Transformers
closest.evidence: scale each update by a learned, input-dependent gate conditioned on both the current state and the proposed update
closest.why: Gates residual updates per-token but as a scalar multiplier on the whole update, not a multiresolution channel-band decomposition.

survives: The specific mechanism of a fixed wavelet/dyadic multiresolution decomposition of the residual channel dimension, with per-band causal gating so tokens selectively read/write coarse vs fine bands, is not implemented by any candidate; nearest works vary depth-wise width or gate whole-layer/whole-update magnitude rather than partitioning and selectively activating explicit frequency bands within the residual width.

closest.title: Residual Matrix Transformers: Scaling the Size of the Residual Stream
closest.evidence: We consider changing the mechanism for retrieving and storing information in the residual stream, and replace the residual stream of the transformer with an outer product memory matrix (Kohonen, 1972, Anderson, 1972)... the size of the residual stream can be scaled independently of compute and model size, improving performance
closest.why: This places an outer-product (Hebbian-style) associative memory directly at the residual stream, read/written per token, explicitly to expand effective residual capacity beyond the fixed channel width, matching the proposal's component, mechanism, and stated new capability.

closest.title: Enhancing Linear Attention with Residual Learning
closest.evidence: RLA maintains an auxiliary recurrent state that learns to accumulate residual errors over time and correct the base prediction
closest.why: Also uses an outer-product-style fast-weight auxiliary state added causally to correct/augment the main representation, though framed at the attention mechanism rather than the residual stream proper.

closest.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
closest.evidence: Test-time training (TTT) views sequence modeling as an online learning problem in which fast weights are updated by an internal learning rule.
closest.why: General fast-weight/TTT framework covering causal outer-product-like updates, overlapping with the mechanism class, though not specifically targeting residual-stream capacity expansion.

survives: Nothing substantive: RMT already implements a causal outer-product fast-weight memory added into the residual pathway at matched compute budget specifically to let the residual stream carry more information than its fixed width, which is exactly the claimed new capability.

closest.title: Contextual Position Encoding: Learning to Count What's Important
closest.evidence: we propose a new position encoding method, Contextual Position Encoding (CoPE), that allows positions to be conditioned on context by incrementing position only on certain tokens determined by the model
closest.why: CoPE makes position content-dependent rather than a fixed function of index for better generalization, overlapping the core capability claim, though via gating/counting rather than sparse dictionary coding.

closest.title: Rethinking Addressing in Language Models via Contexualized Equivariant Positional Encoding
closest.evidence: TAPE introduces dynamic, context-aware positional encodings, overcoming the constraints of traditional fixed patterns... by incorporating sequence content across layers
closest.why: Same placement (positional encoding) and same purpose (content-dependent, generalizable position code beyond fixed index function), but mechanism is equivariant transformation not sparse dictionary/ISTA coding.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: we propose a Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding (DAPE) method, which dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors
closest.why: Same component and same length-generalization goal via data-adaptive (content-dependent) position encoding, differing mechanism (attention-conditioned adjustment vs sparse coding dictionary).

survives: A sparse-dictionary/ISTA mechanism with explicit per-position k-sparse atom selection and joint dictionary learning is mechanistically distinct from CoPE's gating, TAPE's equivariant transform, or DAPE's adaptive bias, so if the k-sparse combinatorial reuse of shared atoms across documents is shown to produce qualitatively different generalization behavior (e.g. atom reuse for structurally analogous positions) that these methods provably lack, the proposal could survive as a genuinely new mechanism at the same component.

closest.title: Graph Inductive Biases in Transformers without Message Passing
closest.evidence: learned relative positional encodings initialized with random walk probabilities
closest.why: Addresses graph positional encoding without message passing, the inverse of the proposal's use of message passing for sequence position, and targets static graphs not streaming KV-cache edit buffers.

closest.title: Size Transferability of Graph Transformers with Convolutional Positional Encodings
closest.evidence: A key design choice in GTs is the use of Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based positional encodings to incorporate structural information
closest.why: Closest in using GNN-based PE for transformers, but for static graph-size transferability, not for collapsing positions across edits/deletions in a streaming KV cache.

survives: None of the papers apply message-passing PE to an explicit dynamically-edited sequence DAG (predecessor + sink + cache-retained edges) specifically to let post-deletion tokens share collapsed effective positions in a streaming edit-buffer/KV-cache setting; this specific mechanism-purpose pairing for streaming edits appears absent.

closest.title: DoPE: Denoising Rotary Position Embedding
closest.evidence: identifies and suppresses noisy attention heads using truncated matrix entropy, then reparameterizes their attention maps with an isotropic Gaussian distribution
closest.why: Same purpose (fixing OOD positional degradation past training length) via an in-place corrective rewrite of positional/attention information, but the rewrite is a denoising reparameterization rather than a delta-rule erase-and-write associative memory with gradient-trained content.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors
closest.why: Same component (positional encoding) and same goal of adapting beyond fixed analytic PE for length generalization, but uses a data-adaptive adjustment network rather than an overwrite-based fast-weight memory keyed on relative distance.

closest.title: Why Does the Effective Context Length of LLMs Fall Short?
closest.evidence: STRING shifts well-trained positions to overwrite the original ineffective positions during inference
closest.why: Explicitly 'overwrites' stale/ineffective position assignments beyond training range, matching the erase/overwrite intent, though via position-index substitution rather than a trained delta-rule associative memory.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would be the specific delta-rule (erase-then-write, beta-gated) fast-weight memory keyed on relative distance and trained end-to-end from scratch specifically for the position channel, as opposed to denoising/reparameterizing attention (DoPE), context-adaptive bias networks (DAPE), or discrete position-index overwriting (STRING) — none of which use a continuously-updated associative memory with the erase-then-write delta rule for positions.

closest.title: Test-Time Training with Next-Token Prediction
closest.evidence: We introduce Test-Time Training with Next-Token Prediction (TTT-NTP), a drop-in fast-weight adaptation method for pretrained LLMs that instead supervises updates using the model's own next contextual hidden state
closest.why: Applies TTT with a next-token self-supervised signal at test time on long contexts, but the adapted object is a fast-weight/value-write mechanism in the cache, not the positional-encoding parameters (RoPE frequencies/ALiBi slopes).

closest.title: Extending the Context of Pretrained LLMs by Dropping Their Positional Embeddings
closest.evidence: positional embeddings are not an inherent requirement of effective language modeling and can be safely removed after pretraining, following a short recalibration phase
closest.why: Also recalibrates the model's handling of position at inference/post-training time for length extension, but by dropping PE entirely rather than test-time-training a handful of RoPE/ALiBi scalar parameters via gradient steps on the incoming stream.

closest.title: CLEX: Continuous Length Extrapolation for Large Language Models
closest.evidence: we propose Continuous Length EXtrapolation (CLEX) for LLMs. We generalise the PE scaling approaches to model the continuous dynamics by ordinary differential equations over the length scaling factor
closest.why: Adapts RoPE-style scaling factors for length extrapolation, but the scaling function is learned during training/fine-tuning, not test-time-trained online via self-supervised next-token loss on the incoming stream itself.

survives: Yes: no paper in the set actually performs online gradient updates on RoPE/ALiBi scalar parameters using a self-supervised next-token loss computed on the live inference stream itself (i.e., true test-time-training restricted to positional parameters, updated every k tokens during a session), as opposed to fixed/learned-at-train-time scaling functions or fast-weight cache rewrites elsewhere in the architecture.

closest.title: Bayesian Attention Mechanism: A Probabilistic Framework for Positional Encoding and Context Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: formulates positional encoding as a prior within a probabilistic model... unifies existing methods (e.g., NoPE and ALiBi) and motivates a new Generalized Gaussian positional prior that substantially improves long-context generalization
closest.why: Closest conceptually: treats positional encoding probabilistically with uncertainty to aid extrapolation, but uses a fixed prior distribution, not a Kalman fusion of two dynamically-weighted position estimates (nominal vs content-derived).

closest.title: Position as Probability: Self-Supervised Transformers that Think Past Their Training for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: PRISM learns continuous relative positions through a differentiable histogram-filter update, preserving position uncertainty via a probabilistic superposition rather than conventional deterministic embeddings.
closest.why: Also maintains a probabilistic/filter-like position estimate for extrapolation, but it is a self-contained histogram filter learned end-to-end, not a fusion of a nominal RoPE angle with a separate content-derived (induction-head-style) measurement via explicit Kalman gain.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: Recurrent fast-weight memories ... compress an expanding context into a fixed-size recurrent state, making the state transition an online learning rule ... Representative variants remain competitive in language modeling and improve length extrapolation on variable-digit addition.
closest.why: Uses fast-weight outer-product-style online updates for sequence modeling and length extrapolation, but the update targets value/key content association for prediction, not a positional-encoding tag bound to relative position via a decaying Hebbian trace.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: we propose a Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding (DAPE) method, which dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors
closest.why: Also aims to make positional encoding adaptive to input content for length extrapolation, but via a learned adjustment network on attention scores, not a decaying Hebbian outer-product fast-weight trace binding content to relative position tags.

closest.title: Reinforced Fast Weights with Next-Sequence Prediction
closest.evidence: Fast weight architectures offer a promising alternative ... by maintaining constant memory overhead regardless of context length ... dynamically update their parameters to store contextual information
closest.why: Fast-weight state update mechanism for long-context modeling, but purpose is improving representation learning via RL-based training objective, not restoring position-content locality signal beyond training length via a positional tag outer product.

survives: None of the retrieved papers place a decaying Hebbian outer-product trace specifically between content vectors and bounded relative-position tags, added as a low-rank bias to the value projection and reset per sequence, purely to refresh position-content locality beyond trained length; the nearest works either adapt positional bias via learned networks (DAPE) or use fast-weights for general content/state memory (Fast Weight Attention, REFINE), so a mechanism whose sole state is a position-tag outer product for locality restoration remains open.

closest.title: zip2zip: Inference-Time Adaptive Tokenization via Online Compression

closest.title: Adaptive Activation Steering for Efficient LLM Reasoning via Closed-Loop PID Control

survives: Yes: no paper closes a PID feedback loop specifically on a tokenizer's merge-threshold parameter using rolling per-byte loss as the error signal to hold compression ratio at a fixed setpoint; the closest matches either use PID for a different component (activation steering) or adjust chunking/compression via curriculum schedules or compression heuristics rather than explicit closed-loop control.

closest.title: ByteSpan: Information-Driven Subword Tokenisation
closest.evidence: we explore whether grouping predictable bytes ... can yield a useful fixed subword vocabulary. We propose a new information-driven subword tokeniser, ByteSpan, that uses an external byte-level LM during training to identify contiguous predictable byte sequences and group them into subwords
closest.why: Nearest analogue: uses an auxiliary byte-level LM's predictive signal to drive merge/grouping decisions during vocabulary construction, but selects by prediction error/predictability rather than a contrastive pull/push objective against sampled hard negative continuations.

closest.title: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization
closest.evidence: we show that BPE itself incorporates the ability to produce multiple segmentations of the same word
closest.why: Also modifies BPE merge selection/application but via stochastic dropout regularization, not a contrastive scoring loop with an auxiliary model re-ranking merges.

closest.title: ByteFlow: Language Modeling through Adaptive Byte Compression without a Tokenizer
closest.evidence: performs compression-driven segmentation based on the coding rate of latent representations, yielding adaptive boundaries
closest.why: Learns segmentation jointly with a model but replaces the tokenizer entirely rather than pre-constructing a frozen BPE-style vocabulary via a contrastive merge-scoring loop.

survives: None of the candidates use a contrastive (pull-toward-true-continuation, push-from-sampled-negative-continuations) objective specifically to re-rank/select BPE merge candidates in an iterative merge-then-score loop before freezing a vocabulary; ByteSpan and ByteFlow use predictability/compression signals, not contrastive separability, so the specific contrastive-merge-scoring mechanism at this component appears open.

closest.title: Modeling Multimodal Aleatoric Uncertainty in Segmentation with Mixture of Stochastic Experts

closest.title: Distributional regression with reject option
closest.evidence: we introduce a framework that enables the model to abstain from estimation in situations of high uncertainty ... relies on thresholding the entropy function of the Continuous Ranked Probability Score
closest.why: Same purpose (abstention driven by predictive-distribution uncertainty/entropy) but abstention is a post-hoc threshold on a derived entropy score, not a trained mixture component with its own weight.

survives: The specific mechanism of adding a (K+1)-th 'ABSTAIN' mixture component—no vocabulary logits, just a learned mixing weight trained via an auxiliary disagreement-based loss, jointly with a frozen trunk and K vocabulary components at the LM output head—does not appear to be instantiated in any retrieved paper; SelectiveNet and reject-option regression use a separate rejection head/threshold rather than an intrinsic mixture component competing for probability mass, so a genuinely novel contribution would need to demonstrate that this in-mixture null-component formulation (vs. auxiliary head) yields materially different calibration/behavior.

closest.title: Singular Relative Entropy Coding with Bits-Back Rejection Sampling
closest.evidence: A relative entropy code for a source X ~ P_X is a stochastic code that encodes random samples from a prescribed P_{Y|X} using as few bits as possible... combines ideas from bits-back coding and (greedy) rejection sampling
closest.why: Nearest in mechanism (entropy/relative-entropy coding tied to sampling) but targets minimal-bit relative entropy coding of a fixed channel, not a bijective sampler receipt enabling replay/re-ranking under a different model.

closest.title: RAS: A Bit-Exact rANS Accelerator For High-Performance Neural Lossless Compression
closest.evidence: RAS couples an rANS core with a probabilistic generator... maintain bit-exactness
closest.why: Uses an entropy-coding (rANS, arithmetic-coding-family) accelerator bound to a probability model for bit-exact lossless compression, but purpose is compression throughput, not retroactive re-sampling/re-ranking of LM generations under a revised distribution.

closest.title: Field Codes for Distributed Coupling Samplers and Certified Empirical Transport
closest.evidence: any communicated transport field approximating an optimal empirical Monge map to error η can be completed by sparse target-cell residuals into an exact-marginal value-certified sampler
closest.why: Conceptually adjacent (coding schemes tied to sampling/transport with exactness guarantees) but concerns distributed optimal-transport communication, not LM decoding receipts for counterfactual replay.

survives: None of the retrieved papers place an arithmetic-coding bijection at the LM sampler step to store per-token code-stream receipts that let a different (recalibrated) model deterministically re-derive alternate token choices from the same bits; this specific bit-exact-replay/counterfactual-resampling capability at the sampler is not addressed by any candidate, so the twist of exact CDF-to-interval bijection enabling off-line re-ranking under a different top-p/temperature remains open.

closest.title: Adaptive Decoding via Test-Time Policy Learning for Self-Improving Generation
closest.evidence: learns a lightweight policy to adjust sampling parameters at test-time while keeping LLM weights frozen
closest.why: same capability (learned per-step control of temperature/sampling parameters at the sampler, frozen base model) but via an RL policy rather than a delta-rule associative memory keyed on hidden state.

closest.title: Hot or Cold? Adaptive Temperature Sampling for Code Generation with Large Language Models
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts the temperature coefficient when decoding different tokens... applies a larger temperature when sampling for challenging tokens
closest.why: same capability (per-token adaptive temperature) but driven by a heuristic token-difficulty rule, not a trained associative memory.

closest.title: EDT: Improving Large Language Models' Generation by Entropy-based Dynamic Temperature Sampling
closest.evidence: propose an effective Entropy-based Dynamic Temperature (EDT) Sampling method, to achieve a more balanced performance... by dynamically selecting the temperature parameter
closest.why: same capability (dynamic per-step temperature from entropy signal) but uses a closed-form entropy function rather than a learned delta-rule memory bank.

survives: Yes: none of these use a trained, continuously overwritten (erase-then-write/delta-rule) associative memory keyed on hidden states to store and retrieve per-position dispersion targets; that specific mechanism (small trainable key-value memory bank updated online via delta rule, read via attention) at the sampler is not demonstrated by any close paper, only heuristic entropy functions or RL policies.
