closest.title: Prioritized Experience Replay
closest.evidence: we develop a framework for prioritizing experience, so as to replay important transitions more frequently, and therefore learn more efficiently
closest.why: This is the base mechanism (TD-error prioritized replay) the proposal explicitly builds on, but it is applied to Q-learning value networks, not to a sampler temperature/top-k controller.

closest.title: Hot or Cold? Adaptive Temperature Sampling for Code Generation with Large Language Models
closest.evidence: we propose Adaptive Temperature (AdapT) sampling, which dynamically adjusts the temperature coefficient when decoding different tokens
closest.why: Same component (temperature controller in decoding) and similar goal of allocating exploration to hard tokens, but uses a static loss-distribution heuristic rather than a learned controller trained via prioritized replay on realized surprisal error.

closest.title: Entropic-Time Inference: Self-Organizing Large Language Model Decoding Beyond Attention
closest.evidence: adaptive temperature control that stabilizes generation near a target entropy regime
closest.why: Also places an entropy-driven adaptive temperature controller in the decoding loop, but as a heuristic control-theoretic module, not an online-learned MLP trained via prioritized replay over past miscalibration.

survives: The specific mechanism of maintaining a ring buffer of (hidden-state, temperature, realized-surprisal) triples and training a small online controller MLP via TD-error-prioritized replay sampling (rather than a heuristic or fixed schedule) does not appear in any candidate paper, so this exact combination remains open.

closest.title: Hot or Cold? Adaptive Temperature Sampling for Code Generation with Large Language Models
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts the temperature coefficient when decoding different tokens

closest.title: Entropic-Time Inference: Self-Organizing Large Language Model Decoding Beyond Attention
closest.evidence: adaptive temperature control that stabilizes generation near a target entropy regime
closest.why: couples sampling temperature to entropy signals at decode time, adjacent adaptive-sampling idea but not a wavelet multiresolution decomposition of the logit distribution.

survives: The specific mechanism of applying a discrete wavelet transform to the sorted per-step logit vector to separately shrink high-frequency (rank-jitter) detail coefficients while temperature-scaling coarse coefficients, then inverse-transforming before softmax, is not implemented in any candidate paper; FiGKD applies wavelet decomposition to logits but for cross-model distillation, not single-model sampling control.

closest.title: PREADD: Prefix-Adaptive Decoding for Controlled Text Generation
closest.evidence: PREADD contrasts the output logits generated using a raw prompt against those generated using a prefix-prepended prompt, enabling both positive and negative control
closest.why: Both modify logits pre-sampling to control generation, but PREADD uses static prompt contrast, not a decaying Hebbian trace of recently sampled tokens.

closest.title: Think Twice Before You Write -- an Entropy-based Decoding Strategy to Enhance LLM Reasoning
closest.evidence: the model computes the entropy of the token distribution, identifies high-uncertainty positions, and selectively branches on these vulnerable points
closest.why: Adapts sampling decisions per step from recent context signals, but uses entropy-based branching rather than a persistent outer-product fast-weight memory biasing logits.

closest.title: Hot or Cold? Adaptive Temperature Sampling for Code Generation with Large Language Models
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts the temperature coefficient when decoding different tokens
closest.why: Adjusts sampling temperature adaptively at decode time, but based on token category/position, not a Hebbian trace of just-sampled tokens with built-in decay.

survives: The specific mechanism of an outer-product Hebbian fast-weight matrix over sampled-token embeddings, updated and exponentially decayed step-by-step to bias top-k/temperature at the sampler with automatic few-step forgetting, is not implemented by any candidate; nearest works use static prompt contrast, entropy-triggered branching, or heuristic temperature schedules rather than a self-decaying associative memory keyed on recent sampling history.

closest.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
closest.evidence: SpecPrefill leverages a lightweight model to speculate locally important tokens based on the context. These tokens...are then sent to the main model for processing.
closest.why: Both reduce TTFT via a lightweight auxiliary scorer over prompt tokens, but SpecPrefill prunes tokens once rather than maintaining/resampling a population of partial-prefill KV hypotheses and emitting a token before the full prompt is exactly encoded.

closest.title: KV Prediction for Improved Time to First Token
closest.evidence: a small auxiliary model is used to process the prompt and produce an approximation of the KV cache used by a base model. This approximated KV cache is then used with the base model for autoregressive generation without the need to query the auxiliary model again.
closest.why: Also approximates/pre-computes the prefill KV cache to cut TTFT, but produces a single approximate cache rather than an SMC population of weighted, resampled partial-prefill particles that collapse to the exact cache.

closest.title: Stream2LLM: Overlap Context Streaming and Prefill for Reduced Time-to-First-Token (TTFT)
closest.evidence: Streaming context incrementally--overlapping retrieval with inference--can mitigate this latency... requests contend for GPU compute and memory, and scheduling must adapt to dynamic context arrivals.
closest.why: Shares the incremental/chunked prefill framing for TTFT reduction but has no particle population, importance weighting, or resampling over partial-cache hypotheses.

survives: None of the candidates maintain a weighted, resampled population of partial-prefill KV-cache hypotheses (SMC) that lets a token be emitted before exact full-prompt encoding and then collapses to the exact cache; the nearest work either prunes/approximates the cache once (SpecPrefill, KV Prediction) or streams context without particle-based resampling (Stream2LLM), so the SMC-specific mechanism at prefill is unaddressed.

closest.evidence: append-prefill, which processes only the new input tokens while reusing cached KV states, incurs an order-of-magnitude smaller decoding slowdown than full prefill
closest.why: involves reusing partially committed KV state and routing decode-before-full-prefill, but has no divergence gate or rollback of already-emitted tokens.

closest.title: From Tokens to Layers: Redefining Stall-Free Scheduling for MoE Serving with Layered Prefill
closest.evidence: splits the processing of long prompts along the token dimension and interleaves prefill with ongoing decode iterations
closest.why: chunked prefill interleaved with decode is structurally similar to chunk-based commit, but tokens generated always reflect the full processed prefix so far with no speculative unlock before full consumption and no rollback mechanism.

closest.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
closest.evidence: leverages a lightweight model to speculate locally important tokens based on the context... sent to the main model for processing
closest.why: speculatively estimates prompt content to save compute but does not begin token emission before the whole prompt is processed, nor rolls back emitted continuations.

survives: The core untaken mechanism is speculative unlocking of decode after only a prefix chunk of the prompt, paired with an explicit rollback-and-regenerate protocol triggered by a trained divergence gate when later chunks retroactively invalidate the shallow encoding; none of the retrieved systems commit to emitting tokens before the full prompt is seen and then visibly roll back generation.

closest.title: A Multi-Model Adaptation of Speculative Decoding for Classification
closest.evidence: When majority worker models agree on a label, it is accepted as the final label, optimizing efficiency by bypassing the computationally expensive judge model... In cases of disagreement, the judge model intervenes to resolve the label.
closest.why: This is the closest known mechanism (multiple cheap workers vote, expensive judge only on disagreement) but applied to classification labels, not to accelerating the first-token emission of prefill by skipping exact full attention.

closest.title: Speculative Decoding for Multi-Sample Inference
closest.evidence: it identifies consensus token sequences that align with the decoding distribution... exploits the intrinsic consensus of parallel generation paths to synthesize high-quality draft tokens without requiring auxiliary models
closest.why: Uses consensus across parallel generation paths as the draft signal, but for multi-sample decode-time drafting, not for replacing exact prefill with cheap approximate-attention lanes voting on token-1.

closest.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
closest.evidence: SpecPrefill leverages a lightweight model to speculate locally important tokens based on the context. These tokens ... are then sent to the main model for processing.
closest.why: Targets TTFT/prefill speedup via a cheap approximation, but reduces token count fed to exact prefill rather than using a voting quorum of multiple cheap attention-approximation lanes to skip exact prefill outright.

survives: No paper places multiple cheap differently-approximated prefill lanes (sliding-window, sink, low-rank) in parallel, uses cross-lane agreement/KL as a quorum gate to emit token-1 without ever running exact full-attention prefill on the agreeing fraction of prompts, and falls back to exact prefill only as a post-hoc arbiter/corrective mechanism — this specific consensus-gated skip-or-fallback structure at the prefill component for TTFT reduction is not covered by the nearest classification-consensus, multi-sample-consensus, or token-pruning-prefill papers.

closest.title: SpecKV: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Compression-Aware Gamma Selection
closest.evidence: SpecKV uses a small MLP trained on these signals to maximize expected tokens per speculation step... draft model confidence and entropy are strong predictors of acceptance rate
closest.why: Same placement (learned head mapping draft confidence/hidden signals to speculation length) and same purpose (choosing k), but uses a point-estimate MLP regressor rather than a mixture-density distribution over run-length.

closest.title: TapOut: A Bandit-Based Approach to Dynamic Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: Existing methods often rely on hand-tuned, sensitive thresholds (e.g., token entropy)... selects among multiple parameter-free dynamic speculation strategies based on past reward and exploration
closest.why: Also replaces a scalar confidence threshold with a more expressive policy for choosing draft length, though via bandit selection rather than a learned probability distribution.

closest.title: Dynamic Speculation Lookahead Accelerates Speculative Decoding of Large Language Models
closest.evidence: We introduce DISCO ... for dynamically selecting the SL... show that the common practice of using the same SL for all iterations (static SL) is suboptimal
closest.why: Same component/purpose (dynamic draft-length selection) but uses a different, non-distributional mechanism to pick SL.

survives: The specific mechanism of modeling accept-run-length as an explicit mixture density (capturing bimodal/heavy-tailed reliability rather than a single scalar or bandit-selected value) and choosing k via a quantile of that mixture is not shown in any candidate paper, which all use point-estimate regressors, thresholds, or bandit/heuristic policies.

closest.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
closest.evidence: By iterating a block of shared layers a variable number of times, the model can use less compute for "easy" tokens and more for "hard" ones... schedules at the granularity of individual loop iterations
closest.why: Same component (layer-schedule) and same goal of amortizing depth per-token, but decision is confidence/difficulty-based per-token rather than a hashed-context trace-cache reusing prior recorded shallow execution paths.

closest.title: BUDDY: BUdget-Driven DYnamic Depth Routing for Adaptive Large Language Model Inference
closest.evidence: Buddy uses a lightweight Decision Module to score intermediate layers conditioned on the input and deterministically executes the top-k layers to satisfy a given budget... reuses the first-layer KV cache as a low-overhead global context source
closest.why: Also learns a small controller mapping hidden state to a reduced layer subset at inference, but it is a per-step budget router, not a hash-keyed trace-memoization table keyed on repeated local context signatures.

closest.title: LoRA-Drop: Temporal LoRA Decoding for Efficient LLM Inference
closest.evidence: applying a temporal compute schedule to a fixed subset of intermediate layers: on most decoding steps, selected layers reuse the previous-token hidden state and apply a low-rank LoRA correction, while periodic refresh steps execute the full model to prevent drift
closest.why: Shares the reuse-with-periodic-verification-against-full-pass structure (analogous to the 1-in-N logit-KL check) but reuses temporally adjacent hidden states rather than a hashed trace keyed to recurring n-gram/context signatures.

survives: The specific mechanism of hashing a k-token context signature into a persistent trace table that memoizes and replays previously-verified shorter layer subsets for recurring/repeated spans (n-grams, boilerplate, copy spans) — as opposed to per-token difficulty/confidence routing or temporal reuse of the immediately preceding token's state — is not directly shown in any single paper, so a proposal emphasizing content-addressed cross-occurrence trace reuse (not just adjacent-step or confidence-based adaptive depth) could still be novel.

closest.title: Adaptive Layer-skipping in Pre-trained LLMs
closest.evidence: FlexiDepth enables adaptive computation in LLMs without modifying their original parameters... generating repetitive tokens or fixed phrases requires fewer layers
closest.why: Same capability (input-dependent depth reduction, especially for repeated tokens) via a trained plug-in router/adapter on a frozen backbone, but the router is a slow-weight trained gate, not a Hebbian fast-weight outer-product accumulator updated online within the sequence.

closest.title: Mixture-of-Top-k Attention: Efficient Attention via Scalable Fast Weights
closest.evidence: The vanilla self-attention mechanism in Transformers can be viewed as a two-layer fast-weight MLP... this fast-weight perspective has motivated the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) attention mechanism
closest.why: Uses the fast-weight framing for routing/attention but applies it to token-expert/attention routing, not to a layer-depth-skipping gate driven by a Hebbian outer-product accumulator over hidden states.

closest.title: Scaling Adaptive Depth with Norm-Agnostic Residual Networks
closest.evidence: The norm-agnostic formulation also leads to an interpretable Mixture-of-Depths (MoD) mechanism that adaptively skips both attention and MLP layers
closest.why: Also produces an adaptive per-token depth-skip gate, but the gate is learned via backprop on residual-norm structure, not a training-free Hebbian fast-weight accumulator reset per sequence.

survives: No candidate combines a genuinely non-backprop, per-sequence-reset Hebbian outer-product accumulator (A <- lambda*A + eta*h h^T) as the actual gating signal for layer-skip depth; all depth-adaptive/layer-skip works here use slow-weight trained routers/gates (even when noting repetition lowers required depth empirically), so the specific mechanism-purpose pairing (fast-weight Hebbian trace driving a depth gate, reset per sequence, no optimizer touch) is not demonstrated.

closest.title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
closest.evidence: treat looping as a refinement of the same approximation, replacing one large update with smaller damped sub-steps
closest.why: loops a mid-stack block multiple times to refine representations, closest in mechanism (repeated block application for refinement) but uses damped Euler-step blending, not an EMA over trajectory states, and is training-free rather than trained from scratch.

closest.title: EMA Is Not All You Need: Mapping the Boundary Between Structure and Content in Recurrent Context
closest.evidence: We use exponential moving average (EMA) traces... as a controlled probe to map the boundary between what fixed-coefficient accumulation can and cannot represent
closest.why: studies EMA of representations over time/context, not EMA over a block's repeated-application depth trajectory.

closest.title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
closest.evidence: simple post-hoc confidence readouts often match or outperform learned linear and MLP gates
closest.why: explores non-learned readouts of loop trajectories as an alternative to halting gates, adjacent to proposal's 'no learned gate' framing but uses confidence-based selection, not EMA averaging of iterates.

survives: Yes: none of the found papers average the T repeated-application intermediate states of a single block via an EMA and feed that average (not the final iterate) forward as the block's output at both train and inference time; the closest looped-transformer work either blends via damped ODE steps or uses learned/confidence-based halting rather than a fixed-decay EMA over the unrolled trajectory.

closest.title: AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth
closest.evidence: AdaPonderLM uses iteration-specific MLP gates with a monotonic halting mask to decide when each token stops recurring
closest.why: same capability (per-token, per-pass halting for looped block re-application) but via learned MLP gates on hidden state, not a Kalman filter fusing measurement/prior with an explicit gain and uncertainty variable.

closest.title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
closest.evidence: treat looping as a refinement of the same approximation, replacing one large update with smaller damped sub-steps
closest.why: shares the idea of repeatedly re-applying a block as an iterative refinement/update but uses an ODE/damping view, not a Kalman gain/innovation-based stopping rule.

closest.title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
closest.evidence: Learned halting objectives in looped Transformers typically use a single exit distribution both as the inference-time stopping rule and as the training-time weighting of per-depth losses
closest.why: addresses halting-gate design for looped blocks (same component/purpose) but analyzes generic learned confidence gates, not a Kalman-filter fusion of measurement and prior with gain-weighted update.

survives: The specific mechanism—explicit Bayesian fusion (Kalman gain) of the block's raw output as a noisy measurement against a running mean/variance prior, with a learned observation-noise head and innovation-based halting threshold—is not instantiated in any candidate; all found methods use scalar confidence/halting gates or ODE-style damping rather than a two-moment (mu, sigma^2) recursive estimator, so this remains a live, non-duplicated idea.

closest.title: Prox: Training-Free FFN Activation Sparsity via Approximate Intermediate-Channel Salience in LLMs
closest.evidence: Prox hinges on the key insight: sparse execution requires only the channel mask induced by the intermediate state, which can be constructed from the magnitude ranking of its entries rather than their exact values.
closest.why: Same component (FFN activation sparsification per token) but selection is magnitude/ranking-based top-k proxy, not a submodular-coverage objective with an approximation-ratio certificate.

closest.title: PrunePath: Towards Highly Structured Sparse Language Models
closest.evidence: replaces independent expert-wise thresholding with a softmax-normalized routing distribution and activates important experts under a cumulative-mass threshold... enabling adaptive expert counts and a direct inference-time sparsity knob
closest.why: Provides an adaptive, budget-controllable alternative to top-k for FFN/expert sparsity, but the guarantee is a probability-mass threshold, not a submodular greedy coverage certificate with (1-1/e) approximation.

closest.title: Learning Neural Networks with Sparse Activations
closest.evidence: we initiate a formal study of PAC learnability of MLP layers that exhibit activation sparsity... classes of functions do lead to provable computational and statistical advantages
closest.why: Offers theoretical guarantees for sparse MLP activations but is a learnability/statistical result, not a per-token submodular selection rule replacing top-k with a coverage certificate.

survives: None of the retrieved papers replace top-k FFN key selection with a submodular greedy surrogate (facility-location/coverage objective) that yields a per-token (1-1/e)-style certified approximation to the dense activation; the closest works either use magnitude ranking (Prox) or cumulative probability mass (PrunePath) as the selection rule, which lack the diminishing-returns submodular guarantee that is the proposal's core claim.

closest.title: Large Product Key Memory for Pretrained Language Models
closest.evidence: Product key memory (PKM) proposed by Lample et al. (2019) enables to improve prediction accuracy by increasing model capacity efficiently with insignificant computational overhead.
closest.why: PKM is the hand-designed sub-linear key-lookup mechanism for FFN memory that the proposal itself names as the nearest known variant, differing only in using a learned index model rather than a fixed product-key factorization.

closest.title: Mixture of Lookup Experts
closest.evidence: these experts can be re-parameterized as lookup tables (LUTs) that retrieves expert outputs based on input ids, and offloaded to storage devices
closest.why: replaces dense FFN/expert scoring with direct table lookup keyed on input, the same sub-linear-lookup capability but via ID-based LUT reparameterization rather than a learned index/bucket predictor.

closest.title: Fast-weight Product Key Memory
closest.evidence: FwPKM updates sparsely activated parameters at both training and inference time using chunk-level gradient descent on a local memory-rewrite objective... enabling rapid memorization and retrieval of many new key-value associations while keeping per-token compute low and fixed
closest.why: another product-key-style sparse FFN memory access mechanism, tuning of the same sparse-retrieval family rather than a learned-index predictor.

survives: A genuinely learned, jointly-trained index model that predicts a bucket via an auxiliary regression/classification loss (rather than a fixed hash/product-key factorization or ID-based LUT) could still be new if it demonstrably outperforms or behaves differently from PKM-style fixed structures at equal capacity, but no paper here implements that specific learned-index training scheme for FFN keys.

closest.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
closest.evidence: we replace the purely additive outer products by a delta rule-like programming instruction, such that the FWP can more easily learn to correct the current mapping from keys to values
closest.why: This establishes the delta-rule fast-weight mechanism itself (same update equation) but applies it inside linear-attention layers, not as a replacement for the FFN up-projection's static key-value memory.

closest.title: Neural Knowledge Bank for Pretrained Transformers
closest.evidence: we design a Neural Knowledge Bank (NKB) ... in the form of additional knowledgeable memory slots to the FFN and the memory-like architecture makes it highly interpretable and flexible
closest.why: Treats the FFN explicitly as an editable key-value memory store, the same object the proposal targets, but edits are static/injected rather than an online per-token delta-rule rewrite.

closest.title: Meta-Learning Fast Weight Language Models
closest.evidence: Fast Weight Layers (FWLs), a neural component that provides the benefits of dynamic evaluation much more efficiently by expressing gradient updates as linear attention... FWLs can easily be added on top of existing transformer models
closest.why: Applies fast-weight/gradient-like online updates trained end-to-end on top of transformer blocks for continual mid-stream adaptation, closely mirroring the proposal's training setup and update mechanism, though not specifically targeting the FFN's up-projection as a factual memory slot to be corrected.

survives: The specific twist of applying the delta rule as an erase-and-rewrite operation directly on the FFN's up-projection weight matrix (treating it as the classic Sukhbaatar/Geva key-value memory) to enable token-level factual correction and readout at a later token, evaluated with matched-FLOPs nano-scale ablation, is not demonstrated as such in any single paper—closest work either does delta-rule in attention (not FFN) or edits FFN memories via static/injected methods (not online per-token delta rule), so a paper combining both specifically at the FFN with this correction-capability framing would still be new.

closest.title: HoReN: Normalized Hopfield Retrieval for Large-Scale Sequential Model Editing
closest.evidence: retrieves edits by angular similarity on the unit hypersphere, and refines queries through damped Hopfield dynamics so paraphrases converge to the correct memory basin
closest.why: Uses associative dynamics among key-value memory entries in an MLP-wrapped memory for editing, closest in mechanism flavor but applied to sequential edit storage/retrieval, not per-token FFN message-passing among hidden units during normal forward computation.

closest.title: Mixture of Experts Meets Decoupled Message Passing: Towards General and Adaptive Node Classification
closest.evidence: combines fine-grained message-passing operations with a mixture-of-experts mechanism to build feature encoding blocks
closest.why: Combines message-passing with FFN/expert-like structures, but for graph node classification, not for propagating updates among a transformer's FFN key-value memory slots.

closest.title: Neuron-Level Analysis of Cultural Understanding in Large Language Models
closest.evidence: Culture-general and culture-specific neurons account for less than 1% of all neurons and are concentrated in shallow to middle MLP layers.
closest.why: Analyzes FFN neurons as discrete knowledge units but does not propose any mechanism for them to exchange updates with each other.

survives: Nothing in the set makes FFN hidden units into graph nodes that exchange value updates with each other after each token write; the nearest work (HoReN) only does content-addressed retrieval/denoising over a codebook for offline sequential edits, not per-token online message-passing between memory slots during normal forward passes, so the proposed simultaneous propagation to semantic neighbors during training-time inference remains untested.

closest.title: Graph-MLP: Node Classification without Message Passing in Graph
closest.evidence: we design a neighboring contrastive (NContrast) loss to bridge the gap between GNNs and MLPs by utilizing the adjacency information implicitly
closest.why: Uses a contrastive loss with layer normalization to inject structural (relational) information into representations, but applied to graph adjacency for MLP node classification, not to LayerNorm statistics for cross-sequence token consistency in language models.

closest.title: On Separate Normalization in Self-supervised Transformers
closest.evidence: we propose in this paper a simple modification that employs separate normalization layers for the tokens and the [CLS] symbol to better capture their distinct characteristics
closest.why: Modifies normalization behavior for self-supervised transformers but via separate statistics per token type, not via a contrastive cross-sequence objective on LayerNorm parameters.

closest.title: Normalized Matching Transformer
closest.evidence: we enforce unit-norm embeddings at every Transformer layer and train with a combined contrastive InfoNCE and hyperspherical uniformity loss
closest.why: Combines InfoNCE contrastive loss with per-layer normalization to shape embeddings, but for keypoint matching feature discrimination, not for pulling per-token LayerNorm statistics toward a cross-sequence context cluster.

survives: None of the retrieved papers apply an InfoNCE-style contrastive loss specifically to the pre-normalization activations of LayerNorm to pull same-local-context tokens across different training sequences into a shared statistical regime while leaving inference-time normalization unchanged; this specific placement (auxiliary contrastive head on LayerNorm's gain/bias, removed at inference) is not covered.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would be the specific placement: using an MDL two-part code (bits for L plus residual entropy) to select among discrete causal normalization window lengths per layer online, since no candidate paper combines MDL model selection with the normalization-window/aggregation-granularity choice at a neural network layer.

survives: Nothing in the set replaces LayerNorm's per-token mean/variance computation itself with a causal, incrementally-updated wavelet multiresolution tree (trained filter taps) inside a standard transformer block; the nearest works either apply multi-scale decomposition to embeddings/retrieval or use trend-extraction blocks for series-level normalization, so a causal wavelet-based normalization statistic at the LayerNorm site appears genuinely unaddressed.

closest.title: 4-bit Shampoo for Memory-Efficient Network Training

survives: None of the found papers combine a per-parameter/block-average convex blend with an explicit annealed alpha schedule keyed to parameter activation events (unmasking, LoRA rank growth) for the specific purpose of giving newly active or rarely-updated parameters a warm-started second moment; that activation-triggered inheritance mechanism, framed as RG coarse-graining, appears to be a genuinely new twist relative to the memory-compression or fixed block-factorization purposes seen in the closest papers.

closest.why: Applies Kalman filtering directly to the stochastic optimization update itself (fusing gradient/state uncertainty) to derive step behavior, rather than fusing a schedule prior with a loss-noise measurement to set LR.

closest.title: PMGS: Reconstruction of Projectile Motion Across Large Spatiotemporal Spans via 3D Gaussian Splatting
closest.evidence: we design a dynamic simulated annealing strategy that adaptively schedules learning rates based on motion states...we devise a Kalman fusion scheme to optimize error accumulation from multi-source observations

closest.title: Stepping on the Edge: Curvature Aware Learning Rate Tuners
closest.evidence: We analyze the closed-loop feedback effect between learning rate tuning and curvature.
closest.why: Closed-loop LR control based on measured training statistics (curvature) is conceptually adjacent but uses curvature/sharpness feedback, not an explicit Bayesian/Kalman fusion of a prior schedule and noisy loss measurement with uncertainty weighting.

survives: The specific mechanism of running an explicit 1D Kalman update that fuses a prior schedule curve (process model) with a windowed loss/gradient-noise measurement, weighted by estimated process/measurement variances, to produce the per-step LR appears novel; no paper implements this precise dual-uncertainty fusion for the LR schedule itself, though the Kalman-for-optimization and closed-loop LR-control literatures are close.

closest.title: Online Learning-guided Learning Rate Adaptation via Gradient Alignment
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts the learning rate by tracking the alignment between consecutive gradients and using a local curvature estimate... produces a flexible, adaptive learning rate schedule that tends to increase when consecutive gradients are aligned and decrease otherwise
closest.why: same component (lr-schedule) and same capability of self-tuning reactivity vs. stability online without hand-tuned mixing, though via gradient alignment rather than an ARC-style dual-tracker hit-ratio mechanism.

closest.title: An Automatic Learning Rate Schedule Algorithm for Achieving Faster Convergence and Steeper Descent
closest.evidence: dynamically scheduling the learning rate based on the difference between the current and previous weight updates... RDBD (Regrettable Delta-Bar-Delta)... allows for prompt correction of biased learning rate adjustments

closest.title: Adaptive Gradient Methods with Local Guarantees
closest.evidence: study the problem of learning a local preconditioner, that can change as the data is changing along the optimization trajectory... automatically choosing the optimal learning rate schedule
closest.why: online adaptive regret-based tuning of LR without manual schedule, same capability goal of self-tuning without hand-set coefficients, but mechanism is regret-based preconditioning, not ARC-style ghost-list balance.

survives: The specific ARC-inherited mechanism—two exponential trackers at different timescales plus a single online-adapted mixing parameter p updated by a hit/predictive-success rule mirroring ARC's ghost-list adjustment—is not explicitly instantiated in any candidate; if that precise dual-tracker/self-tuned-blend-ratio structure (rather than gradient alignment, curvature, or delta-bar-delta signals) is essential and demonstrably different in behavior, it could still be novel.

closest.title: Safe Overtaking for Autonomous Racing Using Hierarchical Optimization and Learning-Based Control
closest.evidence: Model Predictive Control (MPC) combined with Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) provides a principled mechanism for certifying forward invariance of a safe set... a reinforcement learning policy adapts the discrete-time CBF decay parameter online
closest.why: Uses discrete-time CBF machinery with an online-adapted decay parameter for safety certification, the same mechanism class applied to a different control target (vehicle trajectory, not lr-schedule).

closest.title: Stepping on the Edge: Curvature Aware Learning Rate Tuners
closest.evidence: We analyze the closed-loop feedback effect between learning rate tuning and curvature... introduce a new learning rate tuning method, Curvature Dynamics Aware Tuning (CDAT), which prioritizes long term curvature stabilization over instantaneous progress on the objective
closest.why: Places a closed-loop stability-oriented controller directly on the lr-schedule based on loss/curvature signals, the same component and general purpose (preventing instability) but not framed as a CBF with formal invariance guarantee.

closest.title: Feedback Control for Online Training of Neural Networks
closest.evidence: we advocate switching to a performance-based adaptation... a conditional learning rate strategy that combines a feedback PD controller based on the CNN loss function... Stability proof is provided
closest.why: A feedback controller on lr driven by loss with a stability proof, overlapping in mechanism-class (closed-loop control with guarantees) but not a CBF-style forward-invariance/safety-set guarantee.

survives: The specific CBF formalism guaranteeing forward-invariance of a declared safety envelope (h_t staying above zero via the discrete CBF inequality) rather than just a stability-proved or curvature-aware feedback law is not demonstrated for the lr-schedule component in any of these papers; a genuine twist would be the explicit safety-set/barrier-certificate framing with formal never-leaves-envelope guarantees applied to lr, rather than general closed-loop stability.

closest.title: Prioritized Level Replay
closest.evidence: We show TD-errors effectively estimate a level's future learning potential and, when used to guide the sampling procedure, induce an emergent curriculum of increasingly difficult levels.
closest.why: Same core mechanism (TD/loss-based priority buffer driving non-uniform sampling to focus compute on hard, high-error instances during training) but applied to RL levels, not LM token positions keyed by multi-horizon prediction error.

closest.title: Understanding and Mitigating the Limitations of Prioritized Experience Replay
closest.evidence: we show the equivalence between the error-based prioritized sampling method for mean squared error and uniform sampling for cubic power loss... we propose our model-based stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics sampling method
closest.why: Directly analyzes error-based prioritized replay as a training-objective reweighting mechanism, the same generic mechanism proposed, but for RL value learning rather than LM multi-horizon token prediction.

closest.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
closest.evidence: at each position in the training corpus, we ask the model to predict the following n tokens using n independent output heads, operating on top of a shared model trunk
closest.why: Shares the auxiliary k-token-ahead prediction head component of the proposal but does not add any prioritized replay/curriculum over positions based on historical error.

survives: The specific combination of an EMA-tracked k-token-ahead auxiliary loss (not TD-error) as the priority signal, applied per (sequence,position) in a from-scratch single-pass LM pretraining run with importance-weighted replay mixed into fresh data, is not directly instantiated in the RL-replay papers (which prioritize by TD-error over transitions/levels, not multi-horizon LM prediction error over token positions) nor in the MTP papers (which add auxiliary heads but no replay/curriculum), so a paper combining exactly the LM-token multi-horizon-error prioritization mechanism at the training-objective/data-sampling component would still be a novel synthesis, though it is a fairly direct compositional adaptation of Prioritized Level Replay's method to a new keying signal and domain.

closest.evidence: we propose future summary prediction (FSP), which trains an auxiliary head to predict a compact representation of the long-term future, preserving information relevant for long-form generations
closest.why: Same placement (auxiliary head at hidden states predicting compressed future information) and same broad purpose (compression toward future-relevant info), but uses learned/handcrafted summary targets rather than an explicit variational IB penalty (KL/reparameterization noise) with a tunable beta compression-fidelity knob.

closest.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
closest.evidence: at each position in the training corpus, we ask the model to predict the following n tokens using n independent output heads, operating on top of a shared model trunk

closest.title: A Variational AutoEncoder for Transformers with Nonparametric Variational Information Bottleneck
closest.evidence: we formalise the embedding space of Transformer encoders as mixture probability distributions, and use Bayesian nonparametrics to derive a nonparametric variational information bottleneck (NVIB) for such attention-based embeddings
closest.why: Applies a variational IB penalty directly to transformer hidden-state embeddings during training, the same mechanism/component as the proposal, but for a general representation regularization/generative purpose rather than explicit k-step-ahead compression tradeoff.

survives: The specific combination of a variational IB penalty (with explicit beta-controlled KL/stochastic bottleneck) applied jointly with a fixed k-step-ahead auxiliary CE head to yield a probeable, controllable compression-vs-horizon dial is not demonstrated as a single mechanism in any one paper; FSP gets closest on purpose but does not use an IB-style KL/noise bottleneck, and the IB papers get closest on mechanism but not on the k-ahead auxiliary target framing.

closest.title: LACE: Loss-Adaptive Capacity Expansion for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: LACE, a simple online mechanism that expands a model's representational capacity during training by monitoring its own loss signal... When sustained loss deviation exceeds a threshold
closest.why: Uses a loss-error signal to drive an online adaptive control decision during training, but controls model capacity expansion, not replay sampling rate, and uses a threshold trigger rather than a PID loop.

closest.title: MSSR: Memory-Aware Adaptive Replay for Continual LLM Fine-Tuning
closest.evidence: existing replay-based strategies, such as fixed interleaved replay, accuracy-supervised, and loss-driven scheduling, remain limited... schedules rehearsal at adaptive intervals to mitigate catastrophic forgetting
closest.why: Closest in purpose (adaptive replay scheduling driven by a training signal instead of a fixed schedule) but uses memory-strength estimation and interval scheduling, not a PID feedback controller on loss-slope error.

closest.title: Transferability for General Reasoning: An Automated Curriculum for Multi-Domain RLVR
closest.evidence: a bandit-style online curriculum that prioritizes domains whose updates broadly benefit the rest of the training suite... per-domain advantages capture local learnability
closest.why: Adaptive closed-loop control of data-order/sampling rate based on training signals, but uses a bandit/gradient-alignment mechanism for domain mixture, not a PID controller on replay rate.

survives: A genuine PID controller (proportional+integral+derivative gains explicitly tuned and logged) driving replay-buffer sampling fraction from a loss-slope error signal is not shown in any candidate; the nearest works use threshold triggers, bandits, or heuristic loss-driven scheduling rather than an explicit closed-loop PID control law, so implementing and demonstrating the PID-specific dynamics (windup, derivative kick, gain tuning) at matched token budget would still be new.

closest.title: Analyzing Adaptive Cache Replacement Strategies
closest.evidence: Adaptive Replacement Cache (ARC) and CLOCK with Adaptive Replacement (CAR) are state-of-the-art "adaptive" cache replacement algorithms invented to improve on the shortcomings of classical cache replacement policies such as LRU, LFU and CLOCK. By separating out items that have been accessed only once and items that have been accessed more frequently...
closest.why: This is the original ARC mechanism itself, but applied to generic cache management theory, not to LM training data-order selection.

closest.title: DEAP Cache: Deep Eviction Admission and Prefetching for Cache
closest.evidence: Following previous works suggesting that frequency and recency are the two orthogonal fundamental attributes for caching, we use an online reinforcement learning technique to learn the optimal policy distribution between two orthogonal eviction strategies based on them.
closest.why: Same recency/frequency-balancing cache philosophy but for a system caching problem, not for shaping the training data order of a model being trained.

closest.title: GraB: Finding Provably Better Data Permutations than Random Reshuffling
closest.evidence: we propose an online Gradient Balancing algorithm (GraB) that enjoys the same rate as herding, while reducing the memory usage from O(nd) to just O(d)
closest.why: Closest in the actual target domain (online data-order selection during training) but uses a gradient-discrepancy mechanism, not an ARC-style recency/frequency cache-replacement controller.

survives: No paper applies ARC's specific two-list recency/frequency controller with hit/miss-driven partition parameter p to select which training examples stay in a live pool for LM pretraining data order; the closest analog (ARC itself) is a generic cache algorithm and the closest LM data-ordering work (GraB, Velocitune) uses different mechanisms (gradient balancing, velocity-based reweighting) rather than an ARC-style adaptive cache replacement policy, so the specific mechanism-to-purpose mapping remains unclaimed.

closest.title: Velocitune: A Velocity-based Dynamic Domain Reweighting Method for Continual Pre-training
closest.evidence: dynamically assesses learning velocity and adjusts data proportions accordingly, favoring slower-learning domains while shunning faster-learning ones
closest.why: same capability (loss/progress-driven online reweighting of upcoming pretraining data) at the same component (data sampler), but via a scalar velocity/scaling-law controller rather than a decaying Hebbian outer-product associative memory over feature embeddings.

closest.title: EDCO: Dynamic Curriculum Orchestration for Domain-specific Large Language Model Fine-tuning
closest.evidence: EDCO prioritizes samples with high inference entropy in a continuously adapted curriculum ... an entropy-based curriculum generator that selects data points with the highest inference entropy
closest.why: same purpose of online, model-feedback-driven re-ordering/selection of upcoming training data without touching the optimizer, differing only in the signal (entropy vs. decaying loss memory) and scoring mechanism.

closest.title: GraB: Finding Provably Better Data Permutations than Random Reshuffling
closest.evidence: an online Gradient Balancing algorithm (GraB) that enjoys the same rate as herding, while reducing the memory usage from O(nd) to just O(d)
closest.why: also maintains a small online state used to reorder upcoming minibatches in the data pipeline, though driven by gradient discrepancy rather than a Hebbian loss-associative memory.

survives: The specific mechanism of a decaying Hebbian outer-product associative memory over engineered feature/context embeddings (mapping feature patterns to recent loss, then scoring future candidates by matrix-vector readout) is a distinct implementation not described in these works, which use scalar velocity trackers, entropy estimators, or gradient-discrepancy balancing instead of an associative key-value memory; this could survive as a genuinely different mechanism for the same online curriculum capability.

closest.evidence: our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights
closest.why: nearest existing mechanism writes per-sequence information into weights at inference (fast-weight/TTT) but via gradient-based next-token compression, not via graph-message-passing over an induced token graph.

closest.title: Weight-of-Thought Reasoning: Exploring Neural Network Weights for Enhanced LLM Reasoning
closest.evidence: WoT explores the weight space through graph-based message passing, multi-step reasoning processes, and attention mechanisms
closest.why: uses graph message-passing plus weight-related reasoning, but it examines/creates reasoning nodes over weights rather than propagating token states into a low-rank ΔW patch of an FFN layer for within-sequence relational binding.

closest.title: Cross-Domain Graph Anomaly Detection via Test-Time Training with Homophily-Guided Self-Supervision
closest.evidence: a novel test-time training framework for cross-domain GAD... an attention-based mechanism that dynamically learns edge importance weights during message passing
closest.why: combines test-time training with message-passing over a graph, but for anomaly detection domain adaptation, not for producing an inference-time weight patch from within-sequence token graphs.

survives: The specific mechanism—building a per-window token-similarity graph, running message passing, and aggregating into a rank-r outer-product ΔW injected into an FFN weight matrix for the rest of the sequence—does not appear in the retrieved set; nearest works either do gradient-based weight compression (TTT) or graph message-passing for unrelated purposes (anomaly detection, weight-space reasoning), so the proposed graph-to-fast-weight-patch pathway remains open.

closest.evidence: Test-time training (TTT) adapts an LLM during generation by reading and updating request-owned state, such as fast weights, low-rank deltas, or streaming learner state... tags each decode step with its owner, version, and READ/WRITE effect, batches only compatible phases, and commits updates only to the owner.
closest.why: Introduces commit/versioning semantics for fast-weight edits during inference but for serving correctness under batching, not for validating edit quality against a held-out probe with rollback to frozen baseline.

closest.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
closest.evidence: our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights
closest.why: Performs per-sequence weight adaptation at inference (TTT) but with no probe-based validate/commit/rollback guarantee against a frozen baseline.

closest.title: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback
closest.evidence: a sandbox should only duplicate the changes between consecutive checkpoints... enabling change-based transactional C/R for AI agents
closest.why: Implements transactional checkpoint/rollback but at the level of agent sandbox filesystem/process state, not weight deltas validated against a loss probe.

survives: Yes: none of these papers implement a staged ΔW buffer that is accept/reject-gated by comparing frozen-vs-staged loss on a held-out probe window before committing into the live forward pass, which is the proposal's specific transactional guarantee against a frozen baseline; nearest work either handles multi-tenant serving correctness (RW-TTT) or unconditional TTT without any validation/rollback gate (TTT-E2E), or transactional rollback for non-weight agent state (DeltaBox).

closest.title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers
closest.evidence: learn dynamic sparse attention patterns that avoid allocating computation and memory to attend to content unrelated to the query of interest ... combines the modeling flexibility of prior work on content-based sparse attention with the efficiency gains from approaches based on local, temporal sparse attention
closest.why: Same placement (attention-topology, replacing fixed local/window patterns) and same purpose (adaptive per-query content-based key selection under a budget), but selection mechanism is online k-means clustering, not submodular greedy with a certified approximation guarantee.

closest.title: Mixture of Sparse Attention: Content-Based Learnable Sparse Attention via Expert-Choice Routing
closest.evidence: MoSA dynamically selects tokens for each attention head, allowing arbitrary sparse attention patterns... dynamic, learned content-based sparsity can lead to more efficient attention mechanisms
closest.why: Same capability claim (adaptive content-aware sparse budget per query/head trained jointly from scratch), differing only in the selection mechanism (expert-choice routing vs. submodular greedy).

closest.title: FlexPrefill: A Context-Aware Sparse Attention Mechanism for Efficient Long-Sequence Inference
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts sparse attention patterns and computational budget in real-time to meet the specific requirements of each input and attention head... replacing fixed sparse attention patterns
closest.why: Targets the same gap (fixed sliding-window/sink patterns vs. adaptive content-aware mask) at the same component, but uses divergence-based pattern switching rather than submodular maximization.

survives: The specific claim of a certified (1-1/e)-approximation guarantee via submodular greedy selection (with lazy evaluation) for per-query mask construction—rather than heuristic or learned scoring—is not demonstrated in any of these; if the approximation guarantee and its empirical validation (not just the coverage-style objective) is the load-bearing contribution, that could still be new.

closest.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable yet Noisy Rewards under Imperfect Verifiers

survives: None of the retrieved papers apply conformal prediction directly to the optimizer's gradient/step commit decision with a distribution-free guarantee on the probability of a loss-increasing update; the nearest works apply conformal calibration to forecasting intervals or reward correction, not to gating SGD/Adam steps, so a genuine implementation of per-step conformal gradient gating for optimizer commits appears novel.

closest.title: The Speed-Robustness Trade-Off for First-Order Methods with Additive Gradient Noise

closest.title: OGM-CBF: Occupancy Grid Map-based Control Barrier Function for Safe Mobile Robot Control with Memory of out of View Obstacles

closest.why: Same CBF mechanism but applied to robot motion control, not to gradient-step correction during training.

survives: Yes: no paper in the set applies a discrete-time CBF-QP projection directly to the raw gradient/parameter update in neural network training to hold a validation-probe-loss (or gradient-norm) safety margin invariant step-by-step; the closest (2503.10384) uses a relaxed barrier penalty term added to the SGD objective rather than a CBF-style nearest-feasible-update projection with a formal invariance condition h(theta_next) >= (1-alpha) h(theta).

closest.title: RLEP: Reinforcement Learning with Experience Replay for LLM Reasoning

closest.why: Replays past trajectories to steer training, but replays RL rollout trajectories for sample efficiency, not cached optimizer parameter-delta sequences keyed on loss-landscape similarity between checkpoints.

survives: Yes: no paper detects recurring gradient/optimizer trajectory signatures between checkpoint intervals and substitutes a cached specialized parameter-delta sequence (verified periodically) to skip fresh gradient computation during ongoing training; existing work either JIT-compiles checkpoint handlers for fault tolerance, merges/averages checkpoints post-hoc, or replays full RL/agent trajectories for sample efficiency rather than optimizer-step reuse keyed on trajectory-signature matching.

survives: Nothing in the set builds a recursive block-spin-style pyramid over checkpoints that explicitly separates kept coarse (persistent) modes from discarded fine-scale residuals at multiple scales specifically to let one query post-hoc which weight directions/dynamics were scale-invariant versus transient during training without rerunning it; existing work either averages/merges checkpoints for performance gains or does one-shot low-rank projection for merging, not a multi-scale trajectory-compression record for dynamics analysis.

closest.title: Mixture of Attention Heads: Selecting Attention Heads Per Token
closest.evidence: Given an input, a router dynamically selects a subset of $k$ attention heads per token. This conditional computation schema allows MoA to achieve stronger performance than the standard multi-head attention layer.
closest.why: Same component (multi-head attention) and same capability goal (token-to-head routing to enable head specialization) via a learned router, but uses top-k sparse gating rather than a Sinkhorn balanced doubly-stochastic transport plan with explicit load-balance guarantees.

closest.title: MoH: Multi-Head Attention as Mixture-of-Head Attention
closest.evidence: MoH enables each token to select the appropriate attention heads, enhancing inference efficiency without compromising accuracy... MoH replaces the standard summation in multi-head attention with a weighted summation
closest.why: Also routes/weights heads per token at the multi-head attention component to induce specialization, but via MoE-style softmax/top-k weighting, not Sinkhorn optimal transport with balanced marginals.

closest.title: Attention Sink Forges Native MoE in Attention Layers: Sink-Aware Training to Address Head Collapse
closest.evidence: we propose a sink-aware training algorithm with an auxiliary load balancing loss designed for attention layers... To mitigate head collapse
closest.why: Targets the same failure mode (head collapse) and load-balancing goal at attention heads, but via an auxiliary loss/sink mechanism rather than a Sinkhorn-iteration doubly-stochastic routing matrix.

survives: The specific mechanism of running Sinkhorn iterations to produce a doubly-stochastic token-head routing matrix with hard balanced marginals (as opposed to softmax/top-k gating or auxiliary balancing losses) at the multi-head attention component appears not directly instantiated in these papers, so a proposal emphasizing the OT-Sinkhorn balanced-transport mechanism specifically (not just token-to-head routing) could still be a genuine mechanistic novelty if none of these actually use Sinkhorn normalization for heads.

closest.title: KVCOMM: Online Cross-context KV-cache Communication for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
closest.evidence: KVCOMM achieves over 70% reuse rate across diverse multi-agent workloads... by reusing KV-caches and aligning cache offsets of overlapping contexts under diverse prefix contexts
closest.why: Same goal of sharing KV cache across concurrent agents/requests to amortize computation on overlapping content, though via offset-alignment/anchor retrieval rather than a live ANN top-k blend with a learned gate.

closest.title: Unified AI Gateway: A Framework for Joint Model Routing and KV Cache Management
closest.evidence: We synthesize existing evidence on KV cache reuse, compression, cross-model mapping, distributed storage, and transfer

closest.title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference
closest.evidence: with prefix-sharing workloads, smaller, prefix-homogeneous batches -- where all requests share a common prefix -- can achieve higher decode throughput
closest.why: Addresses cross-request cache sharing within a serving batch, but via exact prefix matching/scheduling rather than approximate kNN retrieval blended via a learned gate.

survives: The specific mechanism of a continuously rebuilt ANN index over pooled batch K/V with top-k retrieval and a learned gate blending non-contiguous, non-prefix nearest-neighbor entries (not exact prefix/offset-aligned matches) into attention at decode time is not demonstrated in these prefix-sharing or offset-alignment systems, so a proposal built specifically around approximate kNN fuzzy matching (rather than exact/aligned prefix reuse) could still be novel.

closest.title: Joint Encoding of KV-Cache Blocks for Scalable LLM Serving
closest.evidence: We propose joint encoding of KV-cache blocks, which fuses similar blocks across requests and input chunks into shared representations while preserving standard cache structure.
closest.why: This is exactly the proposal's mechanism: clustering near-duplicate KV segments across independent requests into a shared compressed dictionary, used at inference time to avoid recomputation.

closest.title: Prefix Sharing Is a Sorting Problem
closest.evidence: LLM serving reuses KV cache by exact prefix match, so when a prompt is assembled from a set of reusable pieces... the order chosen for those pieces determines how much computation can be shared.
closest.why: Addresses cross-request reuse of KV/prefix structure but via reordering/hierarchy rather than offline clustering/dictionary fitting, making it adjacent rather than identical to the joint-encoding paper.

closest.title: BatchLLM: Optimizing Large Batched LLM Inference with Global Prefix Sharing and Throughput-oriented Token Batching
closest.evidence: BatchLLM explicitly identifies the common prefixes globally. The requests sharing the same prefix will be scheduled together to reuse the KV context the best.
closest.why: Also amortizes compute across non-overlapping requests via shared KV reuse, though restricted to exact prefix matches rather than a learned/clustered dictionary of near-duplicate segments.

survives: The only room left is if the 'sleep-replay-consolidation' framing does continuous background clustering/autoencoder-based dictionary learning with fuzzy (non-exact) matching that generalizes beyond block-level exact fusion, but 2601.03067 already does cross-request fusion of similar (not just identical) KV blocks into shared representations at serving time, closing most of that gap.

closest.title: CTkvr: KV Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs via Centroid then Token Indexing
closest.evidence: employs a two-stage retrieval strategy: lightweight centroids are precomputed during prefilling for centroid-grained indexing, followed by token-level refinement for precise KV retrieval
closest.why: closest overlap in using an approximate, learned/precomputed indexing structure to retrieve KV cache segments rather than exact match, but it indexes within a single long context for token-level attention sparsity, not cross-request prefix reuse across the serving batch.

closest.title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference
closest.evidence: we show that shared prefix detection in existing schedulers relies on radix-tree traversals, incurring substantial CPU overhead
closest.why: identifies the same exact-match prefix lookup bottleneck the proposal targets, but replaces it with an RL scheduler and a hash-tree structure (CHT), not a learned embedding-based approximate index.

closest.title: Randomization Boosts KV Caching, Learning Balances Query Load: A Joint Perspective
closest.evidence: integrate provably competitive randomized KV cache eviction with learning-based methods to adaptively route queries with evolving patterns
closest.why: uses learning for cache-related decisions (query routing) in serving, but applies learning to load balancing/eviction policy, not to predicting the cache slot position of a matching segment via embedding similarity.

survives: A trained embedding-to-slot-index model that replaces exact hash/radix-tree prefix matching with an approximate learned lookup, retrained periodically on logged (embedding, slot) pairs, is not directly instantiated by any candidate; the nearest works either do approximate indexing within a single context (CTkvr) or improve scheduling/eviction with learning but keep exact prefix matching for cache retrieval.
